alternate_renderings: You take too much upon yourselves.
rationale: Greek uses a let-it-be-enough idiom here. Current wording keeps that direct rebuke.

greek_phrase: ηλαλαξεν πας ο λαος αμα αλαλαγμω μεγαλω και ισχυρω και επεσεν απαν το τειχος κυκλω
chosen_rendering: And the priests sounded with the trumpets, and when the people heard the voice of the trumpets, all the people shouted together with a great and strong shout, and the whole wall fell around, and all the people went up into the city.
alternate_renderings: The people shouted with a great shout and the wall fell down flat.
rationale: Greek says the people shouted together and the whole wall fell around. Current wording preserves that shape.

greek_phrase: οτι δια κυριου εγενετο κατισχυσαι αυτων την καρδιαν
chosen_rendering: Because from the Lord it came to strengthen their heart to meet in war against Israel, so that they might be utterly destroyed, so that no mercy might be given to them, but so that they might be utterly destroyed in the way the Lord said to Moses.
alternate_renderings: It was of the Lord to harden their hearts.
rationale: Greek says from the Lord it came to strengthen their heart. Current wording keeps that formulation.

greek_phrase: παν αναθεμα αγιον αγιων εσται τω κυριω
chosen_rendering: But every devoted thing that a person devotes to the Lord, from all that belongs to him, from human to beast and from the field of his possession, shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed. Every devoted thing is holy of holies to the Lord.
alternate_renderings: Every devoted thing is most holy to the Lord.
rationale: Greek uses the holy-of-holies formula here. Current wording keeps that cultic phrase plain.

greek_phrase: εκκλησιασας τον λαον τους ανδρας και τας γυναικας και τα εκγονα και τον προσηλυτον τον εν ταις πολεσιν υμων
chosen_rendering: Assemble the people, the men and the women and the children and the proselyte in your cities, so that they may hear and so that they may learn to fear the Lord your God, and they will listen so as to do all the words of this law.
alternate_renderings: Assemble the people, men women children and the stranger within your gates.
rationale: Greek says children and the proselyte in your cities. Current wording keeps that list and setting visible.

greek_phrase: τυπτει αυτον αβεννηρ εν τω οπισω του δορατος επι την ψοαν και πιπτει εκει και αποθνησκει υποκατω αυτου
chosen_rendering: And he was not willing to stand away, and Abennēr struck him with the back of the spear in the belly, and the spear came out from behind him, and he fell there and died under him. And it came to be, everyone coming to the place where Asaēl fell there and died, would stand still.
alternate_renderings: Abner struck him under the fifth rib and he died in the same place.
rationale: Greek says in the belly and died under him. Current wording keeps those harder details instead of harmonizing to the familiar phrasing.

greek_phrase: ουτος περιηργυρωσεν τους στυλους και εχωνευσεν τω στυλω δακτυλιους χρυσους και εχρυσωσεν τους μοχλους χρυσιω
chosen_rendering: He silver-covered the posts and cast gold rings for each post and overlaid the bars with gold. He overlaid the posts of the curtain with gold and made gold hooks.
alternate_renderings: And the hanging for the gate of the court was needlework of blue and purple and scarlet.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the post-and-ring furnishing line rather than the MT hanging-description line. Current wording keeps the Greek verse mapping.

greek_phrase: και το ενεδρον εκαθητο εν τω ταμιειω και διεσπασεν αυτα απο των βραχιονων αυτου ως ραμμα
chosen_rendering: And Dalila took new cords for him and bound him with them and said to him, The foreigners are upon you, Sampsōn. And the ambush was sitting in the inner room. And he tore them from his arms like thread.
alternate_renderings: The liers in wait came out of the chamber, and he broke them like a thread.
rationale: Greek says the ambush was sitting in the inner room and he tore them like thread. Current wording preserves that shape.

greek_phrase: εναρχου κληρονομειν συναπτε προς αυτον πολεμον
chosen_rendering: Now then rise and set out and pass through the Ravine of Arnon. Behold, I have handed into your hands Sihon king of Heshbon the Amorite and his land. Begin to inherit; join battle with him.
alternate_renderings: Begin to possess it and contend with him in battle.
rationale: Greek gives the paired imperatives begin to inherit and join battle with him. Current wording keeps both plain.

greek_phrase: επτα εθνη πολλα και ισχυροτερα υμων
chosen_rendering: And if the Lord your God brings you into the land into which you are entering there to inherit it, and he removes great nations from before your face, the Hittite and Gergesite and Amorite and Canaanite and Pherezite and Hivite and Jebusite, seven nations many and stronger than you,
alternate_renderings: Seven nations greater and mightier than you.
rationale: Greek says many and stronger than you. Current wording keeps that direct pair.

greek_phrase: εδωκας αυτοις σωτηρας και εσωσας αυτους εκ χειρος θλιβοντων αυτους
chosen_rendering: And you gave them into the hand of those afflicting them, and they afflicted them, and they cried out to you in the time of their affliction, and you from heaven heard, and in your great compassions gave them saviors, and they saved them from the hand of those afflicting them.
alternate_renderings: You gave them saviors who saved them from the hand of their enemies.
rationale: Greek keeps the afflicters language before and after the rescue. Current wording preserves it.

greek_phrase: τουτω σχοινισμα ερεγαβα η εν τη βασαν εξηκοντα πολεις μεγαλαι τειχηρεις και μοχλοι χαλκοι εις
chosen_rendering: Son of Gaber in Ramath Galaad. To this one belonged the line-measure of Eregaba that is in Basan, sixty great walled cities and bronze bars.
alternate_renderings: To him pertained the towns of Jair and the region of Argob in Bashan.
rationale: Greek maps this verse differently and keeps a line-measure phrase with Eregaba. Current wording leaves that Greek form visible.

greek_phrase: σπασαι την ρομφαιαν σου και αποκεντησον με εν αυτη
chosen_rendering: And Saoul said to the one carrying his equipment, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised ones come and pierce me and mock me. But the one carrying his equipment was not willing, because he feared greatly. And Saoul took the sword and fell upon it.
alternate_renderings: Draw your sword and thrust me through with it.
rationale: Greek says pierce me with it and repeats that verb in Saul's fear. Current wording keeps the repetition.

greek_phrase: εκκρουσθη η χειρ αυτου τη αξινη κοπτοντος το ξυλον και εκπεσον το σιδηριον απο του ξυλου τυχη του πλησιον
chosen_rendering: and whoever enters with his neighbor into the forest to gather wood, and his hand swings with the axe while cutting the wood, and the iron flies from the wood and meets his neighbor and he dies, this one shall flee to one of these cities and live,
alternate_renderings: The axe head slips from the handle and lights upon his neighbor.
rationale: Greek says his hand swings and the iron flies from the wood and meets his neighbor. Current wording keeps that motion.

greek_phrase: και αυτοι λημψονται τα αμαρτηματα αυτων νομιμον αιωνιον εις τας γενεας αυτων
chosen_rendering: And the Levite himself shall minister the ministry of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins, an everlasting statute throughout their generations. And in the midst of the sons of Israel they shall not inherit an inheritance.
alternate_renderings: They shall bear their iniquity; it shall be a statute forever.
rationale: Greek says they shall receive or bear their sins. Current wording keeps that direct burden clause.

greek_phrase: κατα τα επιτηδευματα γης αιγυπτου εν η κατωκησατε επ' αυτη ου ποιησετε και κατα τα επιτηδευματα γης χανααν εις ην εγω εισαγω υμας εκει ου ποιησετε
chosen_rendering: According to the practices of the land of Egypt, in which you dwelt, you shall not do, and according to the practices of the land of Canaan, into which I am bringing you, there you shall not do, and in their ordinances you shall not walk.
alternate_renderings: You shall not do according to the doings or devices of Egypt and Canaan.
rationale: Greek uses practices here and repeats there you shall not do. Current wording keeps that repetition.

greek_phrase: η ημερα αυτη ημερα ευαγγελιας εστιν και ημεις σιωπωμεν και μενομεν εως φωτος του πρωι και ευρησομεν ανομιαν
chosen_rendering: And one man said to his neighbor, We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until the morning light, lawlessness will find us. And now come, let us go in and report to the house of the king.
alternate_renderings: This day is a day of good tidings, and if we delay till morning some mischief will come upon us.
rationale: Greek says good news and lawlessness will find us. Current wording keeps those terms visible.

greek_phrase: και νυν τον σιτον και την κριθην και το ελαιον και τον οινον α ειπεν ο κυριος μου αποστειλατω τοις παισιν αυτου
chosen_rendering: And now let my lord send to his servants grain and barley and oil and wine which my lord spoke of.
alternate_renderings: The son of a woman of the daughters of Dan ... skillful to work in gold and silver and bronze.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the supply request line, not the MT craftsman description line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και ελθη το σημειον η το τερας ο ελαλησεν προς σε λεγων πορευθωμεν και λατρευσωμεν θεοις ετεροις ους ουκ οιδατε
chosen_rendering: and the sign or wonder comes that he spoke to you, saying, Let us go and serve other gods whom you do not know,
alternate_renderings: You shall not listen to that prophet, for the Lord is testing you.
rationale: Greek verse division here preserves only the sign-and-invitation clause. The testing command belongs to the next verse.

chosen_rendering: Mallouch, Heram, Baana.
alternate_renderings: And the rest of the people, the priests, the Levites...
rationale: This LXX verse number here is a short name list, not the longer MT assembly line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: εγω δε και η οικια μου λατρευσομεν κυριω οτι αγιος εστιν
chosen_rendering: But if it does not please you to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve, whether the gods of your fathers beyond the river or the gods of the Amorites among whom you dwell on their land. But I and my house will serve the Lord, because he is holy.
alternate_renderings: But I and my house will serve the Lord.
rationale: Greek explicitly adds because he is holy at the end. Current wording keeps that clause.

greek_phrase: και επιστρεψουσιν καρδιας αυτων εν τη γη ου μετηχθησαν εκει και επιστρεψωσιν και δεηθωσιν σου εν γη μετοικιας αυτων
chosen_rendering: and they will turn their hearts back in the land where they were carried there and turn and entreat you in the land of their migration, saying, We sinned, we acted lawlessly, we did wrong,
alternate_renderings: They shall bethink themselves and repent and make supplication in the land of captivity.
rationale: Greek says they will turn their hearts back and then turn and entreat. Current wording keeps that sequence visible.

greek_phrase: και απεστειλεν αχαζ αγγελους προς θαγλαθφελλασαρ βασιλεα ασσυριων λεγων δουλος σου και υιος σου εγω
chosen_rendering: And Achaz sent messengers to Tiglathpileser king of the Assyrians, saying, I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hand of the king of Syria and from the hand of the king of Israel, those rising against me.
alternate_renderings: Ahaz sent to Tiglath-pileser saying I am your servant and your son.
rationale: Greek keeps the messenger sending explicit and ends with those rising against me. Current wording preserves that line.

greek_phrase: και τω πενητι ουδεν αλλ' η αμνας μια μικρα ην εκτησατο και περιεποιησατο και εξεθρεψεν αυτην
chosen_rendering: And to the poor man there was nothing except one little ewe lamb, which he acquired and kept alive and nourished, and it grew up with him and with his sons together. From his bread it would eat and from his cup it would drink and in his bosom it would sleep, and it was to him as a daughter.
alternate_renderings: The poor man had only one little ewe lamb which he had bought and nourished.
rationale: Greek adds kept alive and nourished before the domestic details. Current wording keeps the fuller tenderness line.

greek_phrase: και οισει το δωρον αυτου περι ου ημαρτεν το δεκατον του οιφι σεμιδαλιν περι αμαρτιας ουκ επιχεει επ' αυτο ελαιον ουδε επιθησει επ' αυτο λιβανον
chosen_rendering: And if his hand cannot find a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he shall bring as his gift for the sin that he sinned a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for sin. He shall not pour oil on it, nor place frankincense on it, because it is a sin-offering.
alternate_renderings: He shall bring the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering; he shall put no oil on it nor frankincense.
rationale: Greek says bring as his gift for the sin that he sinned and then forbids pouring oil or placing frankincense. Current wording keeps that form.

greek_phrase: οι αδελφοι υμων και τα τεκνα υμων εσονται εν οικτιρμοις εναντι παντων των αιχμαλωτισαντων αυτους και αποστρεψει εις την γην ταυτην
chosen_rendering: Because when you return to the Lord, your brothers and your children shall be in mercies before all who took them captive and he will return to this land, because the Lord our God is merciful and compassionate and will not turn away his face from us if we return to him.
alternate_renderings: Your brothers and your children shall find compassion before their captors and he will restore you to this land.
rationale: Greek says they shall be in mercies before all who took them captive. Current wording keeps that unusual expression visible.

greek_phrase: συνετριψαν τας στηλας και εξεκοψαν τα αλση και κατεσπασαν τα υψηλα και τους βωμους
chosen_rendering: And when all these things were finished, all Israel found in the cities of Iouda went out and broke pillars and cut down groves and pulled down high places and altars from all Iouda and Beniamin and from Ephraim and from Manasse until end, and all Israel returned each to his inheritance and to their cities.
alternate_renderings: They broke the images and cut down the groves and threw down the high places and altars.
rationale: Greek says pillars, groves, high places, and altars, and ends with until end. Current wording keeps that sequence visible.

greek_phrase: και εκτεινασα την χειρα επιλαβηται των διδυμων αυτου
chosen_rendering: And if men fight together, a man with his brother, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of the one striking him, and, stretching out her hand, seizes his testicles,
alternate_renderings: She takes hold of his secrets or private parts.
rationale: Greek literally says his twins here. Current wording keeps the concrete bodily term.

greek_phrase: δοτε δοξαν κυριω τω θεω και εισελθατε εις το αγιασμα αυτου
chosen_rendering: And now do not harden your necks; give glory to the Lord God, and enter into his sanctuary which he sanctified forever, and serve the Lord your God, and he will turn away fury of wrath from you.
alternate_renderings: Yield yourselves to the Lord and enter his sanctuary.
rationale: Greek says give glory to the Lord God. Current wording preserves that imperative.

greek_phrase: και αυτη η συνταξις της σκηνης του μαρτυριου καθα συνεταγη μωυση
chosen_rendering: And this was the ordering of the tent of testimony, as it was arranged by Moses for the service of the Levites through Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
alternate_renderings: Three bowls made like almonds in one branch...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the tabernacle-ordering line rather than the MT lampstand-bowls line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: παντα οσα συ ορας εμα εστι και των θυγατερων μου
chosen_rendering: But Laban answered and said to Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, and the sons my sons, and the livestock my livestock, and all that you see is mine and my daughters'. What shall I do to these today or to their children whom they bore?
alternate_renderings: All that you see is mine; what can I do to these my daughters today?
rationale: Greek adds and my daughters' after all that you see is mine. Current wording keeps that possessive extension.

greek_phrase: οτι τουτο η ζωη σου και η μακροτης των ημερων σου
chosen_rendering: loving the Lord your God, obeying his voice, and holding fast to him, because this is your life and the length of your days, for you to dwell on the land that the Lord swore to your fathers, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, to give to them.
alternate_renderings: For he is your life and the length of your days.
rationale: Greek says this is your life, not he is your life. Current wording keeps that reading.

greek_phrase: και εγενετο εν τω συντελεσαι σαλωμων του οικοδομησαι τον οικον κυριου και τον οικον εαυτου μετα εικοσι ετη τοτε εξεκκλησιασεν ο βασιλευς σαλωμων παντας τους πρεσβυτερους ισραηλ εν σιων
chosen_rendering: And it came to be when Solomon finished building the house of the Lord and his own house, after twenty years, then King Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel in Sion, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the City of David, this is Sion.
alternate_renderings: Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel in Jerusalem to bring up the ark.
rationale: This LXX verse number includes the twenty-year completion notice and places the assembly in Sion. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και εθαψαν αυτον εις το σπηλαιον το διπλουν ο εκτησατο αβρααμ το σπηλαιον εν κτησει μνημειου
chosen_rendering: And his sons carried him up into the land of Canaan and buried him in the double cave, which Abraham acquired as a possession for a tomb from Ephrom the Hittite, before Mambre.
alternate_renderings: They buried him in the cave of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field for a burial possession.
rationale: Greek says the double cave and possession for a tomb. Current wording keeps that diction.

greek_phrase: προς ολδαν την προφητιν γυναικα σελλημ υιου θεκουε υιου αραας του ιματιοφυλακος και αυτη κατωκει εν ιερουσαλημ εν τη μασενα
chosen_rendering: And Chelkias the priest and Achikam and Achobōr and Saphphan and Asaiah went to Oldan the prophetess, wife of Sellēm son of Thekoue son of Araas keeper of the wardrobe, and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the Maseña, and they spoke to her.
alternate_renderings: They went to Huldah the prophetess, wife of Shallum son of Tikvah son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe, and she dwelt in Jerusalem in the college.
rationale: Greek identifies her with different household names and Maseña. Current wording keeps the Greek line visible.

greek_phrase: καθως εκωλυσεν σε κυριος του μη ελθειν εις αιμα αθωον και σωζειν την χειρα σου σοι
lemma: κωλυω | αιμα αθωον | σωζω την χειρα
chosen_rendering: And now, my lord, as the Lord lives and as your life lives, just as the Lord kept you back from coming into innocent blood and from saving your hand for yourself, now let your enemies and the ones seeking evil for my lord become like Nabal.
alternate_renderings: The Lord has kept you from coming to shed blood and from avenging yourself with your own hand.
rationale: Greek says innocent blood and saving your hand for yourself. Current wording keeps that harder phrasing.

greek_phrase: θυμιωσιν τω κυριω ολοκαυτωματα πρωι και δειλης και θυμιαμα συνθεσεως και προθεσεις αρτων επι της τραπεζης της καθαρας
chosen_rendering: They burn to the Lord whole burnt offerings morning and evening and incense of compounded spices and presentations of bread upon pure table, and golden lampstand and its lamps for burning to light at evening, because we keep charges of the Lord God of our fathers, but you forsake him.
alternate_renderings: They burn whole burnt offerings morning and evening and sweet incense and set the showbread on the pure table.
rationale: Greek keeps a longer compounded worship list here. Current wording preserves it.

greek_phrase: και γε αυτον και επαταξεν αυτον εν τω αρματι εν τω αναβαινειν γαι η εστιν ιεβλααμ
chosen_rendering: And Ochozias king of Judah saw and fled by way of Baithaggan, and Iou pursued after him and said, Strike him too. And they struck him in the chariot at the ascent of Gai, which is Ieblaam, and he fled to Megiddo and died there.
alternate_renderings: Strike him also in the chariot at the ascent of Gur by Ibleam.
rationale: Greek gives Gai and Ieblaam here. Current wording keeps the Greek place forms visible.

greek_phrase: και εκδυσεται την στολην αυτου και ενδυσεται στολην αλλην και εξοισει την κατακαρπωσιν εξω της παρεμβολης εις τοπον καθαρον
chosen_rendering: And he shall take off his garment and put on another garment, and he shall carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.
alternate_renderings: Because he has sinned and is guilty, he shall restore what he took by robbery or deceit.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the ash-removal line, not the MT restitution line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: την μιαν περι αμαρτιας και την μιαν εις ολοκαυτωμα συν τη θυσια και εξιλασεται ο ιερευς περι του καθαριζομενου εναντι κυριου
chosen_rendering: the one for sin and the one for whole burnt offering with the sacrifice, and the priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the one being cleansed.
alternate_renderings: The one for a sin offering and the other for a burnt offering with the grain offering.
rationale: Greek says with the sacrifice and ends with atonement before the Lord for the one being cleansed. Current wording keeps that close.

greek_phrase: και διαστελεισθε αυτοις και ουχ αμαρτησονται τω κυριω
chosen_rendering: Every case that comes upon you from your brothers dwelling in their cities, between blood and blood and between ordinance and commandment and statutes and judgments, you shall make distinction for them, and they shall not sin against the Lord, and wrath shall not be on you and on your brothers. Thus you shall do and you shall not sin.
alternate_renderings: You shall warn them, so they do not trespass against the Lord.
rationale: Greek says you shall make distinction for them. Current wording keeps that judicial wording.

greek_phrase: και επιφημισηται εν τη καρδια αυτου λεγων οσια μοι γενοιτο οτι εν τη αποπλανησει της καρδιας μου πορευσομαι ινα μη συναπολεση ο αμαρτωλος τον αναμαρτητον
chosen_rendering: and it shall be, if he hears the words of this curse and congratulates himself in his heart, saying, Holy things shall be mine, because in the wandering of my heart I will walk, so that the sinner may not destroy the sinless,
alternate_renderings: He blesses himself in his heart, saying I shall have peace though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart.
rationale: Greek here is markedly different and difficult. Current wording keeps the transmitted Greek strangeness visible instead of harmonizing to the familiar MT line.

greek_phrase: ουχ ουτος ο λογος οτι ανηρ εξ ορους εφραιμ σαβεε υιος βοχορι ονομα αυτου και επηρεν την χειρα αυτου επι τον βασιλεα δαυιδ
chosen_rendering: This is not the matter, but a man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bochori is his name, and he lifted his hand against King David. Give him to me alone, and I will depart from the city. And the woman said to Ioab, Behold, his head will be thrown to you through the wall.
alternate_renderings: The matter is not so; a man of mount Ephraim named Sheba son of Bichri has lifted his hand against King David.
rationale: Greek says this is not the matter and keeps the Sabee Bochori forms. Current wording preserves that line.

greek_phrase: τοις υιοις ιωσηφ υιοις εφραιμ κατα συγγενειας αυτων κατα δημους αυτων κατ' οικους πατριων αυτων κατα αριθμον ονοματων αυτων κατα κεφαλην αυτων παντα αρσενικα απο εικοσαετους και επανω πας ο εκπορευομενος εν τη δυναμει
chosen_rendering: As for the sons of Joseph, the sons of Ephraim, by their families, by their clans, by the houses of their fathers, by the number of their names, by their headcount, every male from twenty years old and upward, every one going out in force,
alternate_renderings: Of the children of Zebulun by their generations, after their families...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Ephraim census heading rather than the MT Zebulun line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: διαρρησσων διαρρηξω την βασιλειαν σου εκ χειρος σου και δωσω αυτην τω δουλω σου
chosen_rendering: And the Lord said to Solomon, Because these things came to be with you and you did not keep my commandments and my ordinances that I commanded you, in tearing I will tear your kingdom out of your hand and give it to your servant.
alternate_renderings: I will surely rend your kingdom from you and give it to your servant.
rationale: Greek doubles the tearing verb here. Current wording keeps that emphatic pattern visible.

greek_phrase: ζησεσθε και πολλοι εσεσθε και ευλογησει σε κυριος ο θεος σου
chosen_rendering: If you obey the commands of the Lord your God that I command you today, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his ordinances and his judgments, then you shall live and be many, and the Lord your God will bless you in all the land into which you are entering there to inherit it.
alternate_renderings: You shall live and multiply, and the Lord your God will bless you in the land.
rationale: Greek says live and be many rather than live and multiply. Current wording keeps that line.

greek_phrase: ουκ εκτοκιεις τω αδελφω σου τοκον αργυριου και τοκον βρωματων και τοκον παντος πραγματος ου αν εκδανεισης
chosen_rendering: You shall not lend at interest to your brother, interest of silver and interest of food and interest of anything that you lend.
alternate_renderings: To a foreigner you may lend at interest, but to your brother you shall not lend at interest.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the no-interest-to-brother line rather than the MT foreigner line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και εδωκαν οι υιοι ισραηλ τοις λευιταις τας πολεις και τα περισπορια αυτων
chosen_rendering: And the sons of Israel gave to the Levites the cities and their surrounding lands.
alternate_renderings: Aaron and his sons offered on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Levite-city grant line rather than the MT Aaronic service line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: ο ανηρ αυτης στησει αυτη και ο ανηρ αυτης περιελει
chosen_rendering: Every vow and every binding oath to afflict a life, her husband shall establish it for her, and her husband shall remove it.
alternate_renderings: Her husband shall confirm it, or her husband shall cancel it.
rationale: Greek uses the establish-remove pair here. Current wording keeps that direct legal phrasing.

greek_phrase: ανατελει αστρον εξ ιακωβ και αναστησεται ανθρωπος εξ ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: I will point him out, but not now. I count him blessed, and he is not near. A star shall rise out of Jacob, and a man shall stand up out of Israel, and he shall crush the leaders of Moab and plunder all the sons of Seth.
alternate_renderings: A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel.
rationale: Greek says a man shall stand up out of Israel rather than a scepter shall rise. Current wording keeps the Greek figure.

greek_phrase: και αποστειλον μοι ξυλα κεδρινα και αρκευθινα και πευκινα εκ του λιβανου
chosen_rendering: And send me cedar woods and juniper woods and pine woods from Lebanon, because I know your servants know how to cut woods from Lebanon, and behold, your servants are with my servants,
alternate_renderings: Send me now a man skillful to work in gold and silver and bronze and iron...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the timber request line rather than the MT artisan request line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και ιησους και βαναιας και σαραβια ησαν συνετιζοντες τον λαον εις τον νομον και ο λαος εν τη στασει αυτου
chosen_rendering: And Iesous and Banaias and Sarabia were causing the people to understand the law, and the people stood in their place.
alternate_renderings: Jeshua and Bani and Sherebiah and many others caused the people to understand the law.
rationale: Greek here gives a shorter personnel list and ends with the people standing in their place. Current wording keeps that form.

greek_phrase: εν ταις ορασεσιν ιωηλ του ορωντος περι ιεροβοαμ υιου ναβατ
chosen_rendering: And the rest of matters of Salomon, first and last, behold, written in the words of Nathan prophet and in the words of Achia the Sēlōnite and in visions of Iōēl the seer concerning Ieroboam son of Nabat.
alternate_renderings: In the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.
rationale: Greek names Iōēl here rather than the familiar MT Iddo. Current wording keeps the Greek source list.

greek_phrase: ουχ ουτως η κλινη εφ' ης ανεβης εκει ου καταβηση απ' αυτης οτι θανατω αποθανη
chosen_rendering: And Elijah spoke to him and said, Thus says the Lord: Why is it that you sent messengers to seek in Baal of flies, god of Akkarōn? And not so, the bed on which you went up there, you shall not come down from it, because by death you will die.
alternate_renderings: Is it not because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his word? therefore you shall not come down from that bed.
rationale: Greek turns from the question into the abrupt line And not so. Current wording keeps that turn visible.

greek_phrase: και ουκ εξεθλιψαν οι υιοι δαν τον αμορραιον τον θλιβοντα αυτους εν τω ορει
chosen_rendering: This is the inheritance of the tribe of the sons of Dan according to their clans, their cities and their villages. And the sons of Dan did not drive out the Amorite who hemmed them in on the mountain, and the Amorites did not allow them to go down into the valley, and they pressed the boundary of their portion away from them.
alternate_renderings: The border of the children of Dan went out too little for them; therefore the children of Dan went up against Leshem.
rationale: Greek appends the Dan-Amorite pressure notice here rather than the MT Leshem notice. Current wording keeps the Greek addition.

greek_phrase: και της φωνης αυτου ακουσεσθε και αυτω προστεθησεσθε
chosen_rendering: After the Lord your God you shall walk, and him you shall fear, and his commands you shall keep, and his voice you shall hear, and to him you shall be joined.
alternate_renderings: You shall serve him and cling to him.
rationale: Greek ends with to him you shall be joined. Current wording keeps that form rather than smoothing to cling.

greek_phrase: ανθ' ων υψωσα σε απο της γης και εδωκα σε ηγουμενον επι τον λαον μου ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: Because I lifted you up from the earth and gave you as a leader over my people Israel, and you walked in the way of Ieroboam and made my people Israel sin, to provoke me by their vanities,
alternate_renderings: Because I exalted you out of the dust and made you prince over my people Israel.
rationale: Greek says from the earth here and ends with vanities. Current wording keeps those details.

greek_phrase: ος αν δω του σπερματος αυτου αρχοντι θανατω θανατουσθω
chosen_rendering: And to the sons of Israel you shall say: If any of the sons of Israel or of the newcomer newcomers in Israel gives of his seed to a ruler, he shall surely be put to death. The people of the land shall stone him with stones.
alternate_renderings: Whoever gives any of his seed to Molech shall surely be put to death.
rationale: Greek says to a ruler here rather than naming Molech. Current wording keeps the transmitted Greek wording.

greek_phrase: εκαλεσαν νηστειαν και εκαθισαν τον ναβουθαι εν αρχη του λαου
chosen_rendering: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people.
alternate_renderings: It happened when Ben-hadad heard this message while drinking that he said, Set yourselves in array.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the Naboth fast line rather than the MT Ben-hadad war line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: εν τοπω ου εαν ακουσητε την φωνην της κερατινης εκει συναχθησεσθε προς ημας και ο θεος ημων πολεμησει περι ημων
chosen_rendering: In place where you hear the sound of the horn, there you shall gather to us, and our God will fight for us.
alternate_renderings: Do not be afraid of them; remember the great and terrible Lord and fight for your brothers.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the horn-gathering line rather than the MT fear-not exhortation. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: ουτος εποιησεν τω θυσιαστηριω παραθεμα εργον δικτυωτον κατωθεν του πυρειου υπο αυτο εως του ημισους αυτου
chosen_rendering: He made for the altar a surrounding frame of net-work beneath its fire-pan underneath it as far as its middle, and he fixed to it four bronze rings on the four sides of the frame of the altar, wide enough for the bars, so that the altar might be carried by them.
alternate_renderings: All the gold used for the work in all the work of the sanctuary was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels.
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the altar-network construction line rather than the MT gold totals line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: εαν δε ολιγοστοι ωσιν οι εν τη οικια ωστε μη ικανους ειναι εις προβατον
chosen_rendering: But if those in the house are too few for an animal from the flock, he shall take along his neighbor nearest to him according to the number of persons. Each according to what is enough for him shall be counted toward the animal from the flock.
alternate_renderings: If the household is too little for the lamb, let him and his neighbor next to his house take it.
rationale: Greek says animal from the flock here rather than lamb alone. Current wording keeps that broader term.

greek_phrase: δανιεις εθνεσιν πολλοις συ δε ου δανιη και αρξεις συ εθνων πολλων σου δε ουκ αρξουσιν
chosen_rendering: May the Lord open for you his good treasury, the heaven, to give rain to your land in its season and bless all the works of your hands. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow, and you shall rule many nations, but they shall not rule you.
alternate_renderings: You shall lend to many nations and you shall not borrow.
rationale: Greek adds the rule-many-nations line here. Current wording keeps the fuller blessing promise.

greek_phrase: πλην εν τω καιρω του γηρως αυτου επονεσεν τους ποδας αυτου
chosen_rendering: And the rest of the matters of Asa and all his dominion that he exercised, behold, are these not written in the Book of the Matters of the Days of the kings of Iouda? Yet in the time of his old age his feet were in pain.
alternate_renderings: In the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet.
rationale: Greek says his feet were in pain here. Current wording keeps that simpler expression.

greek_phrase: και αφανιεις τον πονηρον εξ υμων αυτων
chosen_rendering: And that prophet or that dreamer of the dream shall die, because he spoke to lead you astray from the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of Egypt, who redeemed you from slavery, to drive you out of the way that the Lord your God commanded you to walk in it. And you shall destroy the evil one from among you.
alternate_renderings: So you shall put the evil away from your midst.
rationale: Greek says destroy the evil one from among you. Current wording keeps the singular personified form.

greek_phrase: λεπρα εμμονος εστιν η αφη ακαθαρτος εστιν
chosen_rendering: And the priest shall inspect the mark on the seventh day. If the mark has spread in the garment or in the warp or in the woof or in the leather, in whatever is made of leather for use, the mark is persistent skin-disease. It is unclean.
alternate_renderings: It is a fretting leprosy; it is unclean.
rationale: Greek says persistent skin-disease here. Current wording keeps that direct expression.

greek_phrase: εν τη εορτη η επλασατο απο καρδιας αυτου
chosen_rendering: And he went up upon the altar that he made on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, in the feast that he devised from his own heart, and he made a feast for the sons of Israel and went up upon the altar to offer incense.
alternate_renderings: In the feast which he had devised of his own heart.
rationale: Greek says devised from his own heart. Current wording keeps that sharper line.

greek_phrase: και συνεφωνησαν οι ιερεις του μη λαβειν αργυριον παρα του λαου και του μη ενισχυσαι το βεδεκ του οικου
chosen_rendering: And the priests agreed not to take silver from the people and not to repair the breach of the house.
alternate_renderings: Jehoash said to the priests, All the money of the dedicated things brought into the house of the Lord...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the priestly agreement line rather than the MT collection order. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: μη ελθωσιν οι απεριτμητοι ουτοι και εμπαιξωσιν μοι
chosen_rendering: And Saul said to one carrying his weapons, Draw your sword and pierce me with it, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me. But one carrying his weapons would not, because he feared greatly. And Saul took sword and fell upon it.
alternate_renderings: Lest these uncircumcised come and abuse me.
rationale: Greek says mock me here. Current wording keeps that verb.

greek_phrase: τους αποφθεγγομενους εν κινυραις και εν ναβλαις και εν κυμβαλοις
chosen_rendering: And King Dauid and rulers of force appointed for works sons of Asaph and Haiman and Idithon, those prophesying with lyres and harps and cymbals, and their number by head was according to their works.
alternate_renderings: Those who prophesied with harps, psalteries, and cymbals.
rationale: Greek uses the uttering-oracular verb here and keeps the work-list framing. Current wording preserves that fuller scene.

greek_phrase: πατριαρχαι αρααβ καθως οι αδελφοι αυτου οι νεωτεροι
chosen_rendering: And they too received lots, like their brothers sons of Aaron, before the king and Zadok and Achimelech and chiefs of the father-houses of priests and Levites, elder fathers like their younger brothers.
alternate_renderings: The principal fathers over against their younger brethren.
rationale: Greek keeps the elder-fathers versus younger-brothers contrast here. Current wording leaves that contrast visible.

greek_phrase: εζεκιαν τον ηγουμενον του λαου μου
chosen_rendering: Turn back and say to Ezekias the leader of my people, Thus says the Lord God of Dauid your father: I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the third day you will go up into the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: Say to Hezekiah the captain of my people.
rationale: Greek says leader of my people here. Current wording keeps that term.

greek_phrase: ουτος ο νομος της ολοκαυτωσεως αυτη η ολοκαυτωσις επι της καυσεως αυτης επι του θυσιαστηριου ολην την νυκτα εως το πρωι
chosen_rendering: Charge Aaron and his sons, saying, This is the law of the whole burnt offering: this is the whole burnt offering on its burning upon the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall burn on it; it shall not be extinguished.
alternate_renderings: If a soul sins and commits a trespass against the Lord and lies to his neighbor...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the whole-burnt-offering law rather than the MT trespass case. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: και δωσω τα κωλα σου και τα κωλα παρεμβολης αλλοφυλων εν ταυτη τη ημερα τοις πετεινοις του ουρανου
chosen_rendering: And the Lord will shut you up into my hand today, and I will kill you and remove your head from you, and I will give your limbs and the limbs of the camp of the foreigners in this day to the birds of the sky and to the beasts of the earth, and all the earth will know that there is a God in Israel.
alternate_renderings: I will give the carcasses of the army of the Philistines this day to the birds of the sky.
rationale: Greek says limbs and limbs of the camp here. Current wording keeps that concrete body-part wording.

greek_phrase: αυχενα επιστρεψουσιν εναντι των εχθρων αυτων οτι εγενηθησαν αναθεμα
chosen_rendering: The sons of Israel will certainly not be able to stand against the face of their enemies. They will turn neck before their enemies, because they have become a devoted thing. I will not add to be with you any longer unless you remove the devoted thing from among you.
alternate_renderings: They will turn their backs before their enemies, because they were accursed.
rationale: Greek says turn neck and become a devoted thing here. Current wording keeps those harder forms.

greek_phrase: οτι εχθραινουσιν αυτοι υμιν εν δολιοτητι οσα δολιουσιν υμας δια φογωρ και δια χασβι
chosen_rendering: because they act as enemies toward you in the deceit with which they deceive you over Peor and over Cozbi daughter of the chief of Midian, their sister, the one struck down on the day of the plague over Peor.
alternate_renderings: Because they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.
rationale: Greek doubles the deceit language and keeps the Cozbi form. Current wording preserves that texture.

greek_phrase: και τοδε το δικαιωμα αυτου πασας τας ημερας ας εκαθητο δαυιδ εν αγρω των αλλοφυλων
chosen_rendering: And he did not keep alive man and woman to bring into Geth, saying, Lest they report in Geth against us, saying, Thus David does. And this was his rule all the days David sat in the countryside of the foreigners.
alternate_renderings: This was his manner all the while he dwelt in the country of the Philistines.
rationale: Greek says this was his rule and sat in the countryside of the foreigners. Current wording keeps that form.

chosen_rendering: Thus you shall do with his donkey, and thus you shall do with his garment, and thus you shall do with every loss of your brother, whatever may be lost from him and you find. You shall not be able to overlook it.
alternate_renderings: You may not hide yourself.
rationale: Greek says you shall not be able to overlook it. Current wording keeps that direct expression.

greek_phrase: γεγονεν μεθ' ημων ημερας τουτο δευτερον ετος και ουχ ευρηκα εν αυτω ουθεν
chosen_rendering: And the satraps of the foreigners said, Who are these passing over? And Anchous said to the generals of the foreigners, Is not this David, servant of Saoul king of Israel, who has been with us these days, this second year, and I have found nothing in him from the day he fell in with me until this day?
alternate_renderings: Has he not been with me these days or these years? and I have found no fault in him.
rationale: Greek says these days, this second year and I found nothing in him. Current wording keeps those details.

greek_phrase: και ουκ ηβουληθην αποκτειναι σε και εφεισαμην σου
chosen_rendering: Behold, on this day your eyes have seen that the Lord delivered you today into my hand in the cave, and I was not willing to kill you, and I spared you and said, I will not put my hand upon my lord, because he is anointed of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: I would not slay thee, but spared thee.
rationale: Greek says I was not willing to kill you and I spared you. Current wording keeps both verbs.

greek_phrase: και ελαβον τον επισιτισμον του λαου εν τη χειρι αυτων και τας κερατινας αυτων
chosen_rendering: And they took the food of the people in their hands and their horns, and he sent every man of Israel away, each to his tent, but the three hundred men he kept. And the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.
alternate_renderings: They took the provision of the people in their hand and their trumpets.
rationale: Greek says food of the people in their hands and keeps the three hundred men he kept line. Current wording preserves that scene.

greek_phrase: ει αληθως πασιν υμιν δωσει ο υιος ιεσσαι αγρους και αμπελωνας και παντας υμας ταξει εκατονταρχους και χιλιαρχους
chosen_rendering: And Saoul said to his servants standing by him, Hear now, sons of Benjamin. Will the son of Iessai truly give to all of you fields and vineyards and appoint all of you centurions and commanders of thousands,
alternate_renderings: Will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards and make you all captains of hundreds and captains of thousands?
rationale: Greek says centurions and commanders of thousands here. Current wording keeps those military titles.

greek_phrase: εξεκκλησιασεν την συναγωγην ιουδα και σκηπτρον βενιαμιν εκατον και εικοσι χιλιαδες νεανιων
chosen_rendering: And Roboam entered Ierousalem and assembled the congregation of Iouda and the scepter of Benjamin, one hundred twenty thousand young men who make war, to fight against the house of Israel, to return the kingdom to Roboam son of Solomon.
alternate_renderings: He assembled all the house of Judah with the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men.
rationale: Greek says scepter of Benjamin and one hundred twenty thousand young men here. Current wording keeps those Greek details.

greek_phrase: και εβασιλευσατε τον αβιμελεχ υιον της παιδισκης αυτου επι τους ανδρας σικιμων
chosen_rendering: but you rose up against my father's house today and killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, son of his maidservant, king over the men of Sikima because he is your brother,
alternate_renderings: You made Abimelech son of his bondwoman king over the men of Shechem.
rationale: Greek says maidservant and Sikima here. Current wording keeps those forms.

greek_phrase: ουκ εγνωσαν το κριμα του θεου της γης και απεστειλεν εις αυτους τους λεοντας
chosen_rendering: And they said to the king of the Assyrians, The nations whom you deported and settled in the cities of Samaria did not know the judgment of the god of the land, and he sent the lions among them, and behold, they are putting them to death because they do not know the judgment of the god of the land.
alternate_renderings: They know not the manner of the God of the land; therefore he has sent lions among them.
rationale: Greek says judgment of the god of the land here. Current wording keeps that legal-sounding term.

greek_phrase: φθεγξασθε φωνην ανακρουομενων ανα μεσον ευφραινομενων
chosen_rendering: sound forth the voice of those striking up among rejoicing ones. There they will give righteousness to the Lord; the righteous ones were strengthened in Israel. Then the people of the Lord went down to his cities.
alternate_renderings: There shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord.
rationale: Greek is highly different here and keeps musical striking-up language plus the cities ending. Current wording preserves the transmitted Greek scene.

greek_phrase: και ενεγκαι τα πρωτογενηματα της γης ημων και πρωτογενηματα καρπου παντος ξυλου
chosen_rendering: and to bring firstfruits of our land and firstfruits of fruit of every tree, year by year, into the house of the Lord,
alternate_renderings: Also the firstborn of our sons and of our cattle...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the firstfruits line rather than the MT firstborn line. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: επεβλεψας επι το θυμιαμα μου και εις την θυσιαν μου αναιδει οφθαλμω
chosen_rendering: And why did you look upon my incense and upon my sacrifice with shameless eye, and glorify your sons beyond me, to bless yourselves from the firstfruits of every sacrifice of Israel before me?
alternate_renderings: Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering... to make yourselves fat with the chiefest of all the offerings of Israel?
rationale: Greek says looked upon my incense and upon my sacrifice with shameless eye. Current wording keeps that sharp image.

greek_phrase: διηλθον δια της γης σελχα και διηλθον δια της γης εασακεμ και ουκ ην και διηλθον δια της γης ιακιμ
chosen_rendering: And they passed through the hill-country of Ephraim, and they passed through the land of Selcha and did not find them, and they passed through the land of Shaalim and it was not there, and they passed through the land of Iakim and did not find them.
alternate_renderings: They passed through the land of Shalisha and the land of Shalim and the land of the Benjamites.
rationale: Greek gives the place forms Selcha, Shaalim, and Iakim here. Current wording keeps those forms.

greek_phrase: και τα αγαθα των ποιμνιων και των βουκολιων και των εδεσματων και των αμπελωνων και παντων των αγαθων
chosen_rendering: And Saoul and all the people preserved Agag alive and the good things of the flocks and the herds and the foods and the vineyards and all the good things, and they were not willing to destroy them. But every dishonored and worthless thing they destroyed.
alternate_renderings: Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and oxen and fatlings and lambs and all that was good.
rationale: Greek says foods and vineyards here rather than the familiar MT inventory. Current wording keeps the Greek list.

greek_phrase: ενα αιροντα τρια αιγιδια και ενα αιροντα τρια αγγεια αρτων και ενα αιροντα ασκον οινου
chosen_rendering: And you will pass on from there and beyond, and you will come as far as the oak of Thabor, and you will find there three men going up to God at Baithēl, one carrying three kids, one carrying three vessels of breads, and one carrying a skin of wine.
alternate_renderings: One carrying three kids and another carrying three loaves of bread and another carrying a bottle of wine.
rationale: Greek says three vessels of breads here. Current wording keeps that unusual container wording.

greek_phrase: απεστρεψαν το προσωπον απο της σκηνης κυριου και εδωκαν αυχενα
chosen_rendering: Because our fathers rebelled and did evil before the Lord and forsook him and turned face away from the tent of the Lord and gave neck.
alternate_renderings: They turned away their faces from the habitation of the Lord and turned their backs.
rationale: Greek says gave neck here rather than turned backs. Current wording keeps that image.

greek_phrase: εξελθη το παιδιον αυτης μη εξεικονισμενον επιζημιον ζημιωθησεται καθοτι αν επιβαλη ο ανηρ της γυναικος δωσει μετα αξιωματος
chosen_rendering: If two men fight and strike a pregnant woman, and her child comes out not yet formed, he shall pay a penalty according as the woman's husband lays upon him. He shall pay with assessment.
alternate_renderings: If her fruit depart and yet no mischief follow he shall be punished as the judges determine.
rationale: Greek says child comes out not yet formed and pay with assessment. Current wording keeps those juridical details.

chosen_rendering: And house which I am building is great, because our God is great above all gods.
alternate_renderings: Behold I build a house to the name of the Lord my God to dedicate it to him and to burn before him sweet incense...
rationale: This LXX verse number carries the great-house line rather than the MT long dedication list. Current wording keeps the Greek mapping.

greek_phrase: τους ανδρας τους ασεβεις τους εν γαβαα τους υιους βελιαλ και θανατωσομεν αυτους και εξαρουμεν κακιαν εξ ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: And now give the men, the ungodly ones in Gabaa, the sons of Belial, and we will put them to death and remove evil from Israel. But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: Give up the men the sons of Belial that are in Gibeah and we will put them to death and purge evil from Israel.
rationale: Greek says the men, the ungodly ones, the sons of Belial. Current wording keeps that doubled characterization.

greek_phrase: εν αιμασιν υιου ιωδαε του ιερεως και εθανατωσαν αυτον επι της κλινης αυτου
chosen_rendering: And after they departed from him, leaving him in great weaknesses, his servants conspired against him over bloods of son of Jehoiada the priest and killed him on his bed, and he died. And they buried him in City of Dauid, but they did not bury him in tomb of kings.
alternate_renderings: His servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest and slew him on his bed.
rationale: Greek says bloods of son of Iōdae the priest here. Current wording keeps that form.

greek_phrase: απο των διχηλουντων τας οπλας και ονυχιζοντων ονυχιστηρας
chosen_rendering: And these you shall not eat from those that bring up cud and from those that part the hoof and split the claws: the camel and the hare and the hyrax, because they bring up cud but do not part the hoof. These are unclean for you.
alternate_renderings: These you shall not eat of them that chew the cud and divide the hoof as the camel and the hare and the coney.
rationale: Greek says part the hoof and split the claws here and uses hyrax. Current wording keeps those details.

greek_phrase: δια χειρος ανανιου του διαδοχου του βασιλεως
chosen_rendering: And Ozias had forces making war and going out for battle in number, and their number by the hand of Jeiel the scribe and Maasaiou the judge, by the hand of Ananiou, successor of the king.
alternate_renderings: By the hand of Hananiah one of the king's captains.
rationale: Greek says by hand of Ananiou successor of king here. Current wording keeps that title.

greek_phrase: οικετις διαπεφυλαγμενη ανθρωπω και αυτη λυτροις ου λελυτρωται η ελευθερια ουκ εδοθη αυτη επισκοπη εσται αυτοις
chosen_rendering: And if a man lies with a woman with the bed of seed, and she is a female servant reserved for a man, and she has not been redeemed with a ransom, nor has freedom been given to her, there shall be oversight for them. They shall not die, because she has not been freed.
alternate_renderings: If a man lie carnally with a bondmaid betrothed to a husband and not redeemed nor freedom given her, she shall be scourged.
rationale: Greek says reserved for a man and there shall be oversight for them. Current wording keeps those legal terms.

greek_phrase: εαν δε γενηται η αφεσις των υιων ισραηλ και προστεθησεται η κληρονομια αυτων επι την κληρονομιαν της φυλης οις αν γενωνται γυναικες

chosen_rendering: Say to them: Throughout your generations any man from all your seed who approaches the holy things that the sons of Israel consecrate to the Lord, while his uncleanness is upon him, that person shall be destroyed from before me. I am the Lord your God.
alternate_renderings: cut off from my presence
rationale: Greek says destroyed from before me. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: φυλαξαι ουν αυριον πρωι και κρυβηθι και καθισον κρυβη
chosen_rendering: And Iōnathan reported to David, saying, Saoul seeks to put you to death. Therefore guard yourself tomorrow morning and hide and sit concealed.
alternate_renderings: abide in a secret place, and hide yourself
rationale: Greek says hide and sit concealed. Current wording keeps that doubled concealment.

greek_phrase: αιλαμ κατα προσωπον του οικου ... κατεχρυσωσεν αυτον εσωθεν
chosen_rendering: And vestibule before the house, length according to breadth of the house, twenty cubits, and height one hundred twenty cubits, and he overlaid it inside with pure gold.
alternate_renderings: porch in front of the house ...
rationale: Greek says ai(l)am or vestibule here and inside with pure gold. Current wording keeps that compact LXX form.

greek_phrase: ουτος εποιησεν και τους πασσαλους της σκηνης
chosen_rendering: He made the pegs of the tent and the pegs of the court bronze.
alternate_renderings: This is the sum of the tabernacle ...
rationale: LXX here gives the peg notice instead of the MT inventory summary. Current wording keeps that major variant.

greek_phrase: μη αντι τουτου ου θανατωθησεται σεμει οτι κατηρασατο τον χριστον κυριου
chosen_rendering: And Abessa son of Sarouia answered and said, Shall not Semei be put to death for this, because he cursed the anointed of the Lord?
alternate_renderings: What have I to do with you sons of Zeruiah ...
rationale: LXX here gives Abessa's death-demand line instead of David's MT reply. Current wording keeps that variant.

greek_phrase: μη εκλυσης τας χειρας σου απο των παιδων σου
chosen_rendering: And those dwelling in Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp of Israel in Galgala, saying, Do not let your hands grow weak from your servants. Come up to us quickly and rescue us and help us, because all the kings of the Amorites dwelling in the hill country are gathered against us.
alternate_renderings: slack not thy hand from thy servants
rationale: Greek says let your hands grow weak from your servants. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

greek_phrase: ουκ εσται σοι τουτο βδελυγμος και σκανδαλον ... και αγαθωσει κυριος τω κυριω μου
chosen_rendering: And this will not be to you an abomination and a stumbling for my lord, to pour out innocent blood for nothing and for the hand of my lord to save for himself. And the Lord will do good to my lord, and you will remember your servant to do good to her.
alternate_renderings: no grief nor offence of heart ... avenged himself
rationale: Greek says abomination and stumbling here and keeps the hand-saving phrasing. Current wording follows that LXX line.

greek_phrase: μη εκκλινωσιν τας καρδιας υμων οπισω ειδωλων αυτων εις αυτους εκολληθη σαλωμων του αγαπησαι
chosen_rendering: from the nations of which the Lord said to the sons of Israel, You shall not go in to them, and they shall not go in to you, lest they turn your hearts aside after their idols. To these Solomon clung, to love.
alternate_renderings: Solomon clave unto these in love
rationale: Greek says after their idols and Solomon clung to love. Current wording keeps that LXX ending.

chosen_rendering: And it happened after three months, it was reported to Judah, saying, Tamar your daughter-in-law has prostituted herself, and look, she is with child from prostitution. And Judah said, Bring her out and let her be burned.
alternate_renderings: played the harlot ...
rationale: Greek says prostituted herself and from prostitution. Current wording keeps that direct LXX wording.

greek_phrase: εστησα εις τα κατωτατα του τοπου κατοπισθεν του τειχους εν τοις σκεπεινοις
chosen_rendering: And I stationed in the lowest parts of the place behind the wall, in the sheltered places, and I stationed the people by clans with their swords, their spears, and their bows.
alternate_renderings: when Sanballat and Tobiah heard ...
rationale: LXX here gives Nehemiah's defense deployment instead of the MT opposition report. Current wording keeps that variant.

greek_phrase: περιελευσεται επι το μερος το βλεπον παρα θαλασσαν απο λιβος
chosen_rendering: And the boundary shall pass through and go around on the side facing the sea from the south, from the mountain opposite Bethhoron to the south, and its outlet shall be at Kirjathbaal, this is Kirjathjearim, a city of the sons of Judah. This is the side toward the sea.
alternate_renderings: this was the west quarter
rationale: Greek says side facing the sea and side toward the sea. Current wording keeps that LXX orientation while using standard English place names.

greek_phrase: ουδε δια την οσιοτητα της καρδιας σου
chosen_rendering: Not because of your righteousness or because of the holiness of your heart are you entering to inherit their land, but because of the ungodliness of these nations the Lord will utterly destroy them from before your face, and so that he may establish his covenant that he swore to your fathers, to Abraham and to Isaac and to Jacob.
alternate_renderings: uprightness of your heart ... perform the word
rationale: Greek says holiness of your heart and establish his covenant. Current wording keeps those LXX terms.

chosen_rendering: And he told them to seek Ahaziah, and they seized him while he was being healed in Samaria and brought him to Jehu, and he killed him and buried him, because they said, He is a son of Jehoshaphat who sought the Lord with all his heart. And there was none in the house of Ahaziah strong enough for the kingdom.
alternate_renderings: for he was hid in Samaria ...
rationale: Greek says he was being healed in Samaria. Current wording keeps that LXX scene while using standard English names and all-heart idiom.

greek_phrase: κολλυριδα αρτου και εσχαριτην και λαγανον απο τηγανου
chosen_rendering: And he distributed to all the people, to all the host of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, from man to woman, to each a cake of bread and a roasted cake and a pan-cake, and all the people went away, each to his house.
alternate_renderings: piece of flesh and flagon of wine
rationale: Greek gives bread cake, roasted cake, and pan-cake here. Current wording keeps that LXX food list.

greek_phrase: ανηγγειλεν αυτη παντα τα απο καρδιας αυτου
chosen_rendering: And Dalila saw that he had told her everything from his heart, and she sent and called all the satraps of the foreigners, saying, Come up this once, because he told me all his heart. And all the satraps of the foreigners came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
alternate_renderings: he told her all his heart
rationale: Greek repeats heart twice and uses satraps of the foreigners. Current wording keeps that LXX form.

greek_phrase: εστη πηγμα εν αφεστηκος μακραν σφοδρα σφοδρως
chosen_rendering: then the waters coming down from above stood, a mass standing exceedingly far away, as far as the region of Kariathiarim, but the waters going down went down into the Arabah sea, the Salt Sea, until the end they failed, and the people stood opposite Jericho.
alternate_renderings: rose up upon a heap very far from Adam ...
rationale: Greek gives a mass standing exceedingly far away and Kariathiarim. Current wording keeps that LXX geography.

greek_phrase: ινα τι ακουεις των λογων του λαου λεγοντων
chosen_rendering: And David said to Saoul, Why do you listen to the words of the people saying, Behold, David seeks your life?
alternate_renderings: behold, this day your eyes have seen ...
rationale: LXX here gives only David's challenge question instead of the MT cave-sparing speech. Current wording keeps that variant.

greek_phrase: περι παντος του καταλειφθεντος εν ισραηλ και ιουδα
chosen_rendering: Go, seek the Lord concerning me and concerning everyone left in Israel and in Iouda, concerning the words of book found, because great wrath of the Lord is kindled among us, because our fathers did not listen to the words of the Lord, to do according to all things written in this book.
alternate_renderings: for them that are left ...
rationale: Greek says everyone left in Israel and in Judah and wrath is kindled. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: εφ' οριων γης χανααν επι του γαλααδ του ιορδανου
chosen_rendering: And the sons of Israel heard people saying, Behold, the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben and the half tribe of Manasseh built an altar on the borders of the land of Canaan, at Galaad of the Jordan, on the far side of the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: at the passage of the children of Israel
rationale: Greek says on the borders of the land of Canaan at Galaad of the Jordan. Current wording keeps that LXX location.

chosen_rendering: And I gave the Levites as an offering, given to Aaron and to his sons from the midst of the sons of Israel, to work the works of the sons of Israel in the tent of testimony and to make atonement for the sons of Israel, and there shall not be among the sons of Israel one coming near the holy things.
alternate_renderings: as a gift ... no plague ... sanctuary
rationale: Greek says as an offering, given, and one coming near the holy things. Current wording keeps those LXX terms.

chosen_rendering: And Elijah said, In zeal I have been very zealous for the Lord Almighty, because the sons of Israel forsook your covenant, they pulled down your altars, and they killed your prophets with the sword, and I alone am left, utterly alone, and they seek my life to take it.
alternate_renderings: I, even I only, am left
rationale: Greek intensifies with utterly alone. Current wording keeps that LXX emphasis.

greek_phrase: επιθειναι επι αβιμελεχ ... και επι τους ανδρας σικιμων
chosen_rendering: to bring the injustice of the seventy sons of Jerobaal and to lay their blood upon Abimelech their brother who killed them, and upon the men of Sikima who strengthened his hands so as to kill his brothers.
alternate_renderings: that the cruelty done ... might come
rationale: Greek says to lay their blood upon Abimelech and upon the men of Sikima. Current wording keeps that judicial wording.

greek_phrase: προσεχετωσαν απο των αγιων ... ου βεβηλωσουσιν το ονομα το αγιον μου
chosen_rendering: Speak to Aaron and his sons, and let them attend carefully to the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they shall not profane my holy name in what they consecrate to me. I am the Lord.
alternate_renderings: separate themselves from the holy things
rationale: Greek says let them attend carefully to the holy things. Current wording keeps that LXX instruction.

greek_phrase: μη εξελθατωσαν εκ της πολεως τα παιδαρια αρχοντων των χωρων
chosen_rendering: And these came out from the city, the servant-boys of the rulers of the regions, and the force behind them.
alternate_renderings: Have you killed and also taken possession ...
rationale: LXX here gives the city sortie line instead of the MT Naboth judgment speech. Current wording keeps that major variant.

chosen_rendering: and pass through opposite the ascent of Akrabin and go around Senna and ascend from the south onto Kadesh-Barnea and go out to Asoron and go up to Addara and circle westward Kadesh,
alternate_renderings: went out to the south side to Maalehacrabbim ...
rationale: Greek gives this route with Senna, Asoron, and Addara. Current wording keeps those LXX place forms.

greek_phrase: παντα τα θηρια ... και αυξανεσθε και πληθυνεσθε
chosen_rendering: and all the wild beasts that are with you, and all flesh from birds to cattle, and every creeping thing moving on the earth, bring out with yourself. And increase and multiply upon the earth.
alternate_renderings: every living thing ... that they may breed abundantly
rationale: Greek says wild beasts and then increase and multiply. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: ιεβοσθε ο χαναναιος αρχων του τριτου ... αδινων ο ασωναιος
chosen_rendering: These are the names of the mighty men of David: Iebosthe the Chananite, chief of the third. This is Adinon the Asonaean. He drew his sword over eight hundred wounded at one time.
alternate_renderings: The Tachmonite ... Adino the Eznite ... spear
rationale: Greek preserves different names and says wounded rather than slain. Current wording keeps that LXX reading.

greek_phrase: θραυσμα εστιν λεπρα της κεφαλης η λεπρα του πωγωνος
chosen_rendering: the priest shall inspect the mark, and if its appearance is deeper than the skin and there is in it thin yellowish hair, the priest shall pronounce him unclean. It is a scaly patch; it is skin-disease of the head or skin-disease of the beard.
alternate_renderings: it is a dry scab ...
rationale: Greek says scaly patch here. Current wording keeps that LXX diagnosis.

chosen_rendering: And all dwelling on this land have heard that you are Lord among this people, that you, Lord, are seen eye to eye, and your cloud stands over them, and in a pillar of cloud you go before them by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
alternate_renderings: seen face to face
rationale: Greek says seen eye to eye. Current wording keeps that striking LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: ου εστιν εκει το αναστημα των αλλοφυλων ... χορω προφητων
chosen_rendering: And after these things you will enter the hill of God, where the station of the foreigners is, there at Nasib the foreigner. And it will be when you enter there into the city, you will meet a chorus of prophets coming down from the high place, and before them harp and tambourine and flute and lyre, and they prophesying.
alternate_renderings: garrison of the Philistines ... company of prophets
rationale: Greek says station of the foreigners and chorus of prophets. Current wording keeps those LXX terms.

greek_phrase: το στεαρ και την οσφυν αμωμον συν ταις ψοαις
chosen_rendering: And from the sacrifice of salvation he shall bring an offering to God: the fat and the unblemished hind-part, he shall remove it with the lower back, and the fat of the belly,
alternate_renderings: the whole rump ... hard by the backbone
rationale: Greek says unblemished hind-part with the lower back. Current wording keeps that LXX anatomy.

greek_phrase: προφητας εστησας σεαυτω ινα καθισης εν ιερουσαλημ εις βασιλεα
chosen_rendering: And besides these things, you appointed prophets for yourself so that you might sit in Ierousalem as king in Iouda, and now these words will be reported to the king. So now come, let us take counsel together.
alternate_renderings: appointed prophets to preach of you ... there is a king in Judah
rationale: Greek says appointed prophets for yourself so that you might sit as king. Current wording keeps that LXX accusation.

greek_phrase: κτῆσαι ημας και την γην ημων αντι αρτων
chosen_rendering: So then, let us not die before you and let not the land be made desolate. Buy us and our land for bread, and we and our land will be servants to Pharaoh. Give seed, so that we may sow and live and not die, and the land will not be made desolate.
alternate_renderings: buy us and our land for bread
rationale: Greek explicitly says buy us and our land for bread. Current wording keeps that LXX plea.

greek_phrase: μη ευπορηθη η χειρ αυτου το ικανον
chosen_rendering: But if his hand does not prosper enough to repay him, then the sale shall remain with the one who acquired it until the year of release, and he shall go out in the release and return to his possession.
alternate_renderings: if he be not able to restore it
rationale: Greek says if his hand does not prosper enough. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: απολειται η ψυχη εκεινη εκ του λαου αυτης
chosen_rendering: And if a person touches any unclean thing, whether human uncleanness or unclean quadrupeds or any unclean abomination, and eats from the flesh of the sacrifice of salvation, which belongs to the Lord, that person shall perish from his people.
alternate_renderings: shall be cut off from his people
rationale: Greek says shall perish from his people. Current wording keeps that LXX verb.

greek_phrase: τα πρωτοτοκα υιων ημων και κτηνων ημων ως γεγραπται εν τω νομω
chosen_rendering: and the firstborn of our sons and our cattle as written in the law, and firstborn of our cattle and our flocks, to bring into the house of our God, to the priests ministering in the house of our God,
alternate_renderings: first-fruits of our dough ... tithes of our ground
rationale: LXX here gives the firstborn obligation line rather than the MT firstfruits list. Current wording keeps that variant.

greek_phrase: επισυστησω εφ' υμας την αποριαν την τε ψωραν και τον ικτερον
chosen_rendering: then I also will do this to you: I will bring upon you distress, scab, and jaundice, wasting your eyes and consuming your life, and you will sow your seed for nothing, and your adversaries will eat it.
alternate_renderings: terror, consumption, and burning ague
rationale: Greek says distress, scab, and jaundice here. Current wording keeps that LXX disease list.

greek_phrase: επορευθην μετ' αυτων εν θυμω πλαγιω ... εντραπησεται η καρδια αυτων
chosen_rendering: And I also went with them in anger at odds and destroyed them in the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised heart will be ashamed, and then they will accept their sins.
alternate_renderings: walked contrary ... be humbled
rationale: Greek says anger at odds and heart will be ashamed. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: και επαταξεν κυριος τους αιθιοπας εναντιον ιουδα
chosen_rendering: And the Lord struck Aithiopians before Iouda, and Aithiopians fled.
alternate_renderings: Asa cried unto the LORD ...
rationale: LXX here gives only the victory result instead of Asa's MT prayer. Current wording keeps that variant.

greek_phrase: προσηλυτους τους παροικουντας μετ' αυτου ... προσετεθησαν προς αυτον πολλοι
chosen_rendering: And he assembled Iouda and Beniamin and sojourners dwelling with him from Ephraim and from Manasse and from Symeon, because many from Israel joined themselves to him when they saw that the Lord his God was with him.
alternate_renderings: strangers with them ... they fell to him
rationale: Greek says sojourners dwelling with him and many joined themselves to him. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And they stood away from the tent of Korah all around, and Dathan and Abiram came out and stood by the doors of their tents, and their wives and their children and their baggage.
alternate_renderings: their households; their little ones
rationale: Greek ends with their baggage. Current wording keeps that LXX noun instead of replacing it with a household term.

greek_phrase: εν τω αγαπησαι κυριον τον λαον αυτου εδωκεν σε επ' αυτους εις βασιλεα
chosen_rendering: And Chiram king of Tyre answered in writing and sent to Salomon, Because the Lord loved his people, he gave you king over them.
alternate_renderings: I will give your servants wheat and barley and wine and oil
rationale: LXX here gives Chiram's reply sentence rather than the MT supply list. Current wording keeps that variant.

chosen_rendering: And it happened, when the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord came up out of the Jordan and set their feet on the land, the water of the Jordan rushed down to its place and went as yesterday and the third day along all the bank.
alternate_renderings: as before; over all its banks as formerly
rationale: Greek says as yesterday and the third day. Current wording keeps that unusual LXX time phrase.

chosen_rendering: And Saoul said, Thus you will say to David: The king does not desire in a marriage gift, except one hundred foreskins of foreigners, to avenge on the enemies of the king. And Saoul thought to cast him into the hands of the foreigners.
alternate_renderings: dowry ... Philistines
rationale: Greek says marriage gift and foreigners. Current wording keeps those LXX terms.

greek_phrase: εν απλοτητι καρδιας προεθυμηθην παντα ταυτα
chosen_rendering: And I knew, Lord, that you examine hearts and love righteousness. In simplicity of heart I was willing for all these things, and now I saw your people found here willingly giving to you with gladness.
alternate_renderings: uprightness of heart ... willingly offered
rationale: Greek says simplicity of heart and saw your people found here willingly giving. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: καθαπερ εχθες και τριτην ημεραν και το της σημερον
chosen_rendering: And the scribes from the race of the sons of Israel, those appointed over them by Pharaoh's overseers, were beaten, saying, 'Why have you not completed your quotas of brick-making as yesterday and the day before, and now today as well?'

rationale: Greek stacks the time complaint with yesterday, the third day, and today's work. Current wording keeps that running complaint.

greek_phrase: φυλασσοντες τας φυλακας του αγιου εις τας φυλακας των υιων ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: And those camping before the tent of testimony on the east were Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charges of the sanctuary for the charges of the sons of Israel. And the stranger who touches shall die.
alternate_renderings: keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the children of Israel
rationale: Greek repeats charge and charges in both halves. Current wording keeps that LXX repetition.

greek_phrase: τι οτι εκλεψαν σε οι αδελφοι ημων ανηρ ιουδα
chosen_rendering: And behold, every man of Israel came to the king and said to the king, Why did our brothers, the men of Iouda, steal you away and bring the king and his house across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?
alternate_renderings: why have our brothers the men of Judah stolen you away
rationale: Greek says the men of Iouda steal you away. Current wording keeps that accusation and the direct address to the king.

chosen_rendering: And from the half of the sons of Israel you shall take one out of fifty, from the humans and from the oxen and from the sheep and from the donkeys and from all the cattle, and you shall give them to the Levites who keep the charges in the tent of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: one portion of fifty ... persons
rationale: Greek says one out of fifty and humans. Current wording keeps that LXX counting and noun choice.

chosen_rendering: And Aaron spoke to Moses, saying, If today they have brought near their things for sin and their whole burnt offerings before the Lord, and these things have happened to me, and were I to eat the things for sin today, would it be pleasing to the Lord?
alternate_renderings: their sin offerings
rationale: Greek says the things for sin here. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

greek_phrase: και τας εν γαστρι εχουσας ανερρηξεν
chosen_rendering: Then Manaēm struck Thersa and all that was in it and its borders from Thersa, because they did not open to him, and he struck it, and the pregnant women he ripped open.
alternate_renderings: ripped up all the women with child
rationale: Greek explicitly says the pregnant women he ripped open. Current wording keeps that harsh LXX line.

greek_phrase: πας ο χωριζομενος της ακαθαρσιας εθνων της γης προς αυτους
chosen_rendering: And sons of Israel from the exile ate the Passover, and everyone separating himself from uncleanness of nations of the land to them, to seek the Lord God of Israel.
