rationale: Greek says separating himself from uncleanness of nations of the land to them. Current wording keeps that LXX construction.

greek_phrase: ημεις καταδυναστευομεν τους υιους ημων και τας θυγατερας ημων εις δουλους
chosen_rendering: And now flesh of our brothers is our flesh, as their sons are our sons, and behold we oppress our sons and our daughters into slavery, and some from our daughters are being oppressed, and there is no power in our hands, and our fields and our vineyards belong to the nobles.
alternate_renderings: we bring our sons and daughters into bondage
rationale: Greek says we oppress our sons and daughters into slavery. Current wording keeps that LXX verb.

greek_phrase: γυναικα σοφην ... εση ως γυνη πενθουσα
chosen_rendering: And Iōab sent to Thekōe and took from there a wise woman and said to her, Mourn now and put on mourning garments and do not anoint with oil, and you will be as a woman mourning over one dead for many days.
alternate_renderings: cunning woman ... feign yourself to be a mourner
rationale: Greek says wise woman and you will be as a mourning woman. Current wording keeps that LXX framing.

greek_phrase: εις υμνειν και αινειν ... εφημερια προς εφημεριαν
chosen_rendering: And leaders of the Levites were Asabia and Sarabia and Iesou and sons of Kadmiel, and their brothers opposite them, to hymn and praise by the command of David man of God, course by course.
alternate_renderings: to praise and give thanks ... ward over against ward
rationale: Greek says to hymn and praise, course by course. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: thus may God do to Iōnathan and thus may he add, if I bring the evils upon you and do not uncover your ear and send you away, and you go in peace. And the Lord will be with you as he was with my father.
alternate_renderings: make it known to you
rationale: Greek says uncover your ear. Current wording keeps that Hebrew-like LXX idiom.

greek_phrase: πασσαλος εσται σοι επι της ζωνης σου
chosen_rendering: and a peg shall be for you on your belt, and it shall be, when you sit outside, then you shall dig with it and, turning back, you shall cover your indecency with it.
alternate_renderings: a trowel on your girdle
rationale: LXX places the peg instruction here and keeps the belt wording. Current line stays close to that verse form.

greek_phrase: μη υμεις νυν δικαζεσθε περι του βααλ η υμεις σωζετε αυτον
chosen_rendering: And Joash said to the men standing against him, Will you now judge on behalf of Baal, or will you save him? Whoever pleads his case shall die by morning. If he is a god, let him avenge himself, because his altar was dug down.
alternate_renderings: will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him?
rationale: Greek says judge on behalf of Baal or save him. Current wording keeps that LXX challenge.

greek_phrase: σαουλ κατακληρουται εργον επι ισραηλ ... ου αν εστραφη εσωζετο
chosen_rendering: And Saoul took up rule over Israel and fought all his enemies round about, against Mōab and against the sons of Ammon and against the sons of Edom and against the kings of Zobah and against the foreigners. Wherever he turned, he was being saved.
alternate_renderings: Saul took the kingdom ... wherever he turned he vexed them
rationale: Greek says took up rule and wherever he turned he was being saved. Difficult Baithor/king-Souba sequence regularized to the standard English referent kings of Zobah.

greek_phrase: τα μαρτυρια αυτου οσα διεμαρτυρατο αυτοις ουκ εφυλαξαν
chosen_rendering: And his testimonies, which he testified to them, they did not keep, and they went after vanities and became vain, and after the nations around them, concerning whom he commanded them not to do according to these.
alternate_renderings: they rejected his statutes and his covenant
rationale: Greek says his testimonies, which he testified to them, they did not keep. Current wording keeps that LXX repetition.

greek_phrase: την ερυθραν θαλασσαν ... ους εξωλεθρευσατε αυτους
chosen_rendering: for we heard that the Lord God dried up the Red Sea from before your face when you came out from Egypt, and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
alternate_renderings: the Red sea ... whom ye utterly destroyed
rationale: Greek explicitly says Red Sea and whom you utterly destroyed. Current wording keeps that LXX memory report.

greek_phrase: προσεχεον επι το θυσιαστηριον ... περιεχεον το αιμα τω θυσιαστηριω
chosen_rendering: And they slaughtered calves, and priests received blood and poured it upon the altar, and they slaughtered rams and poured blood upon the altar, and they slaughtered lambs and poured blood to the altar.
alternate_renderings: sprinkled the blood on the altar

rationale: Greek says two line-measures for putting to death, and two line-measures he kept alive. Current wording keeps that LXX measurement line.

greek_phrase: εντιμωθητω δη η ψυχη μου ... εν οφθαλμοις σου
chosen_rendering: And the king added yet to send a third captain of fifty and his fifty, and the third captain of fifty came to him and bent upon his knees before Elijah and begged him and spoke to him and said, Man of God, let my life now be precious, and the life of these fifty servants of yours, in your eyes.

greek_phrase: εν ευφροσυνη και εν ωδαις δια χειρος δαυιδ

rationale: Greek says what he may speak, when it comes, it will stand. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

alternate_renderings: pins and all the instruments of the tabernacle
rationale: Greek says pegs and all the instruments for the works of the tent of testimony. Current wording keeps that LXX inventory line.

chosen_rendering: killing, you shall kill all those dwelling in that city with the slaughter of the sword. With a devoted thing you shall devote it and everything in it.
alternate_renderings: thou shalt surely smite ... utterly destroy it
rationale: Greek doubles the devote verb. Current wording keeps that LXX emphasis.

greek_phrase: ακουσατε μου ανδρες σικιμων και ακουσαι υμων ο θεος
chosen_rendering: And they reported it to Jōatham, and he went and stood on the top of Mount Garizin and lifted up his voice and cried out and said to them, Hear me, men of Sikima, and may God hear you.
alternate_renderings: hearken unto me ... that God may hearken unto you
rationale: Greek says hear me, men of Sikima, and may God hear you. Current wording keeps that LXX address.

greek_phrase: και εγω ειμι ιστημι επι τας χειρας μου χιλιους σικλους αργυριου
chosen_rendering: But the man said to Ioab, Even if a thousand silver shekels were weighed into my hands, I would never put my hand against the king's son. For in our hearing the king charged you and Abessa and Ittai, saying, Guard for my sake the young man Abessalom.
alternate_renderings: though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in my hand
rationale: Greek says even if I stand on my hands a thousand silver shekels. Current wording smooths minimally but keeps the refusal and silver-shekel line.

chosen_rendering: And the boundaries will go down to the ravine of Karana to the south by the ravine of Jariel, terebinth, to Ephraim in the midst of the city of Manasseh, and the boundary of Manasseh is to the north by the torrent, and its outlet shall be the sea.
alternate_renderings: southward of the brook Kanah
rationale: Greek preserves the Jariel terebinth detail here. Current wording keeps that LXX place wording.

chosen_rendering: And it will be, if they do not believe you by these two signs and do not listen to your voice, you shall take from the water of the river and pour it on the dry ground, and the water that you take from the river will become blood on the dry ground.
alternate_renderings: shall become blood upon the dry land
rationale: Greek says blood on the dry ground. Current wording keeps that LXX result.

greek_phrase: επι την αγχιστειαν και επι το ανταλλαγμα του στησαι παν λογον
chosen_rendering: And this was the custom formerly in Israel concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to establish every word: a man would loosen his sandal and give it to his neighbor redeeming his right, and this was a witness in Israel.
alternate_renderings: concerning redeeming and concerning changing
rationale: Greek says concerning redemption and concerning exchange, to establish every word. Current wording keeps that LXX legal custom line.

chosen_rendering: And Dauid said, Salomon my son is tender youth, and house to build for the Lord must be for greatness beyond, for name and for glory in all the earth; I will prepare for him. And Dauid prepared in abundance before his death.
alternate_renderings: young and tender ... exceeding magnifical
rationale: Greek says tender youth and for greatness beyond. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: εισηγαγες εις διαθηκην κυριου τον δουλον σου μετα σεαυτου
chosen_rendering: And you will do mercy with your servant, because you brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself. And if there is wrongdoing in your servant, you put me to death, and why do you thus bring me to your father?
alternate_renderings: thou hast brought thy servant into a covenant of the LORD with thee
rationale: Greek says brought your servant into a covenant of the Lord with yourself. Current wording keeps that LXX covenant line.

greek_phrase: σκολοπες εν τοις οφθαλμοις υμων και βολιδες εν ταις πλευραις υμων
chosen_rendering: But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of the land from before you, then those you leave from them shall be spikes in your eyes and darts in your sides, and they shall be hostile over the land on which you dwell.
alternate_renderings: pricks in your eyes and thorns in your sides
rationale: Greek says spikes in your eyes and darts in your sides. Current wording keeps that harsher LXX image.

chosen_rendering: And the Lord will pass by to strike the Egyptians, and he will see the blood on the lintel and on both doorposts, and the Lord will pass by the door and will not allow the destroyer to enter your houses to strike.
alternate_renderings: will not suffer the destroyer to come in
rationale: Greek says will not allow the destroyer to enter. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: And Dauid said to God, Was it not I who said to number among people? And I am one who sinned; I acted evilly with evil. But these sheep, what did they do? Lord God, let your hand be on me and on the house of my father, and not on your people for destruction, Lord.
alternate_renderings: I have sinned greatly, but as for these sheep
rationale: Greek says I acted evilly with evil. Current wording keeps that emphatic LXX confession.

greek_phrase: οι γραμματεις ... ινα μη δειλιανη την καρδιαν του αδελφου αυτου
chosen_rendering: And the scribes shall add to speak to the people and say, Who is the man who is fearful and cowardly in heart? Let him go and return to his house, lest he make his brother's heart cowardly like his own.
alternate_renderings: lest his brethren's heart faint as well as his heart
rationale: Greek says scribes shall add to speak and lest he make his brother's heart cowardly. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And they were by the great stone that is in Gabaon, and Amessai came before them. And Ioab was girded with his cloak, his garment, and over it he was girded with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath, and the sword came out and fell.
alternate_renderings: Joab's garment that he had put on, and upon it a girdle with a sword ... and as he went forth it fell out
rationale: Greek says the sword came out and fell. Current wording keeps that LXX detail.

chosen_rendering: And now I have sent to you wise man, knowing understanding, Chiram my father,
alternate_renderings: Huram my father's
rationale: Greek says Chiram my father. Current wording keeps that LXX form.

greek_phrase: τις ο θυμος της οργης ο μεγας ουτος
chosen_rendering: And all the nations will say, Why did the Lord do thus to this land? What is this great wrath of anger?
alternate_renderings: what meaneth the heat of this great anger
rationale: Greek says this great wrath of anger. Current wording keeps that doubled LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: παρα το μη δυνασθαι κυριον ... και παρα το μισησαι αυτους
chosen_rendering: lest those dwelling in the land from which you brought us out there say, Because the Lord was not able to bring them into the land that he said to them, and because he hated them, he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.
alternate_renderings: because the LORD was not able ... because he hated them
rationale: Greek repeats because ... and because. Current wording keeps that LXX argument.

greek_phrase: εις ηλους εν ταις πτερναις υμων και εις βολιδας εν τοις οφθαλμοις υμων
chosen_rendering: know that the Lord will certainly not continue to destroy these nations from before you, and they shall become snares for you and scandals and nails in your heels and darts in your eyes until you perish from this good land that the Lord your God gave you.
alternate_renderings: scourges in your sides and thorns in your eyes
rationale: Greek says nails in your heels and darts in your eyes. Current wording keeps that striking LXX image.

chosen_rendering: Blessed are you, Israel. Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord? Your helper shields, and your sword boasts, and your enemies shall lie to you, and you shall step on their neck.
alternate_renderings: the sword of thy excellency
rationale: Greek says your sword boasts. Current wording keeps that unusual LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: εν τω περαν του ιορδανου παρα θαλασσαν
chosen_rendering: And to the half tribe of Manasseh Moses gave a share in Bashanitis, and to the other half Joshua gave a share with their brothers beyond the Jordan by the sea. And when Joshua sent them away to their houses, he blessed them,
alternate_renderings: on this side Jordan westward
rationale: Greek says beyond the Jordan by the sea. Current wording keeps that LXX location wording.

greek_phrase: πασαις ταις γαζαις ταις εν περα του ποταμου
chosen_rendering: And from me, I Arthasastha the king, set a decree to all the treasuries beyond the River, that whatever Ezra the priest and scribe of the law of the God of heaven asks from you, let it be promptly done,
alternate_renderings: all the treasurers which are beyond the river
rationale: Greek says all treasuries beyond the River. Current wording keeps that LXX noun.

chosen_rendering: And now, Israel, hear the ordinances and the judgments that I teach you today to do, so that you may live and multiply and, entering in, inherit the land that the Lord God of your fathers gives you.
alternate_renderings: that ye may live, and go in and possess the land
rationale: Greek says live and multiply and, entering in, inherit. Current wording keeps that LXX sequence.

greek_phrase: εν χειρι παντων των προφητων αυτου παντος ορωντος
chosen_rendering: And the Lord testified in Israel and in Judah by the hand of all his prophets, every seer, saying, Turn from your evil ways and keep my commandments and my ordinances and all the law.
alternate_renderings: by all the prophets and by all the seers
rationale: Greek says by hand of all his prophets, every seer. Current wording keeps that LXX witness formula.

chosen_rendering: And he schemed against your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God. So do what is good in your eyes.
alternate_renderings: my lord the king is as an angel of God
rationale: Greek says like an angel of God. Current wording keeps that LXX comparison.

greek_phrase: αφ' οτε δε παρωργισαν οι πατερες ημων τον θεον του ουρανου
chosen_rendering: But from time when our fathers provoked the God of heaven, he gave them into the hand of Nabouchodonosor king of Babylon the Chaldean, and he destroyed this house and exiled the people to Babylon.
alternate_renderings: our fathers had provoked the God of heaven unto wrath
rationale: Greek says from time when our fathers provoked God of heaven. Current wording keeps that LXX cause line.

greek_phrase: εις το αμαρτανειν τω κυριω εφ' ημας υμεις λεγετε προσθειναι
chosen_rendering: And they said to them, You shall not bring captivity here to us, because you say to add upon our sins and upon our ignorance in sinning to the Lord, because our sin is great, and heat of the wrath of the Lord is upon Israel.
alternate_renderings: ye intend to add to our sins and to our trespass
rationale: Greek says add upon our sins and upon our ignorance in sinning to the Lord. Current wording keeps that LXX accusation.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be, when they saw that there was much silver in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest went up and tied and counted the silver found in the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: put up in bags and told the money
rationale: Greek says they tied and counted the silver. Current wording keeps that LXX handling line.

chosen_rendering: And it happened when he saw the earrings and the bracelets on his sister's hands, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister saying, Thus the man spoke to me, that he came to the man standing by the camels at the spring.
alternate_renderings: the earring and bracelets
rationale: Greek says earrings and bracelets. Current wording keeps that LXX plural detail.

greek_phrase: το στηθυνιον του επιθεματος και τον βραχιονα του αφαιρεματος
chosen_rendering: For I have taken the breast of the presentation and the arm of the contribution from the sons of Israel, from your sacrifices of salvation, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as an everlasting statute from the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: the wave breast and the heave shoulder
rationale: Greek says breast of the presentation and arm of the contribution. Current wording keeps those LXX cultic terms.

greek_phrase: αγαθυναι ο θεος το ονομα σαλωμων ... μεγαλυναι τον θρονον αυτου
chosen_rendering: And the servants of the king entered to bless our lord King David, saying, May God make the name of Solomon your son better than your name, and may he enlarge his throne beyond your throne. And the king bowed on his bed.
alternate_renderings: make the name ... better than thy name
rationale: Greek says make Solomon's name better and enlarge his throne. Current wording keeps that LXX blessing.

greek_phrase: περι αινεσεως ... επι της θυσιας της αινεσεως
chosen_rendering: If he brings it for praise, then on the sacrifice of praise he shall bring loaves from fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and fine flour well mixed with oil.
alternate_renderings: for a thanksgiving ... with the sacrifice of thanksgiving
rationale: Greek says for praise and sacrifice of praise. Current wording keeps that LXX repetition.

greek_phrase: εταραχθησαν ... εν τω φεισασθαι κυριον αυτου
chosen_rendering: And they were troubled, and the angels took hold of his hand and the hand of his wife and the hands of his two daughters, because the Lord spared him.
alternate_renderings: while he lingered ... the LORD being merciful unto him
rationale: Greek says they were troubled and the Lord spared him. Current wording keeps that LXX framing.

chosen_rendering: Do not listen to Ezekias, because thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me, and each man will eat of his vine and each man will eat of his fig tree and each man will drink water from his cistern,
alternate_renderings: make an agreement with me
rationale: Greek says make a blessing with me. Current wording keeps that unusual LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: Turn and set out, you, and enter into the hill-country of the Amorites and to all the neighbors of the Arabah, into mountain and plain and toward the south and the coastland, the land of the Canaanites and Lebanon, as far as the great river Euphrates.
alternate_renderings: to all the places nigh thereunto, in the plain, in the hills
rationale: Greek says to all the neighbors of the Arabah. Current wording keeps that LXX geography line.

chosen_rendering: And what was made for one day was one calf, and six choice sheep, and a goat were made for me, and every ten days wine in abundance for all. Yet with these I did not seek bread of exaction, because service was heavy upon this people.
alternate_renderings: I demanded not the bread of the governorship
rationale: Greek says bread of exaction. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: κατα τον λογον ημερας εν τη ημερα
chosen_rendering: And he established according to the ordinance of David divisions of priests according to their services, and Levites in their charges to praise and minister before priests according to each day's matter on its day, and gatekeepers in their divisions for gate and gate, because thus were commandments of David man of God.
alternate_renderings: according to the duty of every day
rationale: Greek says according to matter of day in its day and gate for gate. Current wording keeps that LXX scheduling formula while making the day-by-day phrase readable.

chosen_rendering: And they shall place upon it all the vessels with which they minister on it, the firepans and the flesh-hooks and the bowls and the cover-pan, all the vessels of the altar. And they shall spread over it a blue leather covering and put through its poles. And they shall take a purple cloth and cover the laver and its base and place them in a blue leather covering and set them upon carrying poles.
alternate_renderings: covering of badgers' skins, blue
rationale: Greek says blue leather covering. Current wording keeps that LXX material order.

greek_phrase: το ενεδρον ισραηλ επαλαιεν εκ του τοπου αυτου
chosen_rendering: And every man of Israel rose from his place and arrayed themselves at Baalthamar, and the ambush of Israel came out from its place from the west of Gabaa.
alternate_renderings: liars in wait came forth out of their places, from the meadows of Gibeah
rationale: Greek says the ambush of Israel came out from its place. Current wording keeps that LXX ambush line.

greek_phrase: οτι λαλησει ο θεος προς ανθρωπον και ζησεται
chosen_rendering: and you were saying, Behold, the Lord our God showed us his glory, and his voice we heard from the midst of the fire. On this day we saw that God will speak to a human and he shall live.
alternate_renderings: God doth talk with man, and he liveth
rationale: Greek says God will speak to a human and he shall live. Current wording keeps that LXX statement.

greek_phrase: τριακοντα χιλιαδες αρματων ... εξ εναντιας βαιθων κατα νοτου
chosen_rendering: And the foreigners gather for war against Israel, and they come up against Israel with thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and people like the sand beside the sea in multitude. And they come up and camp in Machmas, opposite Baithōn toward the south.
alternate_renderings: thirty thousand chariots ... Michmash, eastward from Bethaven
rationale: Greek says opposite Baithōn toward the south. Current wording keeps that LXX location wording.

greek_phrase: ουκ εργα εν τω πρωτοτοκω μοσχω σου
chosen_rendering: Every firstborn, whatever is born among your cattle and your sheep, the males, you shall consecrate to the Lord your God. You shall not work with your firstborn calf, nor shall you shear the firstborn of your sheep.
alternate_renderings: thou shalt do no work with the firstling of thy bullock
rationale: Greek says you shall not work with your firstborn calf. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: ανδρα ορθιον αναβαινοντα εκ της γης
chosen_rendering: And he said to her, What did you recognize? And she said to him, An upright man coming up from the earth, and he had a double cloak wrapped around him. And Saoul knew that this was Samouēl, and he bent on his face to the ground and bowed down to him.
alternate_renderings: an old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle
rationale: Greek says an upright man coming up from the earth. Current wording keeps that LXX description.

greek_phrase: ου προσθησετε αποστρεψαι τη οδω ταυτη ετι
chosen_rendering: Only he shall not multiply horses for himself, nor indeed turn the people back to Egypt so as to multiply horses for himself, because the Lord said, You shall not add to return by this road any longer.
alternate_renderings: ye shall henceforth return no more that way
rationale: Greek says you shall not add to return by this road any longer. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: μετα ταυτα ισχυσουσιν αι χειρες σου
chosen_rendering: and you will hear what they are saying, and after these things your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down into the camp. And he went down, he and Purah his servant, to the edge of the fifty in the camp.
alternate_renderings: afterward shall thine hands be strengthened
rationale: Greek says your hands will be strengthened. Current wording keeps that LXX encouragement.

greek_phrase: οι δουλοι οι οντες εχθες και τριτην ημεραν
chosen_rendering: And the slaves who were with the foreigners yesterday and the third day, who had gone up into the camp, they also turned to be with Israel, those with Saoul and Iōnathan.
alternate_renderings: the Hebrews that were with the Philistines beforetime
rationale: Greek says the slaves who were with the foreigners yesterday and the third day. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: το ορος πληρες ιππων και αρμα πυρος περικυκλω ελισαιε
chosen_rendering: And Elisaie prayed and said, Lord, open the eyes of the servant-boy and let him see. And the Lord opened his eyes, and he saw, and behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisaie.
alternate_renderings: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha
rationale: Greek says mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisaie. Current wording keeps that LXX vision.

greek_phrase: την διηγησιν του ενυπνιου και την συγκρισιν αυτου
chosen_rendering: And it came to be, when Gideon heard the recounting of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down to the Lord and returned to the camp of Israel and said, Rise up, because the Lord has given the camp of Midian into your hands.
alternate_renderings: the telling of the dream and the interpretation thereof
rationale: Greek says recounting of the dream and its interpretation. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

chosen_rendering: And you camp outside the camp seven days, every one who killed and every one touching the wounded. He shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
alternate_renderings: whosoever hath killed any person, and whosoever hath touched any slain
rationale: Greek says everyone touching the wounded. Current wording keeps that LXX term.

greek_phrase: ου πεφθησεται εζυμωμενη μεριδα αυτην εδωκα αυτοις
chosen_rendering: It shall not be baked leavened. I have given it to them as a portion from the Lord's offerings. It is holy of holies, like that for sin and like that for trespass.
alternate_renderings: it shall not be baken with leaven. I have given it unto them for their portion
rationale: Greek says not be baked leavened and portion from the Lord's offerings. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: και παρα κυριου θεου ημων ευοδωθη
chosen_rendering: And Dauid said to all the assembly of Israel, If this seems good to you, and if it has been prospered from the Lord our God, let us send to our brothers left behind in all the land of Israel, and with them to priests and Levites in the cities of their possession, and let them gather to us.
alternate_renderings: if it be of the LORD our God
rationale: Greek says if it has been prospered from the Lord our God. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: χορευσαι εν χοροις ... αρπασετε ανηρ εαυτω γυναικα
chosen_rendering: And you shall watch, and behold, when the daughters of those dwelling in Shiloh come out in Shiloh to dance in dances, then you shall come out from the vineyards and each man seize for himself a wife from the daughters of Shiloh and go away to the land of Benjamin.
alternate_renderings: to dance in dances ... catch you every man his wife
rationale: Greek says dance in dances and each man seize for himself a wife. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And all the assembly rejoiced, priests and Levites and all the assembly from Iouda and those found from Israel and sojourners who came from the land of Israel and those dwelling in Iouda.
alternate_renderings: all the congregation that came out of Israel
rationale: Greek says those found from Israel. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: And the men of Israel turned in the battle, and Benjamin had begun striking down wounded men in Israel, about thirty men, because they said, Surely by defeat they are defeated before us as in the former battle.
alternate_renderings: surely they are smitten down before us
rationale: Greek says surely by defeat they are defeated before us. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: εως ου διεπεσεν πασα γενεα ανδρων πολεμιστων
chosen_rendering: And the days that we traveled from Kadesh-Barnea until we passed through the Ravine of Zaret were thirty-eight years, until all the generation of fighting men fell away, dying from the camp, just as God swore to them.
alternate_renderings: until all the generation of the men of war were consumed
rationale: Greek says until all the generation of fighting men fell away, dying from the camp. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: and they took it and its king and its villages and struck it with the edge of the sword and utterly destroyed it and every breathing thing in it, and they did not leave in it any saved one, in the way they did to Hebron and its king, so they did to Dabir and its king.
alternate_renderings: they left none remaining
rationale: Greek says they did not leave in it any saved one. Current wording keeps that LXX result.

greek_phrase: εποιησεν παντας τους ευρεθεντας ... του δουλευειν κυριω θεω αυτων
chosen_rendering: And Iōsias removed all abominations from all the land that belonged to the sons of Israel and made all found in Ierousalem and in Israel serve the Lord their God. All his days they did not turn away from behind the Lord God of their fathers.
alternate_renderings: caused all that were present in Israel to serve
rationale: Greek says made all found in Jerusalem and in Israel serve. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: επι τον ημμενον του οστεου του ανθρωπινου η του τραυματιου
chosen_rendering: And a clean man shall take hyssop and dip it into the water and sprinkle it upon the house and upon the vessels and upon the persons who are there, and upon the one who touched the bone, the human body, or the slain one, or the dead one, or the grave.
alternate_renderings: upon him that touched a bone, or one slain, or one dead
rationale: Greek says touched the bone, the human body, or the slain one. Current wording keeps that LXX list.

greek_phrase: ος αν ενδειχθη κατακαυθησεται εν πυρι
chosen_rendering: And whoever is pointed out shall be burned with fire, he and everything that belongs to him, because he transgressed the covenant of the Lord and did lawless deed in Israel.
alternate_renderings: he that is taken shall be burnt with fire
rationale: Greek says whoever is pointed out shall be burned with fire. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: επιστησω το προσωπον μου επι την ψυχην
chosen_rendering: And any man of the sons of Israel or of the newcomers dwelling among you who eats any blood, I will set my face against the person who eats the blood and will destroy him from his people.
alternate_renderings: I will even set my face against that soul
rationale: Greek says I will set my face against the person who eats the blood. Current wording keeps that LXX judgment line.

greek_phrase: κατεβησαν οι αδελφοι αυτου και πας ο οικος του πατρος αυτου
chosen_rendering: And his brothers and all the house of his father went down and took him and went up and buried him between Zorah and between Esthaol in the tomb of Manōe his father. And he judged Israel twenty years.
alternate_renderings: his brethren and all the house of his father came down
rationale: Greek says his brothers and all the house of his father went down and took him. Current wording keeps that LXX burial line.

greek_phrase: ινα τι ευρεν ημας παντα τα κακα ταυτα
chosen_rendering: And Gideon said to him, In me, my lord? And if the Lord is with us, why have all these evils found us, and where are all his wonders that our fathers recounted to us, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up out of Egypt? But now he has cast us off and given us into the hand of Midian.
alternate_renderings: why then is all this befallen us
rationale: Greek says why have all these evils found us. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

greek_phrase: ει εστιν μοι εγκρυφιας αλλ' η οσον δραξ αλευρου
chosen_rendering: And the woman said, As the Lord your God lives, I have no cake except as much as a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug, and behold, I am gathering two little sticks and will go in and make it for myself and my children, and we will eat and die.
alternate_renderings: I have not a cake, but an handful of meal
rationale: Greek says no cake except as much as a handful of flour. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: μη ανθρωπος το ξυλον το εν τω αγρω εισελθειν απο προσωπου σου εις τον χαρακα
chosen_rendering: And if you besiege a city many days to fight against it for its capture, you shall not utterly destroy its trees by putting iron to them. Rather, you may eat from it, but you shall not cut it down, because the tree in the field is not a human to enter before your face into siegeworks.
alternate_renderings: for the tree of the field is man's life to employ them in the siege
rationale: Greek says the tree in the field is not a human to enter before your face into siegeworks. Current wording keeps that difficult LXX sentence.

chosen_rendering: And I prayed to God and said, Lord, Lord, King of the gods, do not utterly destroy your people and your portion, whom you redeemed in your great strength, whom you brought out from the land of Egypt in your great strength and with your mighty hand and high arm.
alternate_renderings: Lord GOD ... king of gods
rationale: Greek says King of the gods here. Current wording keeps that LXX title.

greek_phrase: επλεονασαν οι υιοι ισραηλ απαρχην σιτου και οινου
chosen_rendering: And as word was commanded, sons of Israel increased firstfruits of grain and wine and oil and honey and every produce of field, and tithes of all things they brought in abundance.
alternate_renderings: brought in abundance the firstfruits

chosen_rendering: And Dauid sacrificed sacrifices to the Lord and offered whole burnt offerings to God on next day after first day: one thousand calves, one thousand rams, one thousand lambs, and their libations, and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel.
alternate_renderings: sacrifices in abundance for all Israel
rationale: Greek says sacrifices in abundance for all Israel. Current wording keeps that LXX closing phrase.

greek_phrase: ου κατατενει αυτον εν τοις μοχθοις
chosen_rendering: And you shall distribute them to your children after you, and they shall be for you as permanent holdings forever. But among your brothers, the sons of Israel, no one shall stretch his brother hard in toils.
alternate_renderings: ye shall not rule one over another with rigour
rationale: Greek says no one shall cut down his brother in toils. Current wording keeps the harder LXX image by sense.

greek_phrase: ετοιμως το κριμα εσται γιγνομενον εξ αυτου
chosen_rendering: And everyone who is not doing the law of your God and the law of the king, judgment shall promptly be carried out from him, whether to death or to discipline or to confiscation of substance or to bonds.
alternate_renderings: let judgment be executed speedily upon him
rationale: Greek says judgment shall promptly be carried out from him. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: πεσειται αυτοματα τα τειχη της πολεως
chosen_rendering: And it shall be, when you sound with the trumpet, let all the people cry out together, and when they cry out the walls of the city will fall of themselves, and all the people shall enter, each one rushing straight ahead into the city.
alternate_renderings: the wall of the city shall fall down flat
rationale: Greek says walls of the city will fall of themselves. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: παρασιωπηση αυτη και μη ανανευση αυτη
chosen_rendering: and her husband hears and keeps silent to her and does not refuse her, then all her vows shall stand, and all her bindings which she bound against her life shall stand against her.
alternate_renderings: hold his peace at her
rationale: Greek says keeps silent to her and does not refuse her. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

greek_phrase: ουχ οὑτως κοιμηθητω μετα σου την νυκτα ταυτην
chosen_rendering: And Leah said, Is it not enough for you that you took my husband? Will you now take my son's mandrakes too? And Rachel said, Not so. Let him sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son's mandrakes.
alternate_renderings: therefore he shall lie with thee to night
rationale: Greek says not so; let him sleep with you tonight. Current wording keeps that LXX exchange.

greek_phrase: το στηθυνιον του αφορισματος και τον βραχιονα του αφαιρεματος
chosen_rendering: And you shall eat the breast of separation and the arm of contribution in a holy place, you and your sons and your house with you, because it has been given as a statute for you and a statute for your sons from the sacrifices of salvation of the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: wave breast and heave shoulder
rationale: Greek says breast of separation and arm of contribution. Current wording keeps those LXX cultic terms.

greek_phrase: μη βρωσει εφαγαμεν εκ του βασιλεως
chosen_rendering: And every man of Iouda answered the man of Israel, and they said, Because the king is near to me. And why have you been angered about this matter? Did we eat by eating from the king, or did he give us a gift, or did he lift something for us?
alternate_renderings: have we eaten at all of the king's cost
rationale: Greek says did we eat by eating from the king. Current wording keeps that LXX repetition.

chosen_rendering: But in the seventh you shall make a release and let it rest, and the poor of your nation shall eat, and what they leave the wild beasts shall eat. So you shall do with your vineyard and your oliveyard.
alternate_renderings: let it rest and lie still
rationale: Greek says make a release and let it rest. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

chosen_rendering: And I chose the house of your father from all the scepters of Israel for myself, to serve as priest and to go up upon my altar and to burn incense and to lift the ephod, and I gave to the house of your father all the fire-offerings of the sons of Israel for food.
alternate_renderings: out of all the tribes of Israel
rationale: Greek says from all the scepters of Israel. Current wording keeps that LXX image.

chosen_rendering: And you testified to them to turn them back to your law, but they did not hear. Instead, in your commandments and in your judgments they sinned, which if a man does he will live in them. And they gave a stubborn back and hardened their neck and did not hear.
alternate_renderings: withdrew the shoulder
rationale: Greek says they gave a disobedient or stubborn back. Current wording keeps that LXX image.

chosen_rendering: I saw in the spoil a fine variegated cloak and two hundred silver didrachmas and one golden tongue of fifty didrachmas, and desiring them I took them. And behold, they are hidden in the ground in my tent, and the silver is hidden underneath them.
alternate_renderings: a wedge of gold
rationale: Greek says one golden tongue of fifty didrachmas. Current wording keeps that LXX shape-word.

chosen_rendering: Because you transgressed my word in the wilderness of Sin when the congregation fell against me. To sanctify me, you did not sanctify me over the water before them. This is the water of reviling at Kadesh in the wilderness of Sin.
alternate_renderings: water of Meribah
rationale: Greek says water of contradiction or reviling. Current wording keeps that LXX title by sense.

greek_phrase: οὐχί αλλ' εν τη πλατεια καταλυσομεν
chosen_rendering: And he said, Look, lords, turn aside into the house of your servant and lodge and wash your feet, and rising early you shall go on your way. And they said, No, but we will lodge in the square.
alternate_renderings: nay; but we will abide in the street
rationale: Greek says we will lodge in the square. Current wording keeps that LXX city-space term.

greek_phrase: ουκ εποιησαν απο ημερων ιησου υιου ναυη ουτως
chosen_rendering: And all the assembly, those returned from captivity, made booths and sat in booths, for the sons of Israel had not done thus from the days of Iesous son of Naue until that day. And there was very great rejoicing.
alternate_renderings: the children of Israel had not done so
rationale: Greek says had not done thus from days of Joshua son of Nun. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: προβατον φαιον ... παν διαλευκον και ραντον
chosen_rendering: Let all your sheep pass by today, and separate from there every gray sheep among the lambs and every white-marked and speckled one among the goats. This shall be my wages.
alternate_renderings: every speckled and spotted cattle
rationale: Greek says every gray sheep among the lambs and every white-marked and speckled one among the goats. Current wording keeps those LXX color terms.

chosen_rendering: And Achaz removed vessels of the house of the Lord and cut them up and shut doors of the house of the Lord and made for himself altars in every corner in Ierousalem.
alternate_renderings: cut in pieces the vessels
rationale: Greek says he cut them up. Current wording keeps that LXX verb.

chosen_rendering: Your houses will be filled, and the houses of your servants, and all the houses in all the land of the Egyptians, with things your fathers never saw, nor their forefathers, from the day they came to be on the earth until this day. Then Moses turned away and went out from Pharaoh.
alternate_renderings: he turned himself, and went out from Pharaoh
rationale: Greek says Moses turned aside and went out from Pharaoh. Current wording keeps that LXX exit line.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be in those days, the foreigners gathered in their camps to go out to fight against Israel. And Anchous said to David, In knowing you will know that you and your men will go out with me into battle.
alternate_renderings: Know thou assuredly
rationale: Greek says in knowing you will know. Current wording keeps that LXX emphasis.

chosen_rendering: If famine happens, if death happens, if blight happens, mildew, locust, rust, if his enemy afflicts him in one of his cities, every encounter, every pain,
alternate_renderings: whatsoever plague, whatsoever sickness there be
rationale: Greek says every encounter, every pain. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

greek_phrase: μη εχθραινετε αυτοις και μη συναψητε αυτοις εις πολεμον
chosen_rendering: And you will come near to the sons of Ammon. Do not treat them as enemies and do not join them in war, for I shall certainly not give you from the land of the sons of Ammon as an inheritance, because I have given it to the sons of Lot as an inheritance.
alternate_renderings: distress them not, nor meddle with them
rationale: Greek says do not treat them as enemies and do not join them in war. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

chosen_rendering: And behold, in my poverty I prepared for the house of the Lord one hundred thousand talents of gold and one thousand thousand talents of silver, and bronze and iron without weight, because it is in abundance, and wood and stones I prepared, and to these add more.
alternate_renderings: in my trouble I have prepared
rationale: Greek says in my poverty I prepared. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

chosen_rendering: And a wind went out from the Lord and swept quail from the sea and threw them over the camp, a day's journey this way and a day's journey that way, around the camp, about two cubits above the ground.
alternate_renderings: brought quails from the sea
rationale: Greek says swept quail from the sea and threw them over the camp. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: μη δοξαζων δαυιδ τον πατερα σου εναντιον σου
chosen_rendering: And the rulers of Ammon said to Anan, Does Dauid honor your father before you because he sent comforters to you? Did not his servants come to you to search city and spy out land?
alternate_renderings: thinkest thou that David doth honour thy father
rationale: Greek says does David honor your father before you. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: You shall not eat any carcass. It shall be given to the resident alien in your cities, and he shall eat it, or you may sell it to the foreigner, because you are a holy people to the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother's milk.
alternate_renderings: ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself
rationale: Greek says any dying thing or carcass. Current wording keeps that LXX term by sense.

greek_phrase: ου μη αμαρτητε τω κυριω του εσθιειν συν τω αιματι
chosen_rendering: And Saoul said, Scatter among the people and tell them to bring here, each his calf and each his sheep, and let him slaughter on this and not sin against the Lord by eating with the blood. And all the people brought near, each the thing in his hand, and they slaughtered there.
alternate_renderings: sin against the LORD in eating with the blood
rationale: Greek says by eating with the blood. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: And the king said to the runners standing over him, Bring forward and kill the priests of the Lord, because their hand is with David, and because they knew that he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear. And the servants of the king were not willing to bring their hands upon the priests of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: did not shew it to me
rationale: Greek says did not uncover my ear. Current wording keeps that LXX idiom.

greek_phrase: οχλος εν σημασια μετ' ευφροσυνης του υψωσαι ωδην
chosen_rendering: And many from the priests and the Levites and leaders of father-houses, the elders who had seen the first house on its foundation, were weeping with a loud voice when this house was before their eyes, while the crowd with shouting in joy was raising song.
alternate_renderings: many shouted aloud for joy
rationale: Greek says the crowd with a signal-shout in joy was lifting up song. Current wording keeps that LXX picture by sense.

greek_phrase: κατεστησαν αυτην εξω της παρεμβολης ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: And the two young men who had spied the city entered into the house of the woman and brought out Rahab the prostitute and her father and her mother and her brothers and everything that belonged to her and all her kindred, and they stationed her outside the camp of Israel.
alternate_renderings: left them without the camp of Israel
rationale: Greek says they stationed her outside the camp of Israel. Current wording keeps that LXX verb.

greek_phrase: και ειδεν συρος οτι ετροπωσατο αυτον ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: And Syria saw that Israel routed him, and they sent messengers and brought out Syrians from beyond river, with Sophach commander of force of Hadarezer before them.
alternate_renderings: when the Syrians saw that they were put to the worse before Israel
rationale: Greek says Syria saw that Israel routed him. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: ηπειθησατε τω ρηματι μου ... επι του υδατος αντιλογιας
chosen_rendering: because you disobeyed my word among the sons of Israel at the water of contradiction, Kadesh, in the wilderness of Sin, because you did not sanctify me among the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: ye trespassed against me ... at the waters of Meribah-Kadesh
rationale: Greek says you disobeyed my word at the water of contradiction. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

chosen_rendering: And it shall be, when the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth come to rest in the water of the Jordan, the water of the Jordan will fail, and the water coming down will stand.
alternate_renderings: the waters of Jordan shall be cut off
rationale: Greek says the water of the Jordan will fail, and the water coming down will stand. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

chosen_rendering: And I said to them, You see the evil in which we are, how Ierousalem lies waste and its gates were given to fire. Come, let us rebuild wall of Ierousalem, and we will no longer be a reproach.
alternate_renderings: the gates thereof are burned with fire
rationale: Greek says its gates were given to fire. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: For I will bring them into the good land that I swore to their fathers to give to them, a land flowing with milk and honey, and they shall eat and be filled and be satisfied, and they shall turn to foreign gods and serve them and provoke me and scatter my covenant.
alternate_renderings: break my covenant
rationale: Greek says they will scatter my covenant. Current wording keeps that LXX image.

chosen_rendering: And their boundaries came to be from the north from the Jordan, and the boundary shall go up along the shoulder of Jericho on the north and shall go up to the mountain westward, and its outlet shall be the wilderness of Baithon.
alternate_renderings: the goings out thereof were at the wilderness of Beth-aven
rationale: Greek says its outlet shall be the Madbaritis of Baithon, the wilderness of Baithon. Current wording keeps that LXX place line.

chosen_rendering: If a person is overtaken by forgetfulness and sins unintentionally in the holy things of the Lord, then he shall bring for his trespass to the Lord a ram without blemish from the sheep, valued in silver shekels by the sanctuary shekel, for the thing in which he trespassed.
alternate_renderings: if a soul commit a trespass, and sin through ignorance
rationale: Greek says if forgetfulness overtakes a person and he sins unintentionally. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: and bent mercy toward me before the king and his counselors and all the exalted rulers of the king. And I was strengthened, as the good hand of God was upon me, and I gathered leaders from Israel to go up with me.
alternate_renderings: hath extended mercy unto me
rationale: Greek says bent mercy toward me. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be on the seventh day, the little boy died, and the servants of David feared to report to him that the little boy had died, because they said, Behold, while the little boy was still living we spoke to him, and he did not listen to our voice, and how shall we say to him that the little boy has died? He will do evil.
alternate_renderings: he will vex himself
rationale: Greek says he will do evils or do harm. Current wording keeps that LXX fear line.

chosen_rendering: And I shook out my fold and said, Thus may God shake out every man who does not fulfill this word, from his house and from his labor, and thus may he be shaken out and empty. And all the assembly said, Amen, and they praised the Lord, and the people did this word.
alternate_renderings: I shook my lap
rationale: Greek says I shook out my fold. Current wording keeps that LXX garment image.

greek_phrase: και λαβων μωυσης την σκηνην αυτου επηξεν
chosen_rendering: And Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and it was called Tent of Testimony. And everyone seeking the Lord went out to the tent outside the camp.
alternate_renderings: Moses took the tabernacle, and pitched it without the camp
rationale: Greek says Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: ουκ ευλογησεις αυτον ... ουκ αποκριθηση αυτω
chosen_rendering: And Elisaie said to Giezi, Gird your waist and take my staff in your hand and go, because if you meet a man you shall not bless him, and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him, and you shall put my staff on the face of the boy.
alternate_renderings: if thou meet any man, salute him not
rationale: Greek says you shall not bless him, and if a man blesses you, you shall not answer him. Current wording keeps that LXX exchange.

greek_phrase: ενεκρουσεν τον πασσαλον εν τη γναθω αυτου
chosen_rendering: And Jaēl wife of Chaber took the tent peg and put the hammer in her hand and came in to him quietly and drove the peg into his jaw and it went through into the ground. And he writhed between her knees and breathed out and died.
alternate_renderings: smote the nail into his temples
rationale: Greek says drove the peg into his jaw. Current wording keeps that LXX body-part wording.

greek_phrase: διειλαντο την προνομην των εχθρων μετα των αδελφων αυτων
chosen_rendering: and they went away to their houses with much wealth and very much livestock and silver and gold and iron and much clothing, and they divided the plunder of their enemies with their brothers.
alternate_renderings: divide the spoil of your enemies with your brethren
rationale: Greek says they divided the plunder of their enemies with their brothers. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: και οι στυλοι τεσσαρακοντα και οκτω
chosen_rendering: and the pots and the shovels and the bowls and all the vessels that Chiram made for King Solomon for the house of the Lord, and the forty-eight pillars of the house of the king and of the house of the Lord, all the works of the king that Chiram made, all entirely of bronze.
alternate_renderings: and the pots, and the shovels, and the basons
rationale: Current source row carries the longer vessel-summary line here, including forty-eight pillars. Kept as mapped pending wider verse-map audit.

greek_phrase: ος ηρχιτεκτονησεν τα υφαντα και τα ραφιδευτα
chosen_rendering: And Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, was there, chief craftsman in woven works and embroidery and variegated weaving with scarlet and fine linen.
alternate_renderings: an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer
rationale: Greek says he was chief craftsman in woven works and embroidery. Current wording keeps that LXX craft line.

chosen_rendering: If famine comes on the land, if death comes, if blight and jaundice come, locust and caterpillar, if enemy afflicts them before their cities, according to every plague and every pain,
alternate_renderings: blasting, and mildew
rationale: Greek says blight and jaundice. Current wording keeps that LXX list.

chosen_rendering: And they were bringing up and bringing out from Egypt chariot for six hundred silver and horse for one hundred fifty, and thus for all kings of Chettites and kings of Syria they brought by their hands.
alternate_renderings: so brought they out horses
rationale: Greek says they brought by their hands. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be after these things, David inquired of the Lord, saying, Shall I go up into one of the cities of Iouda? And the Lord said to him, Go up. And David said, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Chebrōn.
alternate_renderings: David enquired of the LORD
rationale: Greek says David inquired in the Lord. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: στηρισον την καρδιαν σου κλασματι αρτου
chosen_rendering: And it came to be on the fourth day, they rose early in the morning, and he arose to depart, and the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, Strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread, and after this you may go.
alternate_renderings: comfort thine heart with a morsel of bread
rationale: Greek says strengthen your heart with a morsel of bread. Current wording keeps that LXX idiom.

chosen_rendering: And you came to this place, and Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us in war, and we struck them,
alternate_renderings: came out against us unto battle
rationale: Greek says came out to meeting with us in war. Current wording keeps that LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: και ουκ ηδυνηθη επιστρεψαι αυτην προς εαυτον
chosen_rendering: And it came to be when King Ieroboam heard the words of the man of God, the one who cried against the altar in Baithēl, the king stretched out his hand from the altar, saying, Seize him. And behold, his hand that he stretched out against him dried up, and he could not turn it back to himself.
alternate_renderings: his hand ... dried up, so that he could not pull it in again to him
rationale: Greek says he could not turn it back to himself. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: επι παντος ου εαν επιθυμη η ψυχη σου
chosen_rendering: and you shall give the silver for everything your soul desires, for cattle or for sheep, for wine or for strong drink or for anything your soul desires, and you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and your household.
alternate_renderings: for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after
rationale: Greek says for everything your soul desires. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: And the Lord turned the blood of his injustice onto his head, because he met two men more righteous and better than he and killed them by the sword, and my father David did not know their blood: Abenner son of Ner, commander of Israel, and Amessa son of Iether, commander of Iouda.
alternate_renderings: because he fell upon two men more righteous
rationale: Greek says because he met two men more righteous and better than he and killed them. Current wording keeps that LXX sentence.

chosen_rendering: And Amessai did not guard against the sword in the hand of Ioab, and Ioab struck him with it in the belly, and his entrails poured out on the ground, and he did not strike him a second time, and he died. And Ioab and Abessa his brother pursued after Sheba son of Bochori.
alternate_renderings: smote him therewith in the fifth rib
rationale: Greek says struck him in the psoa or flank-belly area. Current wording keeps that LXX body term by sense.

chosen_rendering: And she said, Let the king now remember the Lord his God, that the avenger of blood not multiply to destroy, and they certainly will not remove my son. And he said, As the Lord lives, if a hair of your son falls to the ground.
alternate_renderings: that the revengers of blood destroy no more
rationale: Greek says that the avenger of blood not multiply to destroy. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: For Chebrōnite, Ioudias was chief of Chebrōnite by their generations, by fathers. In fortieth year of his reign they were sought out, and mighty man was found among them in Iazēr of Gilead.
alternate_renderings: there were found among them mighty men of valour
rationale: Greek says they were sought out, and a mighty man was found among them. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And the house that was before Jerusalem, to the right of the mount of Mosoath, which Salōmōn king of Israel built to Astartē, abomination of the Sidonians, and to Chamōs, abomination of Moab, and to Molochol, abomination of the sons of Ammon, the king defiled.
alternate_renderings: for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Zidonians
rationale: Greek uses terms of abhorrence or offense here. Current wording keeps those LXX cultic labels.

chosen_rendering: And Moses said to Aaron, Come near to the altar and make your sin-offering and your whole burnt offering and make atonement for yourself and for your house, and make the gifts of the people and make atonement for them, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
alternate_renderings: offer the offering of the people
rationale: Greek says make the gifts of the people. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: ερριψαν τον νομον σου οπισω σωματος αυτων
chosen_rendering: And they changed and turned away from you and cast your law behind their body, and your prophets they killed, the ones who testified among them to turn them back to you, and they committed great provocations.
alternate_renderings: cast thy law behind their backs
rationale: Greek says they cast your law behind their body. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: This was the counting of the clan of Kohath, every one ministering in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron counted by the word of the Lord by Moses' hand.
alternate_renderings: this was the sum of the families of the Kohathites
rationale: Greek says this was the numbering or inspection of the people of Kohath. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: ποιησεις επ' εμε ελεημοσυνην και αληθειαν
chosen_rendering: And the days of Israel drew near for him to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him, If I have found favor before you, put your hand under my thigh, and you will do mercy and truth toward me so as not to bury me in Egypt,
alternate_renderings: deal kindly and truly with me
rationale: Greek says you will do mercy and truth toward me. Current wording keeps that LXX pair.

greek_phrase: ου διεπεσεν εις λογος ... ου διεφωνησεν εξ αυτων
chosen_rendering: And behold, I am departing on the way, just as all on the earth, and you shall know in your heart and in your soul that not one word has failed from all the words that the Lord your God spoke concerning all that belongs to you; none of them has fallen away.
alternate_renderings: not one thing hath failed ... not one thing hath failed thereof
rationale: Greek says not one word has fallen and none of them has disagreed or fallen away. Current wording keeps that LXX force.

greek_phrase: το χοριον αυτης το εξελθον δια των μηρων αυτης
chosen_rendering: and her afterbirth that came out through her thighs and the child that she bears, for she shall eat them because of the lack of everything, secretly, in your distress and in the affliction with which your enemy afflicts you in all your cities.
alternate_renderings: her young one that cometh out from between her feet
rationale: Greek says her chorion, the afterbirth that came out through her thighs. Current wording keeps that LXX detail.

chosen_rendering: For Salomon made bronze platform and set it in the midst of court of sanctuary, its length five cubits and breadth five cubits and height three cubits, and he stood upon it and fell on his knees before all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven.
alternate_renderings: Solomon had made a brazen scaffold
rationale: Greek says Solomon made a bronze base or platform. Current wording keeps that LXX term.

greek_phrase: εν τω ετει τω τριτω το δευτερον επιδεκατον
chosen_rendering: And if you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the second tithe, you shall give it to the Levite and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow, and they shall eat in your cities and be filled.
alternate_renderings: which is the year of tithing
rationale: Greek says in the third year, the second tithe. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: Rise, sanctify the people and tell them to sanctify themselves for tomorrow. These things says the Lord God of Israel: The devoted thing is among you. You will not be able to stand before your enemies until you remove the devoted thing from among you.
alternate_renderings: there is an accursed thing in the midst of thee
rationale: Greek says the devoted thing is among you. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: παραρριψον με επι μιαν των ιερατειων σου
chosen_rendering: And it shall be that the one left over in your house will come to bow down to him for an obol of silver, saying, Cast me beside one of your priesthoods that I may eat bread.
alternate_renderings: put me, I pray thee, into one of the priests' offices
rationale: Greek says cast me beside one of your priesthoods. Current wording keeps that LXX plea.

chosen_rendering: And Samouēl said to Iessai, Have the young men failed? And he said, There is still the small one; behold, he is shepherding among the flock. And Samouēl said to Iessai, Send and take him, because we certainly will not recline until he comes here.
alternate_renderings: Are here all thy children
rationale: Greek says have the young men failed or come to an end. Current wording keeps that LXX question.

greek_phrase: ουκ εστιν ημιν σωτηρια απο προσωπου αβεσσαλωμ
chosen_rendering: And David said to all his servants with him in Ierousalēm, Rise, and let us flee, because there is no salvation for us from before Abessalōm. Hurry to go, lest he hurry and overtake us and drive evil upon us and strike the city with the mouth of the sword.
alternate_renderings: we shall not else escape from Absalom
rationale: Greek says there is no salvation for us from before Absalom. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: He raises the poor from the earth and lifts the needy from the dung heap, to seat him with the rulers of peoples and to allot to them a throne of glory.
alternate_renderings: to make them inherit the throne of glory
rationale: Greek says to allot to them a throne of glory. Current wording keeps that LXX inheritance image.

greek_phrase: μη εκλιποι εκ του οικου ιωαβ γονορρυης ... ελασσουμενος αρτοις
chosen_rendering: Let them come down on the head of Iōab and on all the house of his father, and let there not fail from the house of Iōab one with discharge and leper and one holding a staff and one falling by the sword and one lacking breads.
alternate_renderings: let there not fail ... one that hath an issue ... that lacketh bread
rationale: Greek says lacking breads. Current wording keeps that harsh LXX curse list.

greek_phrase: η γενεσθαι τρεις ημερας θανατον εν τη γη σου
chosen_rendering: And Gad came to David and reported to him and said to him, Choose for yourself whether three years of famine shall come to you in your land, or three months of your fleeing before your enemies while they pursue you, or three days of death to be in your land. Now then know and see what word I should answer the one who sent me.
alternate_renderings: three days' pestilence in thy land
rationale: Greek says three days of death to be in your land. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: και αυτοι εγενοντο αυτω εις σκωλον
chosen_rendering: I will seek gods of Damascus who strike me. And he said, Because gods of the king of Syria strengthened them, therefore I will sacrifice to them and they will help me. But they became to him as a stumbling-block and to all Israel.
alternate_renderings: they were the ruin of him
rationale: Greek says they became to him as a skandalon-like stumbling block. Current wording keeps that LXX image.

greek_phrase: ιλεως γενου επι τη κακια του λαου σου
chosen_rendering: Let not the Egyptians ever say, He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and consume them from the earth. Stop from the anger of your wrath and be merciful concerning the evil of your people.
alternate_renderings: repent of this evil against thy people
rationale: Greek says be merciful concerning the evil of your people. Current wording keeps that LXX plea.

greek_phrase: τους αρχοντας των εφημεριων των περι το σωμα του βασιλεως
chosen_rendering: And Dauid assembled all rulers of Israel, rulers of judges and rulers of courses around body of the king and rulers of thousands and of hundreds and treasurers and those over his possessions and mighty lords and fighters of army, in Ierousalem.
alternate_renderings: captains of the companies that ministered to the king by course
rationale: Greek says rulers of the courses around the body of the king. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be when their heart grew good, they said, Call Sampsōn out of the prison house and let him play before us. And they called Sampsōn out of the prison house, and they mocked him, and they set him between the two pillars.
alternate_renderings: when their hearts were merry
rationale: Greek says when their heart grew good. Current wording keeps that LXX idiom.

chosen_rendering: And it came to be because the sons of Israel sinned against the Lord their God who brought them up from the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
alternate_renderings: brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh
rationale: Greek says from under the hand of Pharaoh. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

chosen_rendering: And the men were not willing to listen to him, and the man took hold of his concubine and brought her out to them outside, and they knew her and abused her all night until morning and sent her away when dawn was rising.
alternate_renderings: abused her all the night
rationale: Greek says they mocked or abused her all night. Current wording keeps that LXX line by sense.

chosen_rendering: And the servants of Abessalom came to the woman at the house and said, Where are Achimaas and Ionathan? And the woman said to them, They passed a little beyond the water. And they searched and did not find them and returned to Ierousalem.
alternate_renderings: they be gone over the brook of water
rationale: Greek says they passed a little beyond the water. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: επι τον λοβον του ωτος ... επι το ακρον της χειρος ... επι το ακρον του ποδος
chosen_rendering: And you shall slaughter it and take some of its blood and place it on the tip of Aaron's right ear and on the thumb of his right hand and on the great toe of his right foot, and on the right earlobes of his sons and on the thumbs of their right hands and on the great toes of their right feet.
alternate_renderings: put it upon the tip of the right ear ... thumb ... great toe
rationale: Greek says on the lobe of the ear and on the extremity of hand and foot. Current wording keeps that LXX body-part wording.

chosen_rendering: And Roboam came to Ierousalem and assembled Iouda and Beniamin, one hundred eighty thousand young men making war, and he fought against Israel to return kingdom to Roboam.
alternate_renderings: chosen men, which were warriors
rationale: Greek says young men making war. Current wording keeps that LXX military phrase.

chosen_rendering: Thus you will say to Joseph, Forgive them their injustice and their sin, because they showed evil to you. And now accept the injustice of the servants of the God of your father. And Joseph wept while they spoke to him.
alternate_renderings: forgive ... the trespass of the servants
rationale: Greek says accept the injustice of the servants of the God of your father. Current wording keeps that LXX plea.

greek_phrase: πληρωσαι τας χειρας εν μοσχω εκ βοων και κριοις επτα
chosen_rendering: Did you not cast out priests of the Lord, sons of Aaron, and Levites, and make for yourselves priests from the people of the land? Everyone coming to fill hands with young bull from cattle and seven rams became priest to what was not god.
alternate_renderings: to consecrate himself with a young bullock and seven rams
rationale: Greek says to fill the hands with a young bull and seven rams. Current wording keeps that LXX ordination idiom.

greek_phrase: εκκλασει αυτο εκ των πτερυγων και ου διελει
chosen_rendering: And he shall split it open by the wings and shall not divide it, and the priest shall place it on the altar, on the wood on the fire. It is an offering, a sacrifice, an aroma of sweet fragrance to the Lord.
alternate_renderings: cleave it with the wings thereof, but shall not divide it asunder
rationale: Greek says split it open by the wings and not divide it. Current wording keeps that LXX instruction.

greek_phrase: ποιησεις την λατρειαν ταυτην εν τω μηνι τουτω
chosen_rendering: And it shall be that when the Lord your God brings you into the land of the Canaanites and Hittites and Hivites and Girgashites and Amorites and Perizzites and Jebusites, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall perform this service in this month.
alternate_renderings: keep this service in this month
rationale: Greek says perform this service in this month. Current wording keeps that LXX cultic term.

greek_phrase: εαν ακοη εισακουσητε της φωνης κυριου
chosen_rendering: And it shall be, when you cross the Jordan into the land that the Lord your God gives you, if indeed you listen to the voice of the Lord your God, keeping and doing all his commands that I command you today, then the Lord your God will set you above all the nations of the earth.
alternate_renderings: if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice
rationale: Greek says if in hearing you hear the voice of the Lord your God. Current wording keeps that LXX emphasis.

greek_phrase: τρεις ημερας ρομφαιαν κυριου και θανατον εν τη γη
chosen_rendering: either three years of famine, or three months for you to flee from before your enemies while sword of your enemies destroys, or three days sword of the Lord and death in the land, and angel of the Lord destroying in all inheritance of Israel. And now see what word I should answer to one who sent me.
alternate_renderings: three days the sword of the LORD, even the pestilence
rationale: Greek says three days sword of the Lord and death in the land. Current wording keeps that LXX pairing.

chosen_rendering: The Lord who delivered me from the hand of the lion and from the hand of the bear, he will deliver me from the hand of this uncircumcised foreigner. And Saoul said to David, Go, and the Lord will be with you.
alternate_renderings: this uncircumcised Philistine
rationale: Greek says this uncircumcised foreigner. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

greek_phrase: εγκειται η διανοια του ανθρωπου επιμελως επι τα πονηρα
chosen_rendering: And the Lord God smelled an aroma of sweet fragrance, and the Lord God said, having considered, Let me not continue any longer to curse the earth because of the works of humans, because the mind of the human lies carefully upon evil things from his youth.
