alternate_renderings: the imagination of man's heart is evil from his youth
rationale: Greek says the human mind lies carefully upon evil things from youth. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: προσθειη κυριος επι τον λαον αυτου ως αυτοι εκατονταπλασιως
chosen_rendering: And Ioab said, May the Lord add to his people a hundredfold as they are, and are not eyes of my lord the king seeing that all are servants to my lord? Why does my lord seek this, so that it should not become sin for Israel?
alternate_renderings: the LORD make his people an hundred times so many more as they be
rationale: Greek says a hundredfold as they are. Current wording keeps that LXX blessing formula.

greek_phrase: πας ο λαος απο μικρου και εως μεγαλου
chosen_rendering: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and every man of Judah and all those dwelling in Jerusalem with him, and the priests and the prophets and all the people from small to great. And he read in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant found in the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: all the people, both small and great
rationale: Greek says all the people from small to great. Current wording keeps that LXX expression.

greek_phrase: εισελευσομαι προς την γυναικα μου εις τον κοιτωνα
chosen_rendering: And it came to be after days, in the days of wheat harvest, Sampsōn visited his wife, bringing a kid of the goats, and said, I will go in to my wife in the bedroom. And her father did not allow him to go in to her.
alternate_renderings: I will go in to my wife into the chamber
rationale: Greek says into the bedroom. Current wording keeps that LXX room term.

chosen_rendering: And the men of Gilead seized the crossings of the Jordan of Ephraim, and it happened that the fugitives of Ephraim said, Let us cross over, and the men of Gilead said to them, Are you from Ephraim? And they said, We are not.
alternate_renderings: the fugitives of Ephraim
rationale: Greek says the ones saved out of Ephraim, the fugitives. Current wording keeps that LXX wording.

greek_phrase: απο του αργυριου τον σιτον και τον οινον και το ελαιον εξενεγκατε αυτοις
chosen_rendering: Return to them today their fields, their vineyards, their oliveyards, and their houses, and bring out to them from the silver and the grain and the wine and the oil.
alternate_renderings: the hundredth part of the money, and of the corn, the wine, and the oil
rationale: Greek says bring out to them from the silver and the grain and the wine and the oil. Current wording keeps that LXX command.

greek_phrase: αυτου προσκυνουντος εν οικω νεσεραχ θεου αυτου
chosen_rendering: And it came to be, while he was bowing in the house of Neserach his god, Adramelech and Sarasar his sons struck him with the sword, and they escaped into the land of Ararat, and Esarhaddon his son reigned in his place.
alternate_renderings: as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god
rationale: Greek says while he was bowing in the house of Neserach his god. Current wording keeps that LXX line.

greek_phrase: ανηγαγον τους βατραχους επι γην αιγυπτου
chosen_rendering: And the enchanters of the Egyptians did likewise with their sorceries, and they brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.
alternate_renderings: brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt
rationale: Greek says they brought up the frogs upon the land of Egypt. Current wording keeps that LXX verb.

chosen_rendering: then you shall take from the firstfruits of the fruits of your land that the Lord your God gives you and put them into a basket and go to the place that the Lord your God chooses for his name to be called there.
alternate_renderings: to place his name there
rationale: Greek says chooses for his name to be called there. Current wording keeps that LXX formula.

chosen_rendering: And I sent them out to the leader at Casiphia the place, and I put words in their mouth to speak to their brothers the nethinim at Casiphia the place, to bring us singers for the house of our God.
alternate_renderings: to bring unto us ministers
rationale: Greek says to bring us singers for house of our God. Current wording keeps that LXX term.

chosen_rendering: And he said, Peace. My lord has sent me, saying, Behold, now two servant-boys have come to me from the hill-country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of garments.
alternate_renderings: two changes of garments
rationale: Greek says two exchangeable garments, changes of garments. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: ουκ απερριψεν αυτους απο του προσωπου αυτου
chosen_rendering: And the Lord had mercy on them and pitied them and looked toward them because of his covenant with Abraam and Isaak and Iakob, and the Lord did not wish to destroy them and did not cast them from before his face until now.
alternate_renderings: neither cast he them from his presence as yet
rationale: Greek says he did not cast them from before his face. Current wording keeps that LXX phrase.

chosen_rendering: And Manasseh shall have in Issachar and in Asher Kaithoan and their villages and the inhabitants of Dor and their villages and the inhabitants of Megiddo and their villages and the third part of Mapheta and its villages.
alternate_renderings: Bethshean and Ibleam and Endor and Taanach
rationale: Greek list differs sharply here and keeps the third part of Mapheta. Current line keeps LXX place-list.

chosen_rendering: Let us take ark of our God from Selom, and let it go out from our midst, and it will save us from the hand of our enemies.
alternate_renderings: when it cometh among us
rationale: Greek has let it go out from our midst. Current wording keeps that motion.

chosen_rendering: And the allophyles said, Who did these things? And they said, Sampson bridegroom of Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to one of his friends. And the allophyles went up, and they burned her and her father with fire.
alternate_renderings: Samson the son in the law of the Thamnathite
rationale: Greek here reads bridegroom of Timnite and gave her to one of his friends. Current line follows LXX wording.

chosen_rendering: And you shall say to people, Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, because you cried out before the Lord, saying, Who will feed us with meat? because it was good for us in Egypt. And the Lord will give you meat to eat, and you shall eat meat.
alternate_renderings: who shall give us flesh to eat
rationale: Greek uses feed us with meat. Current line keeps that phrase.

chosen_rendering: And the one who made vow shall shave head of his vow beside doors of the tent of testimony, and he shall place hair upon fire, which is under sacrifice of salvation.
alternate_renderings: under the sacrifice of the peace offering
rationale: Greek has sacrifice of salvation. Current line keeps project-consistent cultic wording.

chosen_rendering: and the boundaries shall go down near this part opposite the face of wooded valley Sonnam, which is from part of Rephaim from north, and it will go down to Hinnom by south of Jebusites, from south it will go down by spring of En-rogel,
alternate_renderings: the valley of the son of Ennom
rationale: Greek geography differs and keeps opposite face of wooded valley Sonnam. Current line follows LXX map wording.

greek_phrase: ουκ εστιν υμιν αραι επ ωμων ουθεν
chosen_rendering: And he said to the Levites who were powerful in all Israel that they should be sanctified to the Lord, and they placed the holy ark in the house that Salomon son of Dauid king of Israel had built. And the king said, You are not to carry anything on your shoulders. Now then, minister to the Lord your God and to his people Israel.
alternate_renderings: it shall not be a burden upon your shoulders
rationale: Greek says not for you to carry anything on your shoulders. Current wording keeps that direct line.

chosen_rendering: And the Lord was furiously angry with Israel, and he delivered them into the hand of plunderers, and they plundered them, and he gave them up into the hand of their enemies all around, and they could not withstand before their enemies.
alternate_renderings: into the hands of spoilers that spoiled them
rationale: Greek keeps plunderers / plundered pairing. Current line preserves that repetition.

chosen_rendering: And they brought about terrifying trance on the land which they inspected among sons of Israel, saying, Land that we passed through to spy out is land that consumes people who dwell on it; all the people whom we have seen there in it are men of great stature.
alternate_renderings: they brought up an evil report of the land
rationale: Greek has brought out ecstasis on the land. Current line keeps the shock-terror wording rather than smoothing to evil report.

chosen_rendering: Three times of year each of your males shall appear before the Lord your God in place that Lord may choose it, in the feast of unleavened bread and in the feast of weeks and in the feast of tent-making. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty-handed.
alternate_renderings: feast of tabernacles
rationale: Greek says feast of tent-making. Current line keeps the transparent LXX term.

greek_phrase: υμνουντες τω κυριω καθ ημεραν εν ημερα
chosen_rendering: And sons of Israel found in Ierousalem kept feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness, and priests and Levites hymning to the Lord day by day with instruments to the Lord.
alternate_renderings: they continued daily praising the Lord
rationale: Greek has priests and Levites hymning to the Lord day by day. Current wording keeps that liturgical line.

chosen_rendering: And the king went up to the house of the Lord, and all Iouda and those dwelling in Ierousalem and priests and Levites and all the people, from great to small, and he read in their ears all words of book of covenant found in the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: he read in their ears
rationale: Greek has read in their ears. Current wording keeps direct hearing formula.

greek_phrase: και των αρχοντων και απο παντος καταλοιπου εν ισραηλ
chosen_rendering: And they came to Chelkias the high priest and gave money brought into the house of God, which Levites keeping gate gathered from the hand of Manassē and Ephraim and of rulers and from all remnant in Israel and sons of Iouda and Beniamin and those dwelling in Ierousalem.
alternate_renderings: and from the princes, and from all the remnant in Israel
rationale: Greek keeps rulers and all remnant in Israel. Current line follows wider LXX donor list.

greek_phrase: εσται ισραηλ εις αφανισμον και εις παραβολην
chosen_rendering: then I will remove Israel from the land that I gave them, and this house that I made holy for my name I will cast away from before me, and Israel will become for ruin and for proverb among all peoples.
alternate_renderings: shall be for a desolation and a byword
rationale: Greek has for ruin and for proverb. Current wording keeps those nouns directly.

greek_phrase: οτι δια τουτο διεσωθη δυναμις συριας εκ χειρος σου
chosen_rendering: And at that time Anani the prophet came to Asa king of Iouda and said to him, Because you trusted in king of Syria and did not trust in the Lord your God, because of this force of Syria escaped from your hand.
alternate_renderings: therefore has the host of Syria escaped out of thy hand
rationale: Greek keeps force of Syria escaped from your hand. Current wording stays close.

greek_phrase: εφυλαξεν τον δουλον αυτου εκ χειρος κακων
chosen_rendering: And David heard and said, Blessed be the Lord, who judged judgment of my reproach from the hand of Nabal and preserved his servant from the hand of evils, and the Lord turned back evil of Nabal on his own head.
alternate_renderings: and has kept his servant from evil
rationale: Greek says preserved his servant from hand of evils. Current wording keeps fuller LXX phrase.

greek_phrase: και την προφητειαν αδαδ του προφητου
chosen_rendering: And when he heard these words and prophecy of Adad the prophet, he was strengthened and cast out abominations from all the land of Iouda and Beniamin and from cities which he seized in the mountain of Ephraim and renewed altar of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: and the prophecy of the prophet Oded
rationale: Greek here reads prophecy of Adad the prophet. Current wording keeps extant LXX form.

greek_phrase: ιαθηναι εν ιεζραελ απο των πληγων
chosen_rendering: And Joram returned to be healed in Iezrael from wounds which Syrians gave him in Rama when he fought Azaēl king of Syria, and Ochozias son of Jehoram king of Iouda came down to visit Jehoram son of Ahab in Iezrael, because he was sick.
alternate_renderings: returned to be healed in Jezrael
rationale: Greek has returned to be healed in Iezrael. Current wording keeps healing phrase.

chosen_rendering: And as young man entered, David arose from the stone Ezel and fell on his face and bowed down to him three times, and each kissed his neighbor, and each wept to his neighbor until great completion.
alternate_renderings: until a great while had passed
rationale: Greek says until great completion. Current wording keeps the unusual LXX ending.

chosen_rendering: shall we turn again to scatter your commandments and intermarry with the peoples of lands? Do not be angry with us until completion, so that there be no remnant and no one escaping.
alternate_renderings: till thou hadst consumed us
rationale: Greek has until completion. Current wording keeps the LXX end-term.

greek_phrase: και η κιβωτος του θεου ελημφθη
chosen_rendering: And the young servant answered and said, Man of Israel fled from before foreigners, and there was great blow among people, and both your sons have died, and the ark of God has been taken.
alternate_renderings: the ark of God has been taken
rationale: Greek keeps ark of God has been taken. Current wording stays direct.

chosen_rendering: And she saw, and behold, the king stood at his station and at the entrance, rulers and trumpets around the king, and all the people of the land rejoiced, and they sounded with trumpets, and singers with the instruments of songs and hymning praise.
alternate_renderings: the singers with musical instruments, and praising
rationale: Greek keeps hymning praise. Current wording preserves liturgical cluster and adds needed English articles.

chosen_rendering: And Jehoiada the priest went out and commanded centurions and leaders of force and said to them, Throw her out beyond house, and whoever enters after her, let him die by sword, because priest said, Let her not die in the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: cast her forth without the house
rationale: Greek has throw her out beyond house. Current wording keeps hard imperative.

chosen_rendering: Daniel, Ganathon, Barouch,

chosen_rendering: And man who may act in pride by not listening to priest who stands there ministering on the name of the Lord your God, or to judge who may be in those days, that man shall die, and you shall destroy evil from Israel.
alternate_renderings: to minister in the name of the Lord
rationale: Greek has ministering on the name of the Lord. Current wording keeps the LXX preposition.

greek_phrase: της ερημου της μεγαλης και της φοβερας
chosen_rendering: And setting out from Horeb, we went through all that great and fearful wilderness which you saw, by road of mountain of Amorite, just as Lord our God commanded us, and we came as far as Kadesh-Barnea.

rationale: Greek has great and fearful wilderness. Current wording stays literal.

alternate_renderings: into the brook Kedron
rationale: Greek has throw outside into torrent of Kedrōn. Current line keeps that wording.

greek_phrase: πλην σκηπτρου ιουδα και βενιαμιν μονων
chosen_rendering: And it came to be when all Israel heard that Ieroboam came back from Egypt, they sent and called him to assembly and made him king over Israel, and there was none after house of David except scepter of Iouda and Beniamin alone.
alternate_renderings: except the tribe of Juda only
rationale: Greek has scepter of Iouda and Beniamin alone. Current wording keeps LXX political term.

greek_phrase: σεμιδαλεως αναπεποιημενης εν ελαιω εις θυσιαν
chosen_rendering: And he brought his gift: one silver dish, its weight one hundred thirty shekels, one silver bowl of seventy shekels by holy shekel, both full of fine flour prepared with oil for sacrifice,

rationale: Greek has prepared with oil for sacrifice. Current wording keeps neutral sacrificial wording.

greek_phrase: και συνετελεσεν σαλωμων ολον τον οικον αυτου
chosen_rendering: and Salomon completed his whole house.
alternate_renderings: Solomon finished all his house
rationale: Greek has completed his whole house. Current wording stays direct.

greek_phrase: υπο την σκεπην των δοκων μου
chosen_rendering: Look, I have two daughters who have not known man. I will bring them out to you, and use them as may please you. Only do no wrong to these men, because for this reason they entered under shelter of my roof-beams.

rationale: Greek has under shelter of my roof-beams. Current wording keeps the concrete house image.

chosen_rendering: and boundary goes up to fourth part of Valley of Achor and goes down to Galgala, which is opposite ascent of Adummim, which is south by valley, and comes out to water of spring of sun.
alternate_renderings: the fountain of the sun
rationale: Greek has spring of sun. Current wording keeps transparent place-name.

alternate_renderings: and they had just awaked those that slept
rationale: Greek has roused watchmen. Current wording keeps the watch-change scene.

alternate_renderings: restored the dead son to life
rationale: Greek has restored dead son to life. Current wording stays direct.

greek_phrase: ιστε οτι εστιν εν ταις οικιαις ταυταις
chosen_rendering: And five men going to inspect land answered and said to their brothers, Do you know that in these houses there are ephod and teraphim and carved image and molten image? And now know what you will do.

rationale: Greek says in these houses. Current wording keeps plural local detail.

alternate_renderings: a wonderful man five cubits high
rationale: Greek has visible man, five cubits tall. Current wording keeps extant LXX descriptor.

greek_phrase: κραταιωσαι πασαν καρδιαν πληρη προς αυτον
chosen_rendering: Because eyes of the Lord look through all the earth to strengthen every heart full toward him. You acted foolishly in this; from now on wars shall be with you.
alternate_renderings: to strengthen every heart that is perfect toward him
rationale: Greek has strengthen every heart full toward him. Current wording keeps full-heart image.

greek_phrase: και οι υιοι ιουδα ηρ και αυναν
chosen_rendering: And sons of Judah were Er and Onan, and Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.

rationale: Greek line preserves a Judah-son list here though MT context differs. Current wording should keep extant LXX reading.

greek_phrase: το διαδημα το επι της κεφαλης αυτου

rationale: Greek has kingship-band rather than crown. Current wording keeps regal band image.

chosen_rendering: And he shall take from it with his handful from fine flour of sacrifice with its oil and all frankincense that is on sacrifice, and he shall offer on the altar offering, aroma of sweet fragrance, its memorial to the Lord.
alternate_renderings: for a memorial of it to the Lord
rationale: Greek has its memorial to the Lord. Current wording keeps memorial term.

chosen_rendering: and that they should sound with trumpets in all their cities and in Ierousalem. And Ezra said, Go out to mountain and bring leaves of olive and leaves of cypress woods and leaves of myrtle and leaves of palms and leaves of thick tree to make booths.
alternate_renderings: pine branches and myrtle branches
rationale: Greek specifically has cypress leaves. Current wording keeps the species.

chosen_rendering: watch yourself lest you seek to follow after them after they have been destroyed from before your face. You shall certainly not seek their gods, saying, How do these nations act toward their gods? I also will do likewise.
alternate_renderings: seek not to follow them
rationale: Greek keeps seek their gods. Current wording preserves direct anti-idol inquiry line.

chosen_rendering: And he said to them, Go, eat fat things and drink sweet things and send portions to those having nothing, because day is holy to our Lord, and do not fall away, because he is your strength.
alternate_renderings: neither be ye sorrowful
rationale: Greek has do not fall away. Current wording keeps the sharper exhortation.

chosen_rendering: And King Achaz cut down frames of bases and removed laver from them, and he brought down sea from bronze oxen under it and set it on stone base.
alternate_renderings: the borders of the bases
rationale: Greek keeps frames of bases. Current wording stays concrete.

chosen_rendering: And sons of Israel did thus just as the Lord commanded Joshua, and taking twelve stones from the midst of Jordan, just as the Lord ordered Joshua at the completion of crossing of sons of Israel, they carried them through with them to camp.
alternate_renderings: when they had completely passed over
rationale: Greek has at completion of crossing. Current wording keeps completion term.

chosen_rendering: And boundary will come out down shoulder of Ekron to north and go out to Sakkarona and pass Mount Bala and come out to Jabnel, and boundary's outlet shall be to sea.
alternate_renderings: the border terminates
rationale: Greek repeats come out / outlet. Current wording keeps motion language.

greek_phrase: εαν γενηται ακουσιον απο οφθαλμων της συναγωγης

alternate_renderings: if a trespass be committed unwillingly, unknown to the congregation
rationale: Greek has unintentionally from eyes of congregation. Current wording keeps LXX phrasing.

chosen_rendering: It shall not be hard before you when you send them away free from you, because he served you six years for yearly wage doubled from hired worker, and the Lord your God will bless you in all that you do.

rationale: Greek has yearly wage doubled from hired worker. Current wording keeps that economic comparison.

chosen_rendering: and she shall remove garments of her captivity from herself and sit in your house and mourn her father and her mother full month, and after these things you shall go in to her and live with her, and she shall be your wife.
alternate_renderings: her garments of captivity
rationale: Greek has garments of her captivity. Current wording keeps that exact phrase.

chosen_rendering: And he went up to Baalpharasin, and Dauid struck them there. And Dauid said, God broke through my enemies by my hand like the breaking of waters. Therefore name of that place was called Breach-of-Pharasin.
alternate_renderings: like a breach of waters
rationale: Greek has like breaking of waters. Current wording keeps breach image.

chosen_rendering: And woman went to all the people and spoke to all city in her wisdom, and they removed head of Sheba son of Bochori and threw it to Ioab. And he sounded horn, and they were scattered from the city, each man to his tent.
alternate_renderings: they took off the head of Sheba
rationale: Greek line keeps removed the head and threw it to Ioab. Current wording stays blunt.

chosen_rendering: And he himself went in the wilderness day's road and came and sat under one broom plant, and he asked for his life to die and said, Let it be enough now. Take away my life from me, Lord, because I am no better than my fathers.
alternate_renderings: asked concerning his life that he might die
rationale: Greek has asked for his life to die. Current wording keeps the direct request.

chosen_rendering: And they came to Galgala of Jordan, which is in the land of Canaan, and sons of Gad and sons of Reuben and half tribe of Manasseh built there altar by Jordan, great altar to behold.
alternate_renderings: a great altar to be seen
rationale: Greek has great altar to behold. Current wording keeps visual emphasis.

chosen_rendering: And Iōnathan had not heard when his father put people under oath, and he stretched out tip of his staff that was in his hand and dipped it into comb of honey and turned his hand to his mouth, and his eyes saw again.
alternate_renderings: his eyes recovered sight
rationale: Greek literally says his eyes were enlightened. Current wording keeps the seeing-restored image.

greek_phrase: οι γινωσκοντες αυτον εχθες και τριτην ημεραν
chosen_rendering: And it came to be, all who knew him yesterday and the third day saw, and behold, he was in the midst of prophets, and each person said to his neighbor, What is this that has happened to son of Kis? Is Saoul also among prophets?
alternate_renderings: all that had known him before
rationale: Greek has knew him yesterday and the third day. Current wording keeps the odd temporal formula.

greek_phrase: οτι εγενηθη μερις υιων ιουδα μειζων αυτων

alternate_renderings: the portion of the children of Juda was greater than theirs
rationale: Greek has became greater than theirs. Current wording keeps that comparative explanation.

alternate_renderings: there was no passover like it
rationale: Greek keeps no Passover like it and did not keep such Passover. Current wording should stay emphatic.

greek_phrase: και εκ πασων των αμαρτιων αυτων
chosen_rendering: And this shall be yours from holy things of gifts: from all their gifts and from all their sacrifices and from all their trespasses and from all their sins, whatever they give back to me from all holy things, they shall be yours and your sons'.
alternate_renderings: from all their sins
rationale: Greek list includes all their sins. Current wording keeps full sequence.

chosen_rendering: from the sons of newcomers attached to them in Israel
alternate_renderings: or of the proselytes abiding among them
rationale: Greek has newcomers attached to them. Current wording keeps that participial relation.

chosen_rendering: Lord, God of heaven and God of earth, who took me from my father's house and from the land where I was born, who spoke to me and swore to me, saying, To you and to your seed I will give this land - he himself will send his angel before you.
alternate_renderings: out of the land whence I sprang
rationale: Greek has land where I was born. Current wording stays plain.

greek_phrase: εκαστον κατα των εργων αυτου και κατα το αρμα αυτου
chosen_rendering: By the word of the Lord he counted them by Moses' hand, each man over his works and over what they carried. And they were counted just as the Lord commanded Moses.
alternate_renderings: appointing each man severally over their respective work, and over their burdens
rationale: Greek has over his works and over his carried load. Current wording keeps direct assignment phrasing.

greek_phrase: και εξηλθον αι χορευουσαι εις συναντησιν δαυιδ

alternate_renderings: there came out women in dances to meet David
rationale: Greek has dancing women came out to meet David. Current wording keeps subject concrete.

greek_phrase: και μακροχρονιοι γενησθε επι της γης
chosen_rendering: And you shall keep his ordinances and his commands that I command you today, so that it may be well with you and with your sons after you, so that you may be long-lived on the land that Lord your God gives you all days.
alternate_renderings: that thou mayest live long upon the land
rationale: Greek has become long-lived on land. Current wording keeps explicit long-life phrasing.

chosen_rendering: And sons of Israel again added to do evil before the Lord, and they served Baals and Astarōths and gods of Sidon and gods of Moab and gods of sons of Ammon and gods of foreigners, and they forsook Lord and did not serve him.
alternate_renderings: the gods of Aram ... the gods of the Philistines
rationale: Greek here reads gods of foreigners. Current wording keeps extant LXX category.

greek_phrase: την σωτηριαν την παρα του θεου
chosen_rendering: Then Moses said to people, Take courage. Stand and see salvation from God that he will accomplish for us today. For in way you have seen Egyptians today, you shall never again see them through all time.
alternate_renderings: the salvation which is from the Lord
rationale: Greek has salvation from God. Current wording keeps source phrase.

chosen_rendering: And they went up against Iouda and overpowered and carried away all baggage they found in the house of the king and his sons and his daughters, and no son was left to him except Ochozias, youngest of his sons.
alternate_renderings: and prevailed against them
rationale: Greek has overpowered. Current wording keeps stronger domination verb.

chosen_rendering: And she vowed a vow to the Lord, saying, Lord, Lord my God of hosts, if you will indeed look upon the humiliation of your servant and remember me and give to your servant seed of men, then I will give him before you as a given thing until the day of his death.
alternate_renderings: if thou wilt indeed look upon
rationale: Greek doubles the look verb for emphasis; current wording renders the force with indeed look rather than woodenly repeating look.

chosen_rendering: And sons of Israel cried out to the Lord, and the Lord raised up for them savior, Aōd son of Gēra, son of Benjamite, an ambidextrous man. And sons of Israel sent gifts by his hand to Eglom king of Moab.
alternate_renderings: a man who used both hands alike
rationale: Greek has ambidextrous man. Current wording keeps concise term.

chosen_rendering: So shall you do these things day by day for seven days, gift, fruit-gift for aroma of sweet fragrance to the Lord. Besides continual whole burnt offering you shall do it and its libation.
alternate_renderings: a gift, a sacrifice
rationale: Greek has gift, fruit-gift. Current wording keeps double offering phrase.

chosen_rendering: And Gaal son of Abed said, What is Abimelech, and who is son of Sychem, that we should serve him? Is he not son of Jerobaal, and Zeboul his overseer, his servant with men of Emmōr father of Sychem? And why should we serve him?
alternate_renderings: Zebul his officer
rationale: Greek has Zeboul his overseer. Current wording keeps transparent office term.

chosen_rendering: And sons of Benjamin did so and took wives according to their number from dancers whom they carried off, and they went away and returned to their inheritance and built for themselves cities and dwelt in them.
alternate_renderings: from the dancers whom they seized
rationale: Greek has dancers whom they carried off. Current wording keeps abduction force.

chosen_rendering: And Iou found brothers of Ochozias king of Judah and said, Who are you? And they said, We are brothers of Ochozias, and we came down to greet sons of the king and sons of ruling lady.
alternate_renderings: the sons of the mistress
rationale: Greek has sons of the ruling lady. Current wording keeps political title.

greek_phrase: δια αυτου εδωκεν κυριος σωτηριαν τη συρια
chosen_rendering: And Naiman, commander of force of Syria, was great man before his lord and honored in face, because through him the Lord gave salvation to Syria; and man was mighty in strength, afflicted with skin-disease.
alternate_renderings: the Lord had given deliverance to Syria
rationale: Greek has gave salvation to Syria. Current wording keeps project-consistent term.

greek_phrase: εκαστος εν τη εαυτου αμαρτια αποθανειται
chosen_rendering: But sons of those who struck him he did not put to death, just as it is written in the book of laws of Moses, as the Lord commanded, saying, Fathers shall not die for sons, and sons shall not die for fathers, because each shall die in his own sin.
alternate_renderings: every man shall die for his own sins
rationale: Greek has each in his own sin shall die. Current wording keeps singular construction.

chosen_rendering: And king rose by night and said to his servants, Let me now tell you what Syria has done to us. They know that we are hungry, and they went out from camp and hid themselves in the field, saying, When they come out from the city, we shall seize them alive and enter into the city.
alternate_renderings: when they come out of the city
rationale: Greek has come out from city. Current wording keeps tactical line.

chosen_rendering: And young men reared with him, those standing before his face, spoke to him, saying, Thus you will speak to this people who said to you, Your father made our yoke heavy, and you now lighten from us.
alternate_renderings: who stood before his face
rationale: Greek has those standing before his face. Current wording keeps the court image.

greek_phrase: εξωθεν του καταπετασματος του επι της διαθηκης
chosen_rendering: In the tent of testimony, outside curtain that is over covenant, Aaron and his sons shall tend it from evening until morning before the Lord. This is everlasting ordinance throughout your generations from the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: without the veil that is before the ark of the covenant
rationale: Greek has curtain that is over covenant. Current wording keeps extant LXX phrasing.

chosen_rendering: And they will say, Because they forsook Lord their God who brought their fathers out of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and they held fast to foreign gods and bowed to them and served them. Therefore the Lord brought all this evil upon them.
alternate_renderings: out of the house of bondage
rationale: Greek has from house of slavery. Current wording keeps project-consistent phrase.

greek_phrase: και ουκ ην φωνη και ουκ ην ακροασις
chosen_rendering: And they took calf and prepared it, and they kept calling in the name of Baal from morning until midday and said, Answer us, O Baal, answer us. And there was no voice, and there was no hearing, and they ran about on the altar that they made.
alternate_renderings: there was no voice, and there was no answer
rationale: Greek has no voice and no hearing. Current wording keeps the sharper sensory pair.

greek_phrase: και ηνοιξεν ο θεος τον γομφον
chosen_rendering: And God opened wound of jawbone, and waters came out of it, and he drank, and his spirit returned in him and he revived. Therefore name of it was called Spring, called of Jawbone, until this day.
alternate_renderings: God broke open a hollow place in the jaw
rationale: Greek has opened wound of jawbone. Current wording keeps extant LXX image.

greek_phrase: εαν γνω ανθρωπος την αφην αυτου και την μαλακιαν αυτου
chosen_rendering: then every prayer and every petition which happens to every man and to all your people Israel, if man knows his own touch and his own weakness and spreads out his hands toward this house,
alternate_renderings: if a man should know his own plague and his own sickness
rationale: Greek has his own touch and his own weakness. Current wording preserves that pair.

greek_phrase: και τω προσηλυτω τω προσκειμενω εν αυτοις
chosen_rendering: And one gathering ashes of heifer shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening, and it shall be for the sons of Israel and for sojourners dwelling among them everlasting statute.
alternate_renderings: for the proselytes abiding among them
rationale: Greek has sojourners attached among them. Current wording keeps project resident wording.

chosen_rendering: If you take numbering of sons of Israel at their visitation, each shall give ransom for his life to the Lord, and there shall be no plague among them at their visitation.
alternate_renderings: in the surveying of them
rationale: Greek repeats at their visitation. Current wording keeps visitation formula.

greek_phrase: εισερχομενου του κυριου μου εις οικον ρεμμαν
chosen_rendering: In this matter may the Lord be merciful to your servant: when my lord enters house of Remman to bow there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow in the house of Remman, when I bow in the house of Remman, may the Lord be merciful to your servant in this matter.
alternate_renderings: when my master goes into the house of Remman
rationale: Greek repeats enters/bow in house of Remman. Current wording keeps repetition.

greek_phrase: και επεβλεψας με ως ορασιν ανθρωπου

alternate_renderings: thou hast looked upon me as the appearance of a man
rationale: Greek has as vision of man. Current wording keeps that unusual phrase.

chosen_rendering: And when you enter into the land that Lord your God is giving you, and you plant every edible tree, then you shall purge away its uncleanness. Its fruit shall be uncleansed to you for three years. It shall not be eaten.
alternate_renderings: then shall ye purge away its uncleanness
rationale: Greek doubles uncleanness language. Current wording keeps that pattern.

chosen_rendering: And taking off garments of her widowhood from herself, she put on veil and adorned herself and sat by the gates of Enaim, which is on road to Timnah, for she saw that Shelah had grown up and he had not given her to him as wife.
alternate_renderings: and ornamented her face
rationale: Greek has adorned herself. Current wording keeps broader reflexive form.

rationale: Greek has cistern/pit wording here. Current line keeps extant LXX term.

greek_phrase: και ο ιορδανης απο ανατολων ηλιου

rationale: Greek has Jordan from rising of sun. Current wording keeps sun-rise orientation.

greek_phrase: κατεκλυσεν το υδωρ της ερυθρας θαλασσης επι προσωπον αυτων

rationale: Greek has flooded water over their face. Current wording keeps the vivid line.

rationale: Greek has between judgment and judgment and between wound and wound. Current wording keeps direct pairings.

rationale: Greek has cloud and gloom. Current wording keeps stronger gloom term.

chosen_rendering: and pattern which he had in his spirit of the courts of the house of the Lord and all storerooms around, for treasuries of the house of the Lord and treasuries of holy things,

rationale: Greek has pattern in his spirit. Current wording keeps extant LXX phrasing.

greek_phrase: και ληθη λαθη απο οφθαλμων της συναγωγης
chosen_rendering: And if whole assembly of Israel unintentionally fails to notice, and matter escapes eyes of assembly, and they do one of all commands of the Lord that must not be done, and become guilty,

rationale: Greek has matter escapes eyes of assembly. Current wording keeps the seeing idiom.

chosen_rendering: And the king commanded Chelkias the high priest and priests of second order and keepers of threshold to bring out from the temple of the Lord all vessels made for Baal and for grove and for all host of heaven.
alternate_renderings: them that kept the door
rationale: Greek has keepers of threshold/station. Current wording keeps temple-duty nuance.

greek_phrase: και ειπεν ιου εαν εστιν η ψυχη υμων μετ εμου
chosen_rendering: And Ioram king returned to be healed in Jezrael from wounds with which Syrians struck him when he fought with Hazael king of Syria. And Iou said, If your soul is with me, let none escape from the city to go announce in Jezrael.
alternate_renderings: if your soul is with me
rationale: Greek keeps if your soul is with me. Current wording should stay literal.

chosen_rendering: Because with few men force of Syria came, and God gave into their hands very great force, because they forsook the Lord God of their fathers, and against Joash he made judgments.
alternate_renderings: they executed judgment against Joas
rationale: Greek has against Iōas he made judgments. Current wording keeps plural noun.

chosen_rendering: Which they made: twelve calves, three facing north and three facing west and three facing south and three facing east, and sea was above them, and their hind parts were inward.
alternate_renderings: and their hinder parts were inward
rationale: Greek has their hind parts were inward. Current wording keeps exact physical note.

greek_phrase: εν τη εξοδω αυτου και εν τη εισοδω αυτου
chosen_rendering: And surround king all around, each man with his weapon in his hand, and one entering within ranks shall die. And be with the king in his going out and in his coming in.
alternate_renderings: in his going out and in his coming in
rationale: Greek has going out / coming in. Current wording keeps stock pair.

greek_phrase: και ιδου εισιν εν γη γεσεμ
chosen_rendering: And Joseph came and reported to Pharaoh, saying, My father and my brothers and their cattle and their oxen and all that is theirs have come out of land of Canaan, and look, they are in the land of Goshen.
alternate_renderings: behold, they are in the land of Goshen
rationale: Greek has look, they are in land of Goshen. Current wording keeps presentative look.

greek_phrase: ποσαι αι ημεραι των ετων της ζωης μου
chosen_rendering: And Berzelli said to the king, How many are days of years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Ierousalem?
alternate_renderings: how many are the days of the years of my life
rationale: Greek keeps days of years of my life. Current wording stays literal.

chosen_rendering: Now let not Ezekias deceive you, and let him not make you trust according to these things, and do not believe him, because no god of any nation and kingdom was able to save his people from my hand and from the hand of my fathers.
alternate_renderings: and believe him not
rationale: Greek doubles warning with do not believe him. Current wording keeps full caution.

greek_phrase: οτι ναζιρ θεου εγω ειμι εκ κοιλιας μητρος μου
chosen_rendering: And he told her everything from his heart and said to her, Razor has not come upon my head, because I am Nazirite of God from my mother's womb, and if I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I will grow weak and become like every man.
alternate_renderings: I have been a holy one of God
rationale: Greek specifically has Nazirite of God. Current wording keeps that cultic identity.

chosen_rendering: for your eyes to be opened toward this house day and night, toward place of which you said, My name will be there, to hear prayer that your servant prays toward this place day and night,
alternate_renderings: my name shall be there
rationale: Greek has My name will be there. Current wording keeps name-there formula.

greek_phrase: βαθυ της δερματος της σαρκος αυτου
chosen_rendering: And priest shall inspect mark on skin of his flesh, and if hair in mark has turned white and appearance of mark is deeper than skin of his flesh, it is mark of skin-disease. And priest shall inspect him and pronounce him unclean.

rationale: Greek has deeper than skin of his flesh. Current wording keeps comparative depth.

greek_phrase: και ο ιερευς παρειστηκει παρα την θυραν της πυλης
chosen_rendering: And five men going to inspect land went up there and took carved image and ephod and teraphim and molten image, while priest stood by doorway of gate and six hundred men girded with the weapons of war.
alternate_renderings: the priest stood by the doorway of the gate
rationale: Greek explicitly keeps priest by doorway while theft happens. Current wording preserves scene.

greek_phrase: και αρων αφελει τας αμαρτιας των αγιων
chosen_rendering: And it shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear away sins of holy things, whatever holy gifts sons of Israel sanctify. And it shall be on Aaron's forehead continually, acceptable for them before the Lord.
alternate_renderings: Aaron shall bear the sins of their holy things
rationale: Greek has bear away sins of holy things. Current wording keeps removal nuance.

greek_phrase: και ην εκει προφητης κυριου εκει ωδηδ ονομα αυτω
chosen_rendering: And there was a prophet of the Lord there, Odēd his name, and he went out to meet force coming to Samareia and said to them, Behold, the wrath of the Lord God of your fathers came upon Iouda and he gave them into your hands.
alternate_renderings: there was there a prophet of the Lord, his name was Oded
rationale: Greek keeps prophet of the Lord there and force coming to Samareia. Current line keeps LXX order and diction.

alternate_renderings: I establish a covenant for thee
rationale: Greek has establish covenant and glorious things. Current wording should stay direct.

greek_phrase: εταπεινωσεν την γυναικα του πλησιον αυτου
chosen_rendering: you shall bring them both out to the gate of their city, and they shall be stoned with stones and die, young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and man because he humbled his neighbor's wife.
alternate_renderings: because he humbled his neighbour's spouse
rationale: Greek keeps humbled his neighbor's wife. Current wording preserves that blunt line.

chosen_rendering: And Salomon and all the assembly with him went to high place in Gabaon, because there was the tent of testimony of God which Moyses servant of the Lord made in the wilderness.
alternate_renderings: God's tabernacle of witness
rationale: Greek has tent of testimony of God. Current wording keeps testimony formula.

chosen_rendering: Seven days you shall bring whole burnt offerings to the Lord, and eighth day shall be holy convocation for you, and you shall bring whole burnt offerings to the Lord. It is conclusion. You shall do no servile work.
alternate_renderings: it is a time of release
rationale: Greek closes with it is exodion/conclusion. Current wording keeps distinct close-term.

greek_phrase: τα θυισκια χρυσα και αι επαρυστριδες χρυσαι
chosen_rendering: And on lampstand were seven gold lamps, and its snuffers gold, and their trays gold.
alternate_renderings: its funnels gold
rationale: Greek has snuffers and trays. Current line keeps tray wording over funnels.

greek_phrase: το καλυμμα το υακινθινον το ον επ αυτης επανω

greek_phrase: καὶ Δαυιδ ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν ἄγγελον κυρίου ἑστῶτα ἀνὰ μέσον τῆς γῆς καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

greek_phrase: καὶ ὁ ῥάμνος εἶπεν τοῖς δένδρεσιν Ἐὰν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ὑμεῖς χρίετέ με ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς βασιλέα

greek_phrase: ἐξήγαγέν σε κύριος ἐν χειρὶ κραταιᾷ καὶ ἐν βραχίονι ὑψηλῷ

chosen_rendering: whether I will live from this sickness

greek_phrase: καὶ αὗται αἱ χρεῖαι Σαλωμων ἐν ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ
chosen_rendering: these were the needs for Solomon in one day

greek_phrase: καὶ ἔλαβον ἃ ἐποίησεν Μιχα καὶ τὸν ἱερέα ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ
chosen_rendering: they took what Micha had made and the priest who was his
alternate_renderings: children of Dan took what Michaias had made and priest that he had

greek_phrase: ἐποίησαν τὸ καταπέτασμα τῆς θύρας τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου

greek_phrase: τί ἀποκριθησόμεθα τῷ κυρίῳ ἢ τί λαλήσωμεν ἢ τί δικαιωθησόμεθα
chosen_rendering: what shall we answer to our lord or what shall we speak or how shall we be justified

greek_phrase: ἦρεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶδεν ἄνθρωπον ἑστηκότα ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ
chosen_rendering: lifting his eyes he saw a man standing before him
alternate_renderings: he lifted up his eyes and looked and behold there stood a man opposite to him
rationale: Keeps the Greek before-him wording.

chosen_rendering: with crushing you shall be crushed
alternate_renderings: you shall utterly be destroyed
rationale: Keeps the Greek doubled crushing idiom visible.

greek_phrase: και Μαγαρωθ και Βαιθαναμ και Θεκουμ, εξ πόλεις και αι κώμαι αυτών. Θεκω και Εφραθα, αύτη εστίν Βαιθλεεμ, και Φαγωρ και Αιταν και Κουλων και Ταταμ και Εωβης και Καρεμ και Γαλεμ και Θεθηρ και Μανοχω, ένδεκα πόλεις και αι κώμαι αυτών
lemma: Μαγαρωθ | Βαιθαναμ | Θεκουμ | Θεκω | Εφραθα | Βαιθλεεμ
chosen_rendering: and Magaroth and Baithanam and Thekoum ... Thekoa and Ephratha this is Bethlehem ... eleven cities and their villages
alternate_renderings: Maarath and Bethanoth and Eltekon six cities with their villages
rationale: Keeps the fuller Septuagint place list preserved at this numbering point.

greek_phrase: καὶ ἡγίασεν Ααρων καὶ τὰς στολὰς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς αὐτοῦ καὶ τὰς στολὰς τῶν υἱῶν αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτοῦ

alternate_renderings: and he sanctified Aaron and his garments and his sons and his sons' garments with him

greek_phrase: τοὺς τετρακοσίους ῥοίσκους ἀμφοτέροις τοῖς δικτύοις
chosen_rendering: four hundred pomegranates for both networks
alternate_renderings: work of the bases was on this manner they had borders between ledges
rationale: Keeps the Septuagint pomegranate-count line at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic base-description verse.

greek_phrase: καὶ ἐπὶ χεῖρα αὐτῶν ἐκράτησεν Ραφαια ἄρχων ἡμίσους περιχώρου Ιερουσαλημ
chosen_rendering: next to them Raphaia ruler of half district of Ierousalem repaired
alternate_renderings: next unto them repaired Rephaiah son of Hur ruler of half part of Jerusalem
rationale: Keeps the Greek district phrasing and concise repair notice.

greek_phrase: φυλάξεσθε τὰ προστάγματά μου τοῦ μὴ ποιεῖν ἀπὸ τῶν νομίμων τῶν βδελυρῶν

rationale: Keeps the Greek command/statute wording.

greek_phrase: οὗτοι δῆμοι Μανασση κατὰ τὴν ἐπίσκεψιν αὐτῶν δύο καὶ πεντήκοντα χιλιάδες καὶ ἑπτακόσιοι
chosen_rendering: these are the clans of Manasseh by their enrollment fifty-two thousand seven hundred
alternate_renderings: sons of Benjamin after their families
rationale: Keeps the Septuagint Manasseh total at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic Benjamin list.

greek_phrase: τρίχος στίχος· λιγύριον καὶ ἀχάτης καὶ ἀμέθυστος
chosen_rendering: third row ligure and agate and amethyst
alternate_renderings: covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins above that

chosen_rendering: sons of Adin

chosen_rendering: sons of Banoui

greek_phrase: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς Ηλιου τὸν Θεσβίτην λέγων

greek_phrase: καὶ ἐν πᾶσι τούτοις ἡμεῖς διατιθέμεθα πίστιν καὶ γράφομεν
chosen_rendering: we are making a faithful covenant and writing it
alternate_renderings: now those that sealed were Nehemiah etc.

chosen_rendering: splitting wood for a whole-burnt offering

greek_phrase: τὸ ἐκπορευόμενον διὰ τῶν χειλέων σου φυλάξῃ καὶ ποιήσεις

greek_phrase: καὶ ἐποίησεν τὴν θάλασσαν δέκα ἐν πηχύσιν ἀπὸ τοῦ χείλους αὐτῆς ἕως τοῦ χείλους αὐτῆς ... καὶ τριάκοντα τρεῖς πήχεις ἐκύκλου αὐτήν

chosen_rendering: every opener of the womb from all flesh
alternate_renderings: every thing that opens the womb in all flesh

greek_phrase: καὶ διεμαρτυράμην ἐν ἡμέρᾳ πωλήσεως αὐτῶν
chosen_rendering: I testified on the day of their selling

greek_phrase: Ελιαβ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ Ιδαερ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ Ελκανα υἱὸς αὐτοῦ
chosen_rendering: Eliab his son Idaer his son Elkanah his son
alternate_renderings: Ahitub begat Zadok and Zadok begat Shallum

greek_phrase: καὶ τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς ῥεούσης ἐν τῷ χωρισμῷ αὐτῆς καὶ τοῦ γονορρυοῦς ἐν τῇ ῥύσει αὐτοῦ τῷ ἄρσενι καὶ τῇ θηλείᾳ
chosen_rendering: of the woman flowing in her separation and of the one with discharge in his flow for the male and for the female

chosen_rendering: sons of Elam-ar

greek_phrase: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐπιστρέψαι τὸν ἐνιαυτὸν υἱὸς Αδερ ἐπεσκέψατο τὴν Συρίαν καὶ ἀνέβη εἰς Αφεκα πολεμῆσαι ἐπὶ Ισραηλ

greek_phrase: καὶ Ιησοῦς υἱὸς Ναυη εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τοὺς ἱερεῖς
chosen_rendering: Joshua son of Nun went in to the priests
alternate_renderings: Joshua the son of Nun called the priests and said unto them

greek_phrase: καθὰ τὰ ἔτη πολλά πληθυνεῖς τὴν κτῆσιν αὐτοῦ καὶ καθὰ τὰ ἔτη ὀλίγα ἐλαττώσεις τὴν κτῆσιν αὐτοῦ
chosen_rendering: according as years are many you shall increase its purchase and according as years are few you shall lessen its purchase

greek_phrase: ἤρξαντο ἐν μιᾷ τοῦ μηνὸς τοῦ πρώτου ἁγιάζειν

alternate_renderings: they began on the first day of the first month to sanctify ... in the sixteenth day of the first month they made an end
rationale: Keeps the Greek new-moon phrasing and the sixteenth-day reading.

greek_phrase: καὶ Εφραιμ οὐκ ἐξώλεθρευσεν τὸν Χαναναῖον τὸν κατοικοῦντα ἐν Γαζερ ... ἕως οὗ Φαραω βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου ἀνέβη καὶ ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν καὶ ἐνέπρησεν αὐτὴν ἐν πυρί

greek_phrase: καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτῶν ποιοῦντες τὸ ἔργον τοῦ οἴκου· Αμασι υἱὸς Ζαχαρια ... Φασσουρ ... Μελχια

rationale: Keeps the Septuagint genealogy and omits the Masoretic total at this numbering point.

greek_phrase: περὶ τετρακοσίους ἄνδρες ἀνέβησαν ὀπίσω Δαυιδ καὶ διακόσιοι ἐκάθισαν μετὰ τῶν σκευῶν
chosen_rendering: about four hundred men went up after David and two hundred sat with the baggage
alternate_renderings: David and his men girded on swords and two hundred abode by the stuff
rationale: Keeps the Greek simpler action line.

greek_phrase: πᾶς ἄρσην ἐν τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν φάγεται αὐτήν ... πᾶς ὁ ἁπτόμενος αὐτῶν ἁγιασθήσεται
chosen_rendering: every male among the priests shall eat it ... everyone who touches them shall be sanctified
