rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: son of Athani son of Zophai son of Nahath,
alternate_renderings: As for Elkanah: the sons of Elkanah; Zophai his son, and Nahath his son,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: son of Izhar son of Kohath son of Levi son of Israel.
alternate_renderings: Elkanah his son, and Ebiasaph his son, and Assir his son,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And if you gather your olives, you shall not go back to gather what is behind you. It shall be for the proselyte and the orphan and the widow. And you shall remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt. Because of this I command you to do this word.
alternate_renderings: When you beat yours olive tree, you shall not go over the boughs again: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Adonibezek said, Seventy kings with the tips of their hands and feet cut off used to gather what was under my table. As I did, so God repaid me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
alternate_renderings: And Adonibezek said, Threescore and ten kings, having their thumbs and their great toes cut off, gathered their food under my table: as I have done, so God has requited me. And they brought him to Jerusalem, and there he died.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, Will you come up with us to Ramoth Gilead for war? And Jehoshaphat said, As I am, so are you; as my people, so your people; as my horses, so your horses.
alternate_renderings: And he said unto Jehoshaphat, Will you go with me to battle to Ramothgilead? And Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Giving prayer to the one praying, and he blessed the years of the righteous, because not by strength is a man mighty.
alternate_renderings: He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: You shall eat no blood in all your dwellings, whether from birds or from cattle.
alternate_renderings: Moreover all of you shall eat no manner of blood, whether it be of fowl or of beast, in any of your dwellings.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Rehoboam loved Maachah daughter of Absalom above all his wives and concubines, because he had eighteen wives and thirty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
alternate_renderings: And Rehoboam loved Maachah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and threescore concubines; and brings forth twenty and eight sons, and threescore daughters.)
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Three times of the year celebrate a feast to me.
alternate_renderings: Three times you shall keep a feast unto me in the year.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Thus says Cyrus king of the Persians: The Lord God of heaven gave me all kingdoms of the earth, and he himself commanded me to build for him a house in Jerusalem in Judah. Whoever among you is from all his people, his God shall be with him, and let him go up.
alternate_renderings: Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, All the kingdoms of the earth has the LORD God of heaven given me; and he has charged me to build him an house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Who is there among you of all his people? The LORD his God be with him, and let him go up.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Outside the sword shall make them childless, and from the storerooms fear, young man with virgin, suckling with gray old man.
alternate_renderings: The sword without, and terror within, shall destroy both the young man and the virgin, the nursing infant also with the man of gray hairs.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Go up onto the top of the Hewn Place, and looking up with your eyes toward the sea and north and south and east, see with your eyes, because you shall not cross this Jordan.
alternate_renderings: Get you up into the top of Pisgah, and lift up yours eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and behold it with yours eyes: for you shall not go over this Jordan.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the sons of Dan by their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamite. These are the clans of Dan by their clans.
alternate_renderings: And the name of the daughter of Asher was Sarah.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And he rose and went to Sarepta, to the gate of the city, and behold, there a widow woman was gathering sticks. And Elijah cried after her and said to her, Please fetch me a little water in a vessel and I will drink.
alternate_renderings: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And when he came to the gate of the city, behold, the widow woman was there gathering of sticks: and he called to her, and said, Fetch me, I pray you, a little water in a vessel, that I may drink.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the priest shall inspect the scaly patch on the seventh day, and if the scaly patch has not spread in the skin after the shaving, and its appearance is not deeper than the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean. And after washing his garments, he shall be clean.
alternate_renderings: And in the seventh day the priest shall look on the scab: and, behold, if the scab be not spread in the skin, nor be in sight deeper than the skin; then the priest shall pronounce him clean: and he shall wash his clothes, and be clean.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Men of Nahbi-aar: 52.
alternate_renderings: The men of the other Nebo, fifty and two.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: But when he was afflicted he added to rebel further from the Lord, and the king said,
alternate_renderings: And in the time of his distress did he trespass yet more against the LORD: this is that King Ahaz.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And these are names of the sons of Gershon: Libni and Shimi.
alternate_renderings: And the sons of Kohath; Amram, Izhar, and Hebron, and Uzziel.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: But if the priest does come and inspect, and if the mark has not spread in the house after the house was plastered, then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the mark is healed.
alternate_renderings: And if the priest shall come in, and look upon it, and, behold, the plague has not spread in the house, after the house was plaistered: then the priest shall pronounce the house clean, because the plague is healed.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and the pure lampstand and its lamps, lamps for burning, and the oil of light,
alternate_renderings: And they made two casings of gold, and two gold rings; and put the two rings in the two ends of the breastplate.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: If you fear the Lord and serve him and hear his voice and do not rebel against the mouth of the Lord, then both you and the king who reigns over you will be going after the Lord.
alternate_renderings: If all of you will fear the LORD, and serve him, and obey his voice, and not rebel against the commandment of the LORD, then shall both all of you and also the king that reigns over you continue following the LORD your God:
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And its opening shall be in the middle, with a woven border all around the opening, joined from the same work so that it may not tear.
alternate_renderings: And there shall be an hole in the top of it, in the midst thereof: it shall have a binding of woven work round about the hole of it, as it were the hole of an armour of jacket, that it be not rent.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: All the nethinim and sons of Solomon's servants: 392.
alternate_renderings: All the Nethinims, and the children of Solomon's servants, were three hundred ninety and two.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And there shall not be an old man of yours in my house all the days.
alternate_renderings: And you shall see an enemy in my habitation, in all the wealth which God shall give Israel: and there shall not be an old man in yours house for ever.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the king saw the altar and went up upon it.
alternate_renderings: And when the king was come from Damascus, the king saw the altar: and the king approached to the altar, and offered thereon.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Jehoiada the priest took one chest and bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar, at the right side as a man enters the house of the Lord. And the priests keeping the threshold put there all the silver found in the house of the Lord.
alternate_renderings: And it was so, when they saw that there was much money in the chest, that the king's scribe and the high priest came up, and they put up in bags, and told the money that was found in the house of the LORD.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the Lord said to Moses, Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh, and look, he goes out to the water, and you shall say to him, These things says the Lord: Send out my people so that they may serve me in the wilderness.
alternate_renderings: And the LORD said unto Moses, Say unto Aaron, Stretch out your rod, and strike the dust of the land, that it may become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the boundary shall go around to the north at Hannathon, and its outlet shall be at Gaiphael,
alternate_renderings: And the border compasses it on the north side to Hannathon: and the utmost limit thereof are in the valley of Jiphthahel:
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the Lord said to Moses, This is the land that I swore to Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, saying, To your seed I will give it. I have shown it to your eyes, but you shall not enter there.
alternate_renderings: And the LORD said unto him, This is the land which I swore unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto your seed: I have caused you to see it with yours eyes, but you shall not go over thither.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Sapphin and Apphin and sons of Ir: his son Aher.
alternate_renderings: Shuppim also, and Huppim, the children of Ir, and Hushim, the sons of Aher.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and the Lord, angered in wrath against you, shut up the heaven, and there will be no rain and the land will not give its fruit, and you will perish quickly from the good land that the Lord gave you.
alternate_renderings: And then the LORD's wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit; and lest all of you perish quickly from off the good land which the LORD gives you.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: All these took foreign women and begot sons from them.
alternate_renderings: All these had taken strange wives: and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Moses set up the tent and put on the capitals and inserted the bars and set up the posts.
alternate_renderings: And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and fastened his sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up his pillars.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And you will save the poor people, and the eyes of the proud you will humble.
alternate_renderings: And the afflicted people you will save: but yours eyes are upon the haughty, that you may bring them down.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the redeemer said to Boaz, Acquire my redemption-right for yourself, and he loosened his sandal and gave it to him.
alternate_renderings: Therefore the kinsman said unto Boaz, Buy it for you. So he drew off his shoe.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the king said to Barzillai, You shall cross over with me, and I will sustain your old age with me in Jerusalem.
alternate_renderings: And Barzillai said unto the king, How long have I to live, that I should go up with the king unto Jerusalem?
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It shall be a holy convocation for you, and you shall humble your lives, and you shall bring a whole burnt offering to the Lord.
alternate_renderings: Also on the tenth day of this seventh month there shall be a day of atonement: it shall be an holy convocation unto you; and all of you shall afflict your souls, and offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And one leader from each tribe you shall take to allot the land for you.
alternate_renderings: And all of you shall take one prince of every tribe, to divide the land by inheritance.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and lampstands and lamps for light according to ordinance and before debir, of pure gold,
alternate_renderings: Moreover the candlesticks with their lamps, that they should burn after the manner before the oracle, of pure gold;
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Asher did not remove those dwelling in Acco, and they became tributary to him, and those dwelling in Dor and those dwelling in Sidon and those dwelling in Ahlab and Achzib and Helbah and Aphek and Rehob.
alternate_renderings: Neither did Asher drive out the inhabitants of Accho, nor the inhabitants of Zidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob:
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: to Jachin twenty-first, to Gamul twenty-second,
alternate_renderings: The one and twentieth to Jachin, the two and twentieth to Gamul,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And their boundaries came to be Zorah and Asa, cities of Sammans,
alternate_renderings: And the coast of their inheritance was Zorah, and Eshtaol, and Irshemesh,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: But I live, and my name lives, and the glory of the Lord shall fill the whole earth.
alternate_renderings: But as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the LORD.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And it happened in the morning, his soul was troubled, and he sent and called all the interpreters of Egypt and all its wise men, and Pharaoh told them his dream, and there was no one to declare it to Pharaoh.
alternate_renderings: And it came to pass in the morning that his spirit was troubled; and he sent and called for all the magicians of Egypt, and all the wise men thereof: and Pharaoh told them his dream; but there was none that could interpret them unto Pharaoh.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Eli was ninety years old, and his eyes had become fixed, and he did not see, and Eli said to the men standing around him, What is the voice of this sound?
alternate_renderings: Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were dim, that he could not see.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And if you sacrifice to the Lord a sacrifice, a vow of rejoicing, you shall sacrifice it for acceptance for you.
alternate_renderings: And when all of you will offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving unto the LORD, offer it at your own will.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Seven days the priest who succeeds him from among his sons, who enters the tent of testimony to minister in the holy place, shall wear them.
alternate_renderings: And that son that is priest in his position shall put them on seven days, when he comes into the tabernacle of the congregation to minister in the holy place.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: "Every opener of the womb of a donkey you shall exchange for a sheep, and if you do not exchange it, you shall redeem it. Every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem."
alternate_renderings: And every first born of an ass you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you will not redeem it, then you shall break his neck: and all the firstborn of man among your children shall you redeem.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: because they abandoned me and burned incense to other gods, so as to provoke me in all the works of their hands, and my wrath will burn in this place and will not be quenched.
alternate_renderings: Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense unto other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands; therefore my wrath shall be kindled against this place, and shall not be quenched.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Praise in his holy name; heart seeking his good pleasure shall rejoice.
alternate_renderings: Glory all of you in his holy name: let the heart of them rejoice that seek the LORD.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And it shall be, just as I determined to do to them, I will do to you.
alternate_renderings: Moreover it shall come to pass, that I shall do unto you, as I thought to do unto them.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: You are my brothers; you are my bones and my flesh. Why then do you become the last to bring back the king to his house?
alternate_renderings: And say all of you to Amasa, Are you not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if you be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Let not my lord set his heart on this pestilent man, because as his name, so he is: Nabal is his name, and folly is with him. But I, your servant, did not see your young men whom you sent.
alternate_renderings: Let not my lord, I pray you, regard this man of Belial, even Nabal: for as his name is, so is he; Nabal is his name, and folly is with him: but I yours handmaid saw not the young men of my lord, whom you did send.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and Kibzaim and the set-apart lands toward it, and upper Bethhoron and its set-apart lands, four cities.
alternate_renderings: And Kibzaim with her suburbs, and Bethhoron with her suburbs; four cities.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And if anyone wrongs us or reveals these words of ours, we will be guiltless of this oath of yours.
alternate_renderings: And if you utter this our business, then we will be quit of yours oath which you have made us to swear.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And they gave by lot from the tribe of sons of Judah and from the tribe of sons of Simeon these cities which he called by name.
alternate_renderings: And these are the sons of Aaron; Eleazar his son, Phinehas his son, Abishua his son,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the foundation of the seat he built in the house of the Lord, and the outer entrance of the king he turned within the house of the Lord because of the king of the Assyrians.
alternate_renderings: And the covert for the sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king's entry without, turned he from the house of the LORD for the king of Assyria.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: But if the mark does spread in the skin after the priest has seen him to cleanse him, he shall appear a second time to the priest.
alternate_renderings: But if the scab spread much abroad in the skin, after that he has been seen of the priest for his cleansing, he shall be seen of the priest again.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And sons of Keturah, concubine of Abraham, and she bore to him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, Soe. And sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan.
alternate_renderings: Now the sons of Keturah, Abraham's concubine: she bare Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah. And the sons of Jokshan; Sheba, and Dedan.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And it shall turn back from the rising of the sun to Baithegenech and join to Zebulun, and from Gai to Phthaiel northward, and the boundary shall enter Saphtbaithme and Inael and pass to Hobah Masomel,
alternate_renderings: And turns toward the sunrising to Bethdagon, and reachs to Zebulun, and to the valley of Jiphthahel toward the north side of Bethemek, and Neiel, and goes out to Cabul on the left hand,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the people in it he brought out and set with the saw and with the iron threshing sledges and made them pass through the brickworks. And thus he did to all the cities of the sons of Ammon. And David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
alternate_renderings: And he brought forth the people that were therein, and put them under saws, and under harrows of iron, and under axes of iron, and made them pass through the brick-kiln: and thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon. So David and all the people returned unto Jerusalem.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And Laban called it Heap of Witness, but Jacob called it Witness Heap. And Laban said to Jacob, Look, this heap and this pillar that I set between me and you, this heap bears witness and this pillar bears witness. Therefore its name was called, Heap bears witness.
alternate_renderings: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you this day. Therefore was the name of it called Galeed;
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and Gella and its set-apart lands, and Debir and its set-apart lands,
alternate_renderings: And Holon with her suburbs, and Debir with her suburbs,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the king said to them, You say, This is my living son, and this one's son is the dead one. And you say, No, but my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.
alternate_renderings: Then said the king, The one says, This is my son that lives, and your son is the dead: and the other says, Nay; but your son is the dead, and my son is the living.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: One bruised or crushed or cut out or torn away you shall not bring to the Lord, and in your land you shall not do so.
alternate_renderings: All of you shall not offer unto the LORD that which is bruised, or crushed, or broken, or cut; neither shall all of you make any offering thereof in your land.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And you shall not defile the land on which you dwell, upon which I tabernacle among you, for I am the Lord tabernacling in the midst of the sons of Israel.
alternate_renderings: Defile not therefore the land which all of you shall inhabit, wherein I dwell: for I the LORD dwell among the children of Israel.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: But if they do not cross armed with you before the Lord into war, then you shall bring their baggage and their wives and their cattle across ahead of you into the land of Canaan, and they shall inherit along with you in the land of Canaan.
alternate_renderings: But if they will not pass over with you armed, they shall have possessions among you in the land of Canaan.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And you will say these things at the season: And you are in health, and your house, and all your things in health.
alternate_renderings: And thus shall all of you say to him that lives in prosperity, Peace be both to you, and peace be to yours house, and peace be unto all that you have.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: Let her not become as one equal to death, like a miscarriage coming out from the womb of its mother and devouring half her flesh.
alternate_renderings: Let her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother's womb.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab son of Reuben, whom the earth, opening its mouth, swallowed, and their households and their tents and all their substance that was with them in the midst of all Israel.
alternate_renderings: And what he did unto Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben: how the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their households, and their tents, and all the substance that was in their possession, in the midst of all Israel:
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: sons of Asena, sons of Maonim, sons of Nephusim,
alternate_renderings: The children of Asnah, the children of Mehunim, the children of Nephusim,
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And from them some were over the vessels of the service, because by number they bring them in and by number they bring them out.
alternate_renderings: And certain of them had the charge of the ministering vessels, that they should bring them in and out by tale.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and Elon and its set-apart lands, and Gathrimmon and its set-apart lands, four cities.
alternate_renderings: Aijalon with her suburbs, Gathrimmon with her suburbs; four cities.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the export of the horses of Solomon was from Egypt and from Kue. The merchants of the king were receiving them from Kue by exchange.

chosen_rendering: And placing the grain on their donkeys, they departed from there.

chosen_rendering: except for close kin nearest to them: for father and mother and sons and daughters and brother,

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: If one person's bull gores the bull of his neighbor and it dies, they shall sell the living bull and divide its silver, and they shall divide the dead one.

chosen_rendering: and to those in Jerimoth and to those in Beersheba and to those in Noo,

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And David seized his garments and tore them, and all the men with him tore their garments.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And you shall not spare a poor man in judgment.
alternate_renderings: Neither shall you countenance a poor man in his cause.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the nakedness of your father's sister and your mother's sister you shall not uncover, for he has uncovered close kin. They shall bear sin.
alternate_renderings: And you shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, nor of your father's sister: for he uncovers his near kin: they shall bear their iniquity.
rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And there we saw the giants, and before them we were like locusts, and so we were before them.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And they removed the foreign gods from their midst and served the Lord. And it was not pleasing in the people, and he grew short of soul in the toil of Israel.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the man who does not hear whatever the prophet speaks in my name, I will exact it from him.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: and the Lord chose you today to become for him a people of special possession, just as he said to you, to keep all his commands,

chosen_rendering: Not so with my servant Moses; in all my house he is faithful.

chosen_rendering: so that these may exist for you as a sign lying there forever, so that when your son asks you tomorrow, saying, What are these stones to you?

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

chosen_rendering: And the nave in front was forty cubits.

rationale: Keeps Septuagint verse wording at this numbering point rather than the Masoretic wording.

greek_phrase: αποστελω αυτω κλινοντας ... τα σκευη αυτου λεπτυνουσιν ... τα κερατα αυτου συγκοψουσιν

chosen_rendering: Chemosh ... Bethel

chosen_rendering: Holon ... Jahazah ... Mephaath

chosen_rendering: Kiriathaim ... Beth-gamul ... Beth-meon

chosen_rendering: Kerioth ... Bozrah
alternate_renderings: Carioth; Bosor; Besor

chosen_rendering: Moab will clap with his hand

chosen_rendering: vine of Sibmah. Your branches

chosen_rendering: all hands will beat

rationale: In a mourning list with shaved heads, shaved beards, and sackcloth, κόπτω is treated as beating/striking in lament rather than literal cutting of hands.

chosen_rendering: Kerioth

rationale: The Greek form points to Kerioth in the Moab oracle; the standard English equivalent is used for consistency with the earlier city list.

chosen_rendering: a snare and fear and pit
alternate_renderings: snare, fear, and pit
rationale: The judgment triad is kept compact and literal because verse 44 repeats each image in sequence.

greek_phrase: το ποτηριον του οινου του ακρατου
chosen_rendering: cup of unmixed wine
alternate_renderings: cup of undiluted wine; cup of pure wine
rationale: Unmixed wine keeps the Greek image of an undiluted judgment cup that the nations must drink.

greek_phrase: βασιλεις αλλοφυλων ... ασκαλωνα ... γαζαν ... ακκαρων ... αζωτου

alternate_renderings: all kings of foreigners

chosen_rendering: Dedan and Teman and Rosh

chosen_rendering: you will certainly not be cleansed

chosen_rendering: will utter ... shouting like grape-treaders

chosen_rendering: He himself enters judgment with all flesh

chosen_rendering: beat yourselves, rams of the sheep
alternate_renderings: cut yourselves, rams of sheep
rationale: As in Jeremiah 31:37, κόπτω is treated as a mourning gesture of beating/striking rather than literal self-cutting.

chosen_rendering: declare ... declare
alternate_renderings: answer; utter an oracle
rationale: In the temple-court setting, χρηματίζω is rendered as declare to avoid the misleading English answer where no question is in view.

chosen_rendering: relent from the evils

chosen_rendering: like Shiloh

chosen_rendering: Micah the Morasthite

chosen_rendering: Kiriath-jearim

rationale: Kiriath-jearim is the standard English equivalent for the Greek place-name form.

chosen_rendering: bonds and yokes
alternate_renderings: bands and yokes

chosen_rendering: under the yoke of the king of Babylon
alternate_renderings: under Babylon's yoke

chosen_rendering: false prophets ... divining ... dreaming ... omens ... sorceries
alternate_renderings: false prophets ... soothsayers ... dreamers ... auguries ... enchantments

chosen_rendering: let them meet me

chosen_rendering: the remaining vessels

chosen_rendering: Hananiah son of Azor ... from Gibeon

rationale: Standard English equivalents are used for Hananiah and Gibeon while preserving Azor from the Greek form.

chosen_rendering: two full years
alternate_renderings: two years of days

greek_phrase: ο προφητης ο προφητευσας εις ειρηνην

chosen_rendering: wooden yokes ... iron yokes

chosen_rendering: trust in an unjust thing

chosen_rendering: to the elders of exile

chosen_rendering: seek the peace of the land

chosen_rendering: seventy years

chosen_rendering: I plan for you a plan of peace

chosen_rendering: roasted in fire

greek_phrase: εις το αποκλεισμα και εις τον καταρρακτην

chosen_rendering: It is long

chosen_rendering: trust in unjust things

greek_phrase: ει ετεκεν αρσεν ... χειρες αυτου επι της οσφυος ... προσωπα εις ικτερον

greek_phrase: τον δαυιδ βασιλεα αυτων αναστησω αυτοις

greek_phrase: poiōn gēn kai plassōn autēn tou anorthōsai autēn

chosen_rendering: I will reveal to them a hearing

chosen_rendering: they will fear and be embittered

chosen_rendering: Still it will be heard

chosen_rendering: under the hand of one counting

chosen_rendering: all his camp and all the land under his rule

chosen_rendering: in being handed over, will be handed

chosen_rendering: in being seized you will be seized

chosen_rendering: Ah, lord, they will beat themselves for you

chosen_rendering: proclaim release ... turned back

chosen_rendering: free according to their own desire

rationale: Desire renders psyche in this legal freedom idiom while the note preserves the Greek soul wording.

greek_phrase: kalo aphesin hymin eis machairan kai eis ton thanaton kai eis ton limon
chosen_rendering: release to you to sword and to death and to famine
alternate_renderings: liberty to sword pestilence famine; release to sword death famine
rationale: The translation keeps the bitter aphesis reversal and follows the LXX death wording rather than harmonizing to pestilence.

greek_phrase: ton moschon hon epoiesan ergazesthai auto
chosen_rendering: the calf which they prepared to perform it with
alternate_renderings: the calf which they made to work with it; the calf used in covenant enactment

greek_phrase: dynamis basileos Babylonos tois apotrechousin ap auton

chosen_rendering: the house of the Rechabites

chosen_rendering: shall certainly not drink wine forever

chosen_rendering: dwell in tents ... sojourn

chosen_rendering: from before the force
alternate_renderings: from the face of the force; for fear of the army
rationale: The phrase is kept close to the Greek face/before idiom while making the military pressure from Chaldeans and Assyrians readable.

chosen_rendering: receive discipline, to listen to my words

rationale: Discipline keeps the regular paideia rendering and the infinitive shows the intended result: hearing the Lord's words.

chosen_rendering: upheld the word ... rising early and speaking
alternate_renderings: the word stood; kept the word ... speaking early

chosen_rendering: amend your practices
alternate_renderings: make your practices better
rationale: Amend your practices gives natural English for making conduct better while preserving the concrete repentance command.

greek_phrase: ou me eklipē ... parestēkōs kata prosōpon mou
chosen_rendering: will certainly not fail to stand before my face
alternate_renderings: will not lack a man standing before me; a man will certainly not fail before my face
rationale: The promise keeps the emphatic not-fail formula and the before-my-face service language for Jonadab's sons.

chosen_rendering: a scroll-sheet ... which I declared to you
alternate_renderings: scroll-sheet ... which I answered to you; book-scroll
rationale: The wording keeps the concrete chartion bibliou phrase while aligning echrematisa with the prior Jeremiah 37:2 decision to render divine disclosure as declared.

chosen_rendering: I am kept under guard
alternate_renderings: I am guarded; I am shut up
rationale: The passive guard wording explains why Jeremiah sends Baruch to read publicly in the temple instead of entering himself.

greek_phrase: peseitai eleos auton kata prosopon kyriou
chosen_rendering: their plea for mercy will fall before the face of the Lord
alternate_renderings: their mercy will fall before the Lord
rationale: The Greek mercy-falling idiom is rendered as a plea for mercy so the petition sense is clear while preserving the before-the-face wording.

chosen_rendering: sent Jehudi ... to Baruch
alternate_renderings: sent to Baruch Jehudi
rationale: The clause identifies Jehudi as the messenger sent to Baruch; the rendering untangles the compressed Greek order without dropping the lineage.

chosen_rendering: we must surely announce
alternate_renderings: announcing let us announce
rationale: The doubled announce construction is rendered with surely to mark the officials' resolved report to the king.

greek_phrase: treis selidas kai tessaras ... xyro tou grammateos
chosen_rendering: three columns or four ... the scribe's knife
alternate_renderings: three pages and four ... scribe's knife
rationale: Columns fits a scroll-reading scene better than modern pages, and the scribe's knife belongs to the physical cutting and burning of the sheet.

chosen_rendering: Jerahmeel ... Seraiah son of Esriel
alternate_renderings: Jeremeeel ... Seraiah son of Azriel
rationale: Jerahmeel is standardized from the Greek royal-official name while Esriel preserves the Greek patronymic in this verse.

chosen_rendering: In entering, the king of Babylon will enter
alternate_renderings: the king of Babylon will surely enter
rationale: The doubled entering verb is kept visibly because Jehoiakim objects to the oracle's certain Babylonian invasion claim.

greek_phrase: ouk edokan auton eis oikon tes phylakes
chosen_rendering: they had not put him into the house of the prison
alternate_renderings: they had not given him into the house of prison
rationale: The line marks Jeremiah's freedom before his arrest at Benjamin gate; put him into makes the prison idiom readable.

chosen_rendering: In running away, the Chaldeans will depart from us
alternate_renderings: fleeing away, they will go away
rationale: The doubled flight/departure wording preserves Judah's false confidence that the Chaldean withdrawal will last.

chosen_rendering: some wounded men remain
alternate_renderings: some remain pierced
rationale: The hypothetical wounded survivors still rise and burn the city; wounded men clarifies the military image.

chosen_rendering: Seraiah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah
alternate_renderings: Seraiah son of Shelemiah son of Ananiah
rationale: Standard English equivalents are used for the Benjamin-gate arrest scene while retaining Seraiah for the Greek form.

chosen_rendering: house of the pit ... cells
alternate_renderings: house of pit ... dungeon
rationale: The Greek prison sequence is kept concrete: Jeremiah is moved from the scribe's house into the pit-house and cells.

greek_phrase: peseto to eleos mou kata prosopon sou
chosen_rendering: my plea for mercy fall before your face
alternate_renderings: my mercy fall before your face
rationale: The same mercy-falling idiom as 43:7 is rendered as a plea while preserving before-your-face formality.

chosen_rendering: from outside where they baked
alternate_renderings: from outside where loaves fall
rationale: The verb is taken in the baking/cooking sense in the daily bread-ration scene; the line ends when bread fails from the city.

chosen_rendering: his soul will be for gain
alternate_renderings: his life will be as spoil
rationale: The phrase keeps the Greek soul and gain wording for the one who leaves the city and survives.

chosen_rendering: in being handed over, will be handed
alternate_renderings: will surely be handed over
rationale: The doubled handing-over verb matches the prior certainty formula used for Jerusalem's delivery to Babylon.

greek_phrase: ou chresmologei eirenen ... all' e ponera
chosen_rendering: does not prophesy peace ... but evil things
alternate_renderings: does not seek peace ... but evil
rationale: The accusation concerns Jeremiah's oracle content; prophesy peace fits the speech verb better than seek peace.

chosen_rendering: pit ... mire
alternate_renderings: pit ... mud
rationale: The verse keeps the physical descent into the pit and the detail that there was no water there but mire.

greek_phrase: labe eis tas cheiras sou ... triakonta anthropous
chosen_rendering: take thirty men in your hands
alternate_renderings: take thirty men with you
rationale: The phrase keeps the hand-language while making the king's rescue order to Ebed-melech clear.

chosen_rendering: the house of Aselisi
alternate_renderings: the third house
rationale: The Greek preserves Aselisi rather than a transparent third-entrance phrase, so the draft keeps the LXX place label in the temple setting.

greek_phrase: ei apokteno se kai ei doso se
chosen_rendering: I will not kill you ... I will not give you
alternate_renderings: if I kill you ... if I give you
rationale: The negative oath form is rendered by its English force: Zedekiah promises not to kill Jeremiah or hand him over.

chosen_rendering: in going out, you go out
alternate_renderings: if you surely go out
rationale: The doubled going-out verb stresses Zedekiah's surrender to Babylon's rulers as the path to life.

chosen_rendering: men of peace ... slippery places
alternate_renderings: peace-men ... slipping-places
rationale: The women's taunt preserves the men-of-peace label and the image of Zedekiah's feet being placed in slippery places.

greek_phrase: ripto to eleos mou kat' ophthalmous tou basileos
chosen_rendering: I cast my plea for mercy before the eyes of the king
alternate_renderings: I cast my mercy before the eyes of the king
rationale: The mercy-falling/casting idiom is rendered as a plea while preserving the courtly before-the-eyes formula.

chosen_rendering: the lord's word was not heard
alternate_renderings: the word of the Lord was not heard
rationale: In context the phrase refers to the private word from the king not being overheard; lowercase lord marks the royal title rather than a divine oracle.

chosen_rendering: he and all his force
alternate_renderings: all his force
rationale: The added he and commas make the Babylonian army subject readable while keeping force for the military host.

chosen_rendering: the city was breached
alternate_renderings: city was broken through
rationale: The formal date line is smoothed with articles while preserving the breach event.

greek_phrase: hegemones basileos Babylonos ... pyli te mese
chosen_rendering: rulers of the king of Babylon ... the middle gate
alternate_renderings: princes of the king of Babylon ... middle gate
rationale: The line keeps the LXX list of Babylonian rulers and their sitting in the middle gate after the city breach.

greek_phrase: eis kaka kai ouk eis agatha
chosen_rendering: for evil things and not for good things
alternate_renderings: for evils and not for good
rationale: The plural good/evil pairing matches the Lord's words coming upon the city in judgment.

greek_phrase: anthropon hon sy phobe apo prosopou auton
chosen_rendering: the men whose face you fear
alternate_renderings: the men you fear from before their face
rationale: The wording keeps face-language for the feared men while avoiding a doubled English prepositional phrase.

greek_phrase: sozōn sōsō se ... psyche sou eis heurema
chosen_rendering: in saving, I will save you ... your soul will be for gain
alternate_renderings: I will surely save you ... your life will be as spoil
rationale: The rescue promise keeps the doubled saving verb and repeats the soul-for-gain phrase from Jeremiah 45:2.

chosen_rendering: Nebuzaradan the chief cook
alternate_renderings: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard
rationale: Chief cook keeps the literal LXX title already used in this section while identifying Nebuzaradan's release of Jeremiah from Ramah.

greek_phrase: cheiropedon ... thesō tous ophthalmous mou epi se
chosen_rendering: handcuffs ... set my eyes on you
alternate_renderings: chains ... look well to you
rationale: The verse keeps the handcuff image and the eye-care idiom in Nebuzaradan's offer of protection.

greek_phrase: hegemones tes dynameos tes en agro
chosen_rendering: the leaders of the force in the field
alternate_renderings: the captains of the forces in the fields
rationale: The smoke-pinned phrase is kept with field singular in verse 7 while verse 13 keeps the plural fields form.

chosen_rendering: wine and summer fruit and oil
alternate_renderings: wine and fruit and oil
rationale: The seasonal harvest term is rendered summer fruit in Gedaliah's instruction to gather supplies into vessels.

chosen_rendering: gave a remnant to Judah
alternate_renderings: gave remnant to Judah
rationale: The line describes news reaching Judeans in neighboring lands that Babylon had left a remnant under Gedaliah.

greek_phrase: ei gnōsei ginōskeis ... pataxai sou psychen
chosen_rendering: In knowledge do you know ... strike your soul
alternate_renderings: Do you know for certain ... kill you
rationale: The doubled knowing phrase and soul-striking idiom are preserved in the warning about Ishmael's plot.

chosen_rendering: Elasa ... from the seed of the king
alternate_renderings: Eleasah ... of the royal family
rationale: Elasa follows the Greek name form and seed of the king keeps the dynastic wording for Ishmael.

chosen_rendering: manna and frankincense
alternate_renderings: manna and frankincense
rationale: The offering list keeps the LXX wording rather than substituting a Hebrew-based meal-offering term.

chosen_rendering: slaughtered them into the pit
alternate_renderings: slaughtered them into a pit
rationale: The article is kept because verse 9 identifies the pit as Asa's great pit.

chosen_rendering: the great pit ... because of Baasha
alternate_renderings: the great pit ... against Baasha
rationale: The pit note is smoothed while preserving Asa's construction because of Baasha king of Israel.

chosen_rendering: the chief cook entrusted
alternate_renderings: the captain of the guard committed
rationale: Chief cook continues the literal LXX title and entrusted fits the handover of the king's daughters to Gedaliah.

chosen_rendering: all their camp ... the great water
alternate_renderings: all their army ... much water
rationale: Camp keeps the repeated force terminology and the water phrase is rendered as a recognizable landmark near Gibeon.

chosen_rendering: whom he turned back from Ishmael
alternate_renderings: whom he recovered from Ishmael
rationale: The repeated turned-back verb is kept for Johanan's recovery of the remnant from Ishmael and from Gibeon.

chosen_rendering: Gaberoth-chamaam
alternate_renderings: Geruth Chimham
rationale: The translation keeps the Greek place form in the flight-toward-Egypt notice near Bethlehem.

chosen_rendering: from before the Chaldeans ... before their face
alternate_renderings: for fear of the Chaldeans
rationale: The face-language is retained in the explanation for the remnant's flight toward Egypt.

greek_phrase: peseto to eleos hemon kata prosopon sou
chosen_rendering: our plea for mercy now fall before your face
alternate_renderings: let our supplication be accepted
rationale: The mercy-falling idiom is rendered as a plea while preserving the before-your-face address to Jeremiah.

chosen_rendering: the way ... the word which we should do
alternate_renderings: the way ... the thing we should do
rationale: The line keeps word for logos even in the idiom of doing what the Lord says.

greek_phrase: Kyrios en hemin eis martyra dikaion kai piston
chosen_rendering: the Lord be among us as a righteous and faithful witness
alternate_renderings: the Lord be a true and faithful witness between us
rationale: Among us makes the witness formula readable while keeping the Greek in-us phrasing visible.

greek_phrase: hon hemeis apostellomen se pros auton
chosen_rendering: the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, we will hear
alternate_renderings: unto whom we send thee
rationale: The awkward relative clause is clarified as the people sending Jeremiah to pray to the Lord while keeping the voice phrase fronted.

chosen_rendering: in settling you settle ... I have ceased
alternate_renderings: if you will still abide ... I repent
rationale: The doubled settling verb is retained and anapepaumai is rendered ceased in the promise to spare the remnant.

chosen_rendering: before the face of the king of Babylon
alternate_renderings: because of the king of Babylon
rationale: The warning keeps the face-language for the king whom the remnant fears.

greek_phrase: doso hymin eleos kai eleeso hymas
chosen_rendering: I will give you mercy and have mercy on you
alternate_renderings: I will show mercies to you
rationale: The repeated mercy noun and verb are kept in the restoration promise.

greek_phrase: dote to prosopon hymon eis Aigypton
chosen_rendering: set your face toward Egypt
alternate_renderings: set your faces to enter Egypt
rationale: The face-setting idiom is kept for the remnant's resolved flight to Egypt.

chosen_rendering: the sword which you fear before its face ... the famine
alternate_renderings: the sword which you fear ... the famine
rationale: The sword and famine warning keeps the face idiom and the pursuit image of famine overtaking them behind them.

chosen_rendering: my wrath dripped ... subject people
alternate_renderings: my fury poured out ... an execration
rationale: The LXX dripping-wrath image is kept and hypocheirioi is clarified as subject people rather than underhand.

chosen_rendering: in knowing, you will know
alternate_renderings: know certainly
rationale: The doubled knowing phrase marks Jeremiah's warning that the Egypt flight will end in death.

chosen_rendering: you acted wickedly in your souls
alternate_renderings: you dissembled in your hearts
rationale: The line keeps souls while making Jeremiah's charge against their false promise readable.

chosen_rendering: ceased speaking to the people all the words of the Lord
alternate_renderings: finished speaking all the words of the Lord
rationale: The opening keeps the full redundant LXX phrase that frames the people's rejection after Jeremiah finishes the oracle.

chosen_rendering: You are speaking lies
alternate_renderings: Lies
rationale: The clipped Greek accusation is expanded just enough to make the charge against Jeremiah readable.

chosen_rendering: is setting you against us
alternate_renderings: incites you against us
rationale: The accusation targets Baruch as pushing Jeremiah against the remnant; setting you against us keeps that force without adding conspiracy language.

chosen_rendering: all the remnant of Judah
alternate_renderings: all the remnants of Judah
rationale: The plural remnant term is rendered as a collective remnant for the group carried into Egypt.

chosen_rendering: the souls whom Nebuzaradan had left
alternate_renderings: the persons whom Nebuzaradan left
rationale: Souls is kept for the people left under Gedaliah before the forced move to Egypt.

greek_phrase: en prothyrois en pyle tes oikias Pharao
chosen_rendering: the forecourt at the gate of the house of Pharaoh
alternate_renderings: the entry of Pharaoh's house
rationale: Forecourt at the gate keeps the LXX threshold/gate setting for the hidden stones sign-act.

greek_phrase: arei ta hopla autou ep' autous
chosen_rendering: raise his weapons over them
alternate_renderings: spread his royal pavilion over them
rationale: The LXX reads weapons rather than pavilion and the translation keeps that martial image over the hidden stones.

chosen_rendering: those for death, to death
alternate_renderings: such as are for death to death
rationale: The repeated destination formula is punctuated to preserve the threefold death/exile/sword cadence.

greek_phrase: phtheiriei ... hosper phtheirizei poimen to himation autou
chosen_rendering: delouse the land of Egypt as a shepherd delouses his garment
alternate_renderings: wrap himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd with his garment
rationale: The LXX uses a delousing/searching image; the translation preserves the strange shepherd-garment comparison.

greek_phrase: stylous heliou poleos tous en On
chosen_rendering: pillars of Sun-city those in On
alternate_renderings: images of Heliopolis
rationale: The phrase is kept as Sun-city in On so both the Greek city label and Egyptian place name remain visible.

chosen_rendering: Migdol ... Tahpanhes ... Pathros
alternate_renderings: Migdol ... Tahpanhes ... Pathros
rationale: The address keeps the LXX Egyptian place list for Judeans living in Egypt.

chosen_rendering: desolate, without dwellers
alternate_renderings: desolate without inhabitants
rationale: Without dwellers keeps the source phrase while reading as a normal English result clause.

chosen_rendering: rising early and sending
alternate_renderings: rising up early and sending
rationale: This matches earlier Jeremiah wording for the Lord's repeated sending of prophets.

greek_phrase: estaxen he orge mou kai ho thymos mou
chosen_rendering: my wrath and my anger dripped
alternate_renderings: my wrath was poured out
rationale: The dripping-wrath image is retained as in Jeremiah 49:18.

chosen_rendering: great evils against your souls
alternate_renderings: great evil against yourselves
rationale: The line keeps souls in the accusation that the Egypt remnant is destroying itself.

chosen_rendering: Have you forgotten the evils
alternate_renderings: Have you not forgotten the wickedness
rationale: The question charges the remnant with forgetting Judah's former evils rather than asking whether they remember them.

chosen_rendering: did not hold fast to my ordinances
alternate_renderings: did not walk in my law
rationale: Hold fast better matches antechomai than endure in the obedience summary.

chosen_rendering: Behold I set my face
alternate_renderings: Behold I set my face
rationale: The verse remains a split sentence completed by verse 12 because the LXX verse division breaks the judgment clause there.

chosen_rendering: except escaped ones
alternate_renderings: except fugitives
rationale: Escaped ones keeps the rescue/survival root while marking the tiny exception to the no-return oracle.

chosen_rendering: their wives were burning incense to other gods
alternate_renderings: their women burned incense
rationale: The response identifies the men who knew about their wives' incense and the large women's assembly in Pathros.

chosen_rendering: we will not listen to you
alternate_renderings: we will not hear from you
rationale: Listen to you captures the people's blunt refusal of Jeremiah's word in the Lord's name.

chosen_rendering: in doing, we will do ... queen of heaven
alternate_renderings: we will certainly do ... queen of heaven
rationale: The doubled doing phrase and queen-of-heaven title are preserved in the people's defiant vow.

chosen_rendering: were well off
alternate_renderings: were good
rationale: The people's claim is that queen-of-heaven worship brought prosperity; well off avoids a misleading moral reading.

chosen_rendering: made cakes for her
alternate_renderings: made cakes to worship her
rationale: Cakes keeps the LXX ritual food term in the women's defense of their offerings.

chosen_rendering: rose upon his heart
alternate_renderings: came into his mind
rationale: The heart image is retained for the Lord's remembrance of their incense in Judah and Jerusalem.

chosen_rendering: because of the evil of your deeds
alternate_renderings: from the face of the evil of your deeds
rationale: Because of gives the causal force while keeping deeds and abominations explicit.

chosen_rendering: in doing we will do ... in abiding, you abided
alternate_renderings: we will surely perform ... you have performed
rationale: The doubled doing and abiding phrases show the women completing the vows they spoke.

chosen_rendering: my name shall certainly no longer be in the mouth
alternate_renderings: if my name still becomes in the mouth
rationale: The divine oath is rendered by its English force: the Lord's name will no longer be used in Judah's oath formula in Egypt.

chosen_rendering: watched over them for evil and not for good
alternate_renderings: watched over them to hurt and not to help
rationale: The wording keeps the watch-over formula while matching the good/evil pairing from the Greek.

chosen_rendering: whose word stands
alternate_renderings: whose word shall stand
rationale: The remnant will learn whether their word or Jeremiah's word remains standing.

chosen_rendering: Hophra ... those seeking his soul
alternate_renderings: Pharaoh Hophra ... those seeking his life
rationale: Hophra follows the common English royal name while soul keeps the repeated life-seeking phrase.

greek_phrase: en to biblio apo stomatos Ieremiou
chosen_rendering: the scroll from the mouth of Jeremiah
alternate_renderings: the book at the mouth of Jeremiah
rationale: The Baruch notice keeps the dictated-scroll setting in the fourth year of Jehoiakim.

chosen_rendering: Alas, alas ... toil upon pain
alternate_renderings: Woe is me ... grief to my sorrow
rationale: Alas keeps the lament cry and toil upon pain preserves the doubled burden phrase.

greek_phrase: hous egō ōkodomēsa ... hous egō ephyteusa
chosen_rendering: what I built, I tear down ... what I planted, I pull up
alternate_renderings: that which I built I will break down ... that which I planted I will pluck up
rationale: The oracle mirrors Jeremiah's build/plant language and reverses it in judgment.

chosen_rendering: your soul for gain
alternate_renderings: your life as spoil
rationale: The Baruch promise repeats the soul-for-gain survival phrase used earlier in Jeremiah 45 and 46.

chosen_rendering: Hamutal ... Libnah
alternate_renderings: Amitaal ... Lobena
rationale: Standard English forms are used for Zedekiah's mother and her town while noting the Greek name forms.

chosen_rendering: built around it with four-cornered stones
alternate_renderings: built forts against it round about
rationale: The LXX describes siege construction with four-cornered stones rather than importing a generic siege mound.

chosen_rendering: the city was broken through
alternate_renderings: the city was breached
rationale: The wording preserves the break-through event and keeps the smoke-pinned city phrase for this recap.

chosen_rendering: Riblah ... spoke judgment with him
alternate_renderings: Riblah ... gave judgment upon him
rationale: Riblah is the standard place form for Greek Deblatha; spoke judgment with him keeps the court formula.

chosen_rendering: mill-house
alternate_renderings: prison
rationale: The Greek says mill-house; the translation keeps that concrete confinement term instead of replacing it with prison.

chosen_rendering: Nebuzaradan the chief cook
alternate_renderings: Nebuzaradan captain of the guard
rationale: Chief cook continues the literal LXX title used for Nebuzaradan in this section.

chosen_rendering: some of the remnant of the people as vine-dressers and farmers
alternate_renderings: the poor of the land for vinedressers and husbandmen
rationale: The LXX has remnant rather than poor of the land and keeps the agricultural assignments concrete.

chosen_rendering: the bronze pillars ... the bronze sea
alternate_renderings: the pillars of brass ... the brasen sea
rationale: The plunder notice keeps the bronze temple furnishings and the Chaldeans' shattering action.

chosen_rendering: whatever was gold, gold ... silver, silver
alternate_renderings: what was of gold in gold and what was of silver in silver
rationale: The repeated metal terms are retained to mark sorted temple vessels.

greek_phrase: ouk en stathmos tou chalkou auton
chosen_rendering: no weighing of their bronze
alternate_renderings: without weight
rationale: The line keeps the claim that Solomon's bronze furnishings were beyond weighing.

chosen_rendering: capital ... netting and pomegranates
alternate_renderings: chapiter ... network and pomegranates
rationale: The temple detail keeps the capital projection and decorative netting with pomegranates.

greek_phrase: ton hierea ton proton ... treis tous phylassontas ten hodon
chosen_rendering: the first priest ... the three who kept the way
alternate_renderings: the chief priest ... three keepers of the door
rationale: The LXX says first and second priest and describes three men keeping the way rather than naming a door.

chosen_rendering: the secretary of the forces
alternate_renderings: the principal scribe of the host
rationale: The official is kept as secretary of the forces who wrote for the people of the land.

chosen_rendering: Riblah
alternate_renderings: Deblatha
rationale: Riblah is used as the standard place form for the Greek Deblatha in the execution notice.

greek_phrase: tetardi kai eikadi ... elaben ten kephalen
chosen_rendering: twenty-fourth ... lifted up the head
alternate_renderings: twenty-fifth/twenty-seventh ... lifted up the head
rationale: The LXX date here is the twenty-fourth and the release idiom is kept as lifted up the head.

chosen_rendering: Evil-merodach
alternate_renderings: Evilmerodach
rationale: The Babylonian king's name is hyphenated in the standard English form while preserving the LXX release notice.

chosen_rendering: before his face
alternate_renderings: before him
rationale: The face-language is kept for Jehoiakim eating continually at the Babylonian king's table.

chosen_rendering: the ration for him was given
alternate_renderings: the allowance given him
rationale: The closing notice keeps the daily ration supplied by the king of Babylon until Jehoiakim's death.

chosen_rendering: How the city sat alone ... subject to tribute
alternate_renderings: How city sat alone ... became for tribute
rationale: The line supplies English articles while preserving the city, widow, and tribute clauses.

chosen_rendering: exiled because of her affliction ... in the midst of those afflicting her
alternate_renderings: exiled from her affliction ... between oppressors
rationale: The apo phrases are rendered causally in readable English, and the final phrase keeps the surrounding afflicters.

chosen_rendering: before the face of the afflicter
alternate_renderings: before afflicter
rationale: The face-language is retained for the captivity line while supplying the English article.

chosen_rendering: desirable things ... laughed at her deportation
alternate_renderings: desires ... laughed at her captivity
rationale: The verse keeps the memory, desirable-things, and deportation language in an English sentence.

chosen_rendering: she lowered her boastful words
alternate_renderings: he brought her down exceedingly
rationale: The active verb and hyperogka are rendered as her lowering boastful words, matching the LXX/Brenton sense without importing the MT wording.

chosen_rendering: nations entering her sanctuary ... not to enter into your assembly
alternate_renderings: nations entering her sanctuary ... not to enter your assembly
rationale: The verse keeps the sanctuary/assembly contrast and the infinitive entry wording.

chosen_rendering: restore life
alternate_renderings: restore soul
rationale: Psyche is rendered as life in the famine context where the people trade desired things for food.

greek_phrase: ου προς υμας ... φθεγξαμενος εν εμοι
chosen_rendering: Is it nothing to you ... The Lord, who spoke in me, humbled me
alternate_renderings: Not to you ... word spoken in me
rationale: The road appeal is made readable while keeping the pain comparison and the Lord's speaking/humbling action.

chosen_rendering: fire into my bones ... a net for my feet ... desolate
alternate_renderings: fire into my bones ... net for my feet ... ruined
rationale: The verse keeps the fire/net/desolation images while smoothing the result clause.

chosen_rendering: watched over my ungodlinesses ... gave pains into my hands
alternate_renderings: kept watch over my sins ... laid pains on my hands
rationale: The guarded wording keeps the LXX watch and pains language while clarifying the woven-in-my-hands clause.

greek_phrase: ο παρακαλων με ο επιστρεφων ψυχην μου
chosen_rendering: the comforter restoring my soul
alternate_renderings: comforter restoring my soul
rationale: The article is supplied for the comforter while keeping the soul-restoring phrase.

chosen_rendering: like one sitting apart
alternate_renderings: as a removed woman
rationale: The phrase is rendered as one sitting apart to preserve the separation image without over-specifying the metaphor.

chosen_rendering: I provoked his mouth
alternate_renderings: I embittered his mouth
rationale: The provocation idiom is kept with mouth-language rather than flattening the clause to disobedience.

chosen_rendering: Outside, a sword bereaved me; inside the house like death
alternate_renderings: Outside sword bereaved me, inside the house like death
rationale: The inside/outside contrast is clarified while preserving the smoke-guarded inside-the-house-like-death wording.

chosen_rendering: You brought a day; you called a time
alternate_renderings: You brought day. You called time.
rationale: The day/time line is kept as direct divine action in readable English.

chosen_rendering: glean them as they made a gleaning
alternate_renderings: strip them as they stripped me
rationale: The repeated gleaning root is retained to mirror the Greek judgment wording.

chosen_rendering: submerged all the beautiful things of Jacob
alternate_renderings: sank all beauties of Jacob
rationale: Katapontizo is rendered as submerged while keeping the beautiful-things phrase and the no-sparing clause.

chosen_rendering: every horn of Israel ... a flame of fire

greek_phrase: παντες οι βασιλεις αυτων επεσαν ουκ ην ο επικαλουμενος εν αυτοις προς με

alternate_renderings: all their kings fell; there was no one among them calling on me

greek_phrase: εφραιμ εν τοις λαοις αυτου συνανεμειγνυτο
chosen_rendering: Ephraim mingled itself among his peoples
alternate_renderings: Ephraim mixed itself among his peoples

chosen_rendering: Ephraim became a cake not turned
alternate_renderings: Ephraim became a hidden cake not turned

greek_phrase: κατεφαγον αλλοτριοι την ισχυν αυτου αυτος δε ουκ επεγνω
chosen_rendering: Foreigners devoured his strength but he did not know
alternate_renderings: Strangers devoured his strength but he did not know

greek_phrase: πολιαι εξηνθησαν αυτω και αυτος ουκ εγνω
chosen_rendering: gray hairs blossomed on him and he did not know
alternate_renderings: gray hairs came upon him and he did not know

greek_phrase: ταπεινωθησεται η υβρις ισραηλ εις προσωπον αυτου

alternate_renderings: the pride of Israel will be brought down before his face

greek_phrase: ουκ επεστρεψαν προς κυριον τον θεον αυτων ουκ εξεζητησαν αυτον εν πασι τουτοις
chosen_rendering: they did not return to the Lord their God and they did not seek him in all these things
alternate_renderings: they did not return to the Lord their God nor seek him in all this

greek_phrase: ην εφραιμ ως περιστερα ανους ουκ εχουσα καρδιαν
chosen_rendering: Ephraim was like a foolish dove having no heart
alternate_renderings: Ephraim was like a silly dove not having a heart
rationale: Retains no-heart wording for the LXX image.

greek_phrase: αιγυπτον επεκαλειτο και εις ασσυριους επορευθησαν
chosen_rendering: he called on Egypt and they went to Assyrians
alternate_renderings: they called on Egypt and went to Assyrians
rationale: Follows the Greek singular-to-plural pronoun shift.

greek_phrase: καθως αν πορευωνται επιβαλω επ' αυτους το δικτυον μου
chosen_rendering: As they go I will cast my net on them
alternate_renderings: Whenever they go I will cast my net upon them

greek_phrase: καθως τα πετεινα του ουρανου καταξω αυτους
chosen_rendering: like birds of heaven I will bring them down
alternate_renderings: like birds of the sky I will bring them down
rationale: Retains birds of heaven and bring-down wording.

greek_phrase: παιδευσω αυτους εν τη ακοη της θλιψεως αυτων
chosen_rendering: I will discipline them with the report of their affliction
alternate_renderings: I will discipline them by hearing of their affliction
rationale: Uses report for akoē in context while keeping affliction.

greek_phrase: ουαι αυτοις οτι απεπηδησαν απ' εμου
chosen_rendering: Woe to them because they leaped away from me
alternate_renderings: Woe to them because they started aside from me
rationale: Retains the leaping-away image.

greek_phrase: δειλαιοι εισιν οτι ησεβησαν εις εμε
chosen_rendering: They are cowardly because they acted impiously toward me
alternate_renderings: They are wretched because they sinned against me
rationale: Retains cowardly and acted-impiously wording.

greek_phrase: εγω δε ελυτρωσαμην αυτους αυτοι δε κατελαλησαν κατ' εμου ψευδη
chosen_rendering: But I redeemed them and they spoke lies against me
alternate_renderings: Yet I redeemed them but they spoke falsehoods against me
rationale: Retains redeemed and spoke-lies-against-me contrast.

greek_phrase: ουκ εβοησαν προς με αι καρδιαι αυτων αλλ' η ωλολυζον εν ταις κοιταις αυτων
chosen_rendering: their hearts did not cry to me but they howled on their beds
alternate_renderings: their hearts did not cry to me but they howled on their beds
rationale: Retains heart-cry contrast with bed-howling.

chosen_rendering: for grain and wine they cut themselves
alternate_renderings: for grain and wine they gashed themselves
rationale: Retains cut-themselves for katatemnō.

chosen_rendering: they were disciplined by me
alternate_renderings: they were trained in me

chosen_rendering: I strengthened their arms
alternate_renderings: I strengthened their arms
rationale: Retains strengthened-arms wording.

chosen_rendering: toward me they reckoned evil things
alternate_renderings: against me they devised evil things
rationale: Retains reckoned evil things with the toward-me phrase.

greek_phrase: απεστραφησαν εις ουθεν εγενοντο ως τοξον εντεταμενον
chosen_rendering: They turned aside to nothing; they became like a bent bow
alternate_renderings: They turned aside to what is nothing; they became like a bent bow
rationale: Retains the nothing and bent-bow images.

greek_phrase: πεσουνται εν ρομφαια οι αρχοντες αυτων δι' απαιδευσιαν γλωσσης αυτων
chosen_rendering: Their rulers will fall by sword because of their undisciplined tongue
alternate_renderings: Their princes will fall by the sword because of the untrained state of their tongue

greek_phrase: ουτος ο φαυλισμος αυτων εν γη αιγυπτω
chosen_rendering: This is their scorn in the land of Egypt
alternate_renderings: This is their setting-at-nought in the land of Egypt
rationale: Retains scorn for phaulismos in Egypt.

greek_phrase: εις κολπον αυτων ως γη ως αετος επ' οικον κυριου
chosen_rendering: Into their bosom like land like an eagle against the house of the Lord
alternate_renderings: He shall come into their midst as land as an eagle against the house of the Lord
rationale: Preserves the verbless LXX pileup and eagle-against-house image.

greek_phrase: παρεβησαν την διαθηκην μου και κατα του νομου μου ησεβησαν
chosen_rendering: they transgressed my covenant and acted impiously against my law
alternate_renderings: they transgressed my covenant and sinned against my law
rationale: Keeps covenant transgression and impiety against law distinct.

greek_phrase: εμε κεκραξονται ο θεος εγνωκαμεν σε
chosen_rendering: They will cry to me O God we have known you
alternate_renderings: They will cry to me O God we knew you
rationale: Renders the perfect form as have known.

chosen_rendering: Israel turned away from good things; they pursued an enemy
alternate_renderings: Israel turned away from good things; enemies pursued him
rationale: Reads echthron as object of the active pursued verb.

greek_phrase: εαυτοις εβασιλευσαν και ου δι' εμου
chosen_rendering: They reigned for themselves and not through me
alternate_renderings: They made kings for themselves but not through me
rationale: Follows the LXX finite verb rather than supplying made kings.

chosen_rendering: They ruled and they did not make it known to me
alternate_renderings: They ruled and did not declare it to me
rationale: Retains ruled and made-known-to-me wording.

greek_phrase: το αργυριον αυτων και το χρυσιον αυτων εποιησαν εαυτοις ειδωλα
chosen_rendering: Their silver and their gold they made into idols for themselves
alternate_renderings: Their silver and gold they made images for themselves
rationale: Retains the possessive repetition and idols.

chosen_rendering: so that they might be destroyed
alternate_renderings: so that they might be utterly destroyed
rationale: Keeps the purpose/result clause explicit.

chosen_rendering: Cast off your calf Samaria
alternate_renderings: Cast away your calf Samaria
rationale: Uses cast off for apotripsai and keeps direct address to Samaria.

greek_phrase: παρωξυνθη ο θυμος μου επ' αυτους
chosen_rendering: My anger was provoked against them
alternate_renderings: My wrath was kindled against them
rationale: Retains provoked for paroxynthē and against them.

greek_phrase: εως τινος ου μη δυνωνται καθαρισθηναι
chosen_rendering: How long will they be unable to be cleansed
alternate_renderings: How long will they be unable to purge themselves
rationale: Keeps the inability and passive cleansing question.

greek_phrase: εν τω ισραηλ και αυτο τεκτων εποιησεν και ου θεος εστιν
chosen_rendering: For in Israel a craftsman made it and it is not God
alternate_renderings: For in Israel a workman made it and it is not God

greek_phrase: διοτι πλανων ην ο μοσχος σου σαμαρεια
chosen_rendering: your calf Samaria was leading astray
alternate_renderings: your calf Samaria was a deceiver
rationale: Renders the participle as leading astray.

greek_phrase: ανεμοφθορα εσπειραν και η καταστροφη αυτων εκδεξεται αυτα
chosen_rendering: they sowed wind-blight and their destruction will receive them
alternate_renderings: they sowed blighted seed and their destruction will await them
rationale: Retains wind-blight and adds their to destruction.

greek_phrase: δραγμα ουκ εχον ισχυν του ποιησαι αλευρον
chosen_rendering: A handful has no strength to make flour
alternate_renderings: a sheaf has no strength to make flour
rationale: Keeps handful and the lack of strength for flour.

greek_phrase: εαν δε και ποιηση αλλοτριοι καταφαγονται αυτο
chosen_rendering: if it does make it foreigners will devour it
alternate_renderings: even if it produces it strangers will devour it
rationale: Retains foreigners and devouring of the produced flour.

greek_phrase: κατεποθη ισραηλ νυν εγενετο εν τοις εθνεσιν ως σκευος αχρηστον
chosen_rendering: Israel was swallowed up now it became among the nations like a useless vessel
alternate_renderings: Israel was swallowed up now he became among nations like a worthless vessel
rationale: Keeps swallowed-up Israel and useless-vessel image.

chosen_rendering: they went up to Assyrians
alternate_renderings: they went up to the Assyrians
